\section{BW20: Tag-free balance-wire geometry and sharp native synchronization bound}\label{sec:bw20}
We address Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} by combining I21's physical adapter, GD26's factored pivot, BW18's relative gates and M26's matching switches. The construction removes artificial syndrome coordinates, but the lower bound below excludes universal removal of genuine equality synchronization by pure balance gadgets.

\begin{lemma}[Simple tag-free signed wire replacement]\label{lem:bw20-wire}
A signed wire in an explicit native E4/B4 port network can be replaced by a private copy of $K_5-pq$ with all five internal vertices B4, zero internal signs, and the two exterior wires of signs $s,0$. It preserves the exact exterior relation of the original wire, with polynomial construction and lift, and contributes no E4 tags. It need not preserve multiplicities.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Write the two open stub bits as $a,b$. Summing the five balance equations gives $10=2\sum_e x_e+a+b$, where the sum is over internal edges. Thus $a=b$. For $a=b=0$ choose any Hamiltonian cycle avoiding $pq$, for instance $p,u,q,v,w,p$ with the other vertices $u,v,w$. For $a=b=1$ take the bitwise complement of all internal and stub values. Every vertex then has exactly two ones in either case. The exterior signs enforce the original wire. Distinct gadgets have disjoint vertices and give a simple loopless four-regular closed graph. Unlike the E4 wire replacement in I21 this lift is not unique; only decision and projected source support are asserted.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Sharp synchronization resource and matching path bound]\label{lem:bw20-sync}
Consider any finite open signed E4/B4 gadget with $k$ E4 vertices and distinct actual boundary stubs. Retain optionally a system of $r$ affine guard equations on its actual port bits. If two guard-feasible boundary words differ in $d$ positions, then $d$ is even and the boundary relation contains at least $2^{\max(0,d/2-k-r)}$ distinct words. In particular, an exact all-equal relation on $d\ge4$ even boundary bits requires $k+r\ge d/2-1$. Without additional guards the bound on $k$ is attained.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Use I21's matching adapter, with four port nodes and two private dummies for each B4, two disjoint internal port-pair edges with the same unique binary tag for each E4, a direct edge for each positive wire and a subdivided edge for each negative wire. At each boundary port introduce a distinct leaf that is present precisely when the boundary bit is one. A matching of the resulting graph satisfying all tag XORs equal to zero is equivalent to a native port word, since external occupancy determines each port bit. Each extra affine equation on the port bits is a linear sum of external matching edge indicators, so it adds at most one tag coordinate. Constant terms enter the target. This construction applies also to the empty guard; no nonaffine external constraint is dropped.

Lift the two boundary words to matchings, interpreted on the common ambient graph with absent leaves unmatched. Their symmetric difference has alternating cycles and paths, with endpoints precisely the $d$ changed leaves; hence there are $d/2$ disjoint alternating paths and $d$ is even. Switching any subset of these paths preserves matching feasibility on the corresponding leaf set. Let the columns of a binary matrix be the $k+r$ tag differences of these paths. Its kernel has dimension at least $\max(0,d/2-k-r)$. Each kernel switch preserves the target and gives a distinct boundary word, proving the bound (the actual rank of the path matrix gives a sharper version). For the two-word equality relation the kernel dimension cannot exceed one. A chain of $k$ E4 vertices has $4k-2(k-1)=2k+2$ exposed stubs, and enforces precisely all-equal without extra tags. Signed boundary phase changes do not alter the Hamming distance argument. No pure B4 enlargement can implement this equality relation on four or more stubs, even with unlimited size. This is a physical gadget resource bound, not a time or proof-size lower bound; it does not exclude external nonaffine consumers, alternate decoders, or a polynomial algorithm for the genuine joint tags.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Native factored pivot transport]\label{lem:bw20-gate}
The explicit GD26 factored pivot gate and unaffected wide NAE owners compile to strict simple signed E4/B4 geometry with graph-object count linear in their current literal and gate volume, with exact projected acceptance and polynomial witness lift. The compiler may use Lemma~\ref{lem:bw20-wire} to avoid all artificial wire tags.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For actual reference literal $h$, BW18's three signed NAE triples implement $z\oplus h=(a\oplus h)(b\oplus h)$. Negating inputs and output implements relative OR. Build both GD26 flags in this relative gauge by binary gates and their rejecting conjunction; the two flag meanings swap when $h$ changes, leaving the reject bit invariant. Require the output equal to $h$ by $\operatorname{NAE}(z,\neg h,\neg h)$. Each gate output is unique given its inputs. For an unaffected wide NAE owner choose its first literal as its own reference, OR the remaining relative literals and require the result unequal to that reference by $\operatorname{NAE}(z,h,h)$. This expresses the presence of an opposite bit without adding a global reference hub. Handle empty or singleton rejection explicitly; a single tail literal needs no binary gate. The two GD26 flag types give the exact original pivot lift. Apply I21's duplicated triples and signed occurrence paths, but replace physical wires using Lemma~\ref{lem:bw20-wire}. Each original triple's fourth bit is forced by integer balance. Every native witness decodes to gate values and actual exterior coordinates and yields an original pivot witness; conversely every accepted exterior word extends through the gates and native gadget choices. Preserve actual guards in the source map, not as unconditional pin claims. Rank-one duplicate-position NAE deductions, parity and equality closure are paid before and after accepted deductions and at stagnation. Absolute guards, if present, remain separate or explicitly compiled; the executed chart is unguarded. Linear construction in current volume does not bound repeated projection or arbitrary joint gate acquisition in original input length.
\end{proof}

\subsection{GD27: signed quadratic dual contraction and the common-polar obstruction}
\label{sec:gd27}
\paragraph{Scope and status.}
PROVED as restricted exact lemmas, independent review pending; U-PROGRESS, universal SEM/CLOSE and unconditional COST remain OPEN. We strengthen GD26's factored projection by an algebraic consumer and explicitly test a candidate universal decomposition. No full closure or public proof follows.

\paragraph{Map-free parity escape.}
In GD26's cubic Tseitin-to-signed-NAE3 construction, every private pivot has exactly two occurrences; each edge variable has eight and the reference has four per graph vertex. Exact degree-two pivot elimination therefore discovers the private bits by scanning actual occurrences, without a supplied vertex-group decomposition. The elimination preserves the other variables' occurrence counts until grouping. Group the resulting four-literal owners by their actual coordinate scopes. In a simple cubic graph each vertex contributes a distinct scope with four owners; their 16 boundary words give exactly
\[
x_a+x_b+x_c+r=b_v
\]
over $\mathbb F_2$. Gaussian elimination detects the odd-charge contradiction or supplies an even-charge assignment. Reverse each private pivot using GD26's exact flags and verify the source. The number of owners and variables decreases, all scans, bounded tables, grouping, affine elimination, reconstruction and source verification cost polynomial in original $N$. General inputs may decline; nonaffine groups are retained. This removes the earlier supplied-group assumption on that family, not arbitrary normalization.

\paragraph{Quadratic dual identity.}
In the Boolean ring over $\mathbb F_2$ the violation of a signed NAE3 owner is
\[
q(a,b,c)=1+a+b+c+ab+ac+bc
\]
for its literal bits. It is zero exactly on satisfying triples. General bounded-fan-in Boolean consumers can be compiled to quadratic equations using uniquely defined gate wires, whose entire acquisition and encoded size must be charged. Necessary affine equations are solved and substituted; row reduction of polynomial coefficients exposes further affine consequences. Reclose after each accepted consequence. Each independent affine consequence decreases free dimension; contradiction $1=0$ is terminal. Retain guards and exact source identities. If $q_1,\ldots,q_r$ are a coefficient basis in $d$ free bits, character orthogonality gives
\[
Z=2^{-r}\sum_{\lambda\in\mathbb F_2^r}G\!\left(\sum_i\lambda_iq_i\right),
\qquad
G(Q)=\sum_{x\in\mathbb F_2^d}(-1)^{Q(x)}.
\]
For $Q=uv+uA(z)+vB(z)+C(z)$, summing over the pair gives $2(-1)^{A(z)B(z)+C(z)}$. Here $A,B$ are affine; the residual remains quadratic. Repeating, the final affine form sums to zero if nonconstant and otherwise to a signed power of two. Thus every term is polynomially computable; the signed numerator has $O(d+r+1)$ bits. Enumerating terms gives $2^r\operatorname{poly}(N)$ time and polynomial peak space. A fixed original-$N$ cap $r\le c\log_2(N+2)$ is a polynomial terminal. Source self-reduction by pins cannot increase coefficient-span dimension under substitution, and each pin is followed by certified closure. \paragraph{Dual-observation tree consumer.}
Suppose a paid primal affine parametrization gives disjoint coordinate blocks with
$q_i=c_i+\sum_jq_{ij}(x_j)$, where $q_{ij}$ have no cross-block monomials or constants. Let $W_j\subseteq(\mathbb F_2^r)^*$ be the span of coefficient-observation vectors for block $j$, including its linear coefficients. Include a constant-sign factor for $\lambda\cdot c$, of rank at most one. For each functional on $W_j$ compute the local Gauss factor by the preceding pair elimination. Then
\[
2^r Z=\sum_\lambda(-1)^{\lambda\cdot c}
\prod_j G_j(\lambda|_{W_j}).
\]
For a binary tree over factors let $W_v$ be the sum of the observation spans in a subtree, $E_v$ the sum outside, and $B_v=W_v\cap E_v$. A table indexed by functionals on $B_v$ sums the products over all extensions to $W_v$. At an internal node with children $a,b$, combine child boundary functionals only when they agree on $W_a\cap W_b$ and induce the desired parent functional on $B_v$. Indeed the intersection is contained in both child boundaries and $B_v\subseteq B_a+B_b$: for $w\in B_v$ write $w=u+v$, $u\in W_a,v\in W_b$; then $u=w+v\in E_a$ and $v=w+u\in E_b$. Every consistent pair of full child functionals has a unique extension to their sum, so induction proves the signed table identity without overcount. At the root multiply by $2^{r-\dim W_{\rm root}}$ for unused dual directions, then divide by $2^r$. Bases, intersections and restriction maps are computable by Gaussian elimination. Leaf acquisition costs $2^{\dim W_j}\operatorname{poly}(N)$; every internal combination uses at most $2^{\dim B_a+\dim B_b}$ pairs. Signed integer magnitudes are bounded by $2^{d+r}$ in this construction. Thus uniformly discovered polynomial-description decompositions with fixed original-$N$ logarithmic bounds on every leaf and boundary rank give polynomial exact counting. Witness recovery needs no new decomposition: pin a bit in the discovered primal coordinates, replace that block's factor by its restricted local Gauss sum, and reuse the same observation space and tree. Pins only restrict summation and preserve dependence on the original $W_j$; retain any newly forced coordinates within this fixed representation. A positive count permits successive verified pins, then the paid original-source lift. This establishes a restricted polynomial terminal including discovery when the decomposition is actually supplied or uniformly acquired and charged. It does not prove universal acquisition or a logarithmic rank bound.

For the connected quadratic chain $p_i=x_i y_i$, $p_i+p_{i+1}=0$, the local factor is $4$ when adjacent dual bits agree and $2$ otherwise; exterior dual bits are zero. Two-state contraction yields $Z=3^k+1$ with $4k-2$ transition updates, despite equation rank $k-1$. Optional endpoint constraints give consistent or contradictory guarded controls. This is a quadratic-source control, not a claimed native tetrahedral adapter.

\paragraph{Common-polar obstruction, invariant under basis.}
Let a raw signed NAE3 chart have distinct actual variables in each triple and a 2-vertex-connected primal graph. Each owner polar form has rank two and row plane spanned by $e_a+e_b,e_a+e_c$ in the actual dual space; signs do not change it. Under any common direct-sum block diagonalization of all owner polar forms, even rank additivity places each rank-two plane in one block dual. Every primal edge difference is in an owner plane. Two adjacent edges at vertex $v$ lie on a simple cycle, since the graph remains connected after deleting $v$. Summing edge differences along the cycle gives zero. Directness of block duals forbids splitting the cycle across blocks, since a nonempty proper edge subset of a simple cycle cannot have zero incidence vector. Thus adjacent edges, and hence all edges, belong to one block. A spanning tree gives $n-1$ independent differences, so a block has dimension at least $n-1$. Fixing one actual reference preserves this dimension since restriction is injective on the even-weight difference span. This rules out universal small common polar blocks on raw sources, even after an invertible affine basis change; it does not exclude term-specific decompositions, new variables, arbitrary normalization or polynomial decision. The GD26 gadget family evades the obstruction by the map-free nonlocal group elimination above.

\paragraph{Closure is not free.}
Given a 3-CNF $F$, introduce a common reference $r$ and switch $s$. Replace every clause by $\operatorname{NAE}(r,\neg s,a,b,c)$ and split it into three ternary owners by fresh private pivots, using exact NAE splitting. When $r=0$ this enforces $(\neg s\lor a\lor b\lor c)$; global complementation preserves the signed source. There is always a known witness with $s=r=0$ and private lifts. A witness with $s\ne r$ exists iff $F$ is satisfiable. Therefore determining whether the relative parity $s=r$ is universally forced is coNP-complete even with a supplied satisfying witness. This is not a P versus NP lower bound; it prevents silently assuming polynomial complete semantic affine closure. Also every raw NAE3 owner is equivalent to $\operatorname{NAE}(a,b,c,e)\land\operatorname{NAE}(a,b,c,\neg e)$, realizable by degree-two pivots in ternary gadgets. Small gates alone do not establish polynomial consumption.

\subsection{BD20: shared-syndrome planar Pfaffian consumer and raw rank obstruction}\label{sec:bd20}
\paragraph{Status.} PROVED scoped, independent review pending. This is a direct attempt at GD27's signed-mode coverage target in Obligation~\ref{obl:progress}, combining exact matching and algebraic cancellation. Universal SEM/CLOSE and unconditional COST remain OPEN.
\begin{lemma}[Shared observation rank controls signed planar consumption]\label{lem:bd20-planar}
Consider a signed NAE3 chart on $n$ actual bits, with $m$ ternary owners and additional authenticated Boolean predicates $H$. Construct a pair-interaction registry by assigning each literal pair in each ternary owner weight $L=2^{n+1}$ when the signed literal bits differ, and $1$ otherwise. Merge parallel pair factors by multiplication. Suppose a uniformly acquired planar core of the pair graph leaves a correction $C(Rx)$ incorporating every omitted pair factor and $H$, with $R$ independent binary observation rows and a polynomial-description circuit for $C$. The factorization is supplied by actual observation maps, not semantic identity testing. If $r=\operatorname{rank}R$, then exact guarded decision and witness reconstruction cost $2^r\operatorname{poly}(N)$ bit work and space, including polynomially charged acquisition of the supplied core and maps, and are polynomial for $r\le c\log_2(N+2)$ with fixed $c$ and fixed original-$N$ description bounds.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Every satisfied ternary owner contributes exactly two differing pairs, and every violated owner none. Thus for the full weighted sum $Z$ over all assignments satisfying $H$, the base-$L$ digit at position $2m$ is exactly the satisfying count; no carries occur since each coefficient is at most $2^n$. For projected systems this is the count of projected assignments, not necessarily original source lifts. Evaluate the correction on all $2^r$ actual observation words, then acquire the unnormalized integer Walsh coefficients $\widehat C(\lambda)$. Exact Fourier inversion gives
\[
2^r Z=\sum_{\lambda\in\mathbb F_2^r}\widehat C(\lambda)
\sum_x(-1)^{\lambda Rx}\prod_{e\in P}w_e(x_u+x_v).
\]
This coalesces all omitted-factor modes by their actual syndrome; no independent guard minimization. For a fixed mode write $T$ for the support of $\lambda R$, $A_e=w_e(0)+w_e(1)$, $B_e=w_e(0)-w_e(1)$. Its inner sum is
\[
2^{n-|E(P)|}\sum_{S:\partial S=T}\prod_{e\notin S}A_e\prod_{e\in S}B_e.
\]
This follows by expanding each pair factor into its constant and parity character, then summing over actual bits. A zero $B_e$ forces $e$ absent; multiply $A_e$ and remove that edge. The positive original pair weights ensure $A_e\ne0$. Odd boundary cardinality in any remaining component makes the sum zero. Otherwise pair the marked vertices within each component and XOR connecting paths to acquire a $T$-join $J$. Substitution $S=J\mathbin{\triangle}S'$ swaps $A_e,B_e$ on $J$ and reduces exactly to the weighted even-subgraph sum on the planar graph, with signed nonzero weights.

For clarity a linear-volume Fisher-type gadget suffices: split a degree-$d>3$ vertex into a planar tree of $d-2$ ternary parity nodes in cyclic port order, with auxiliary edges of both weights $1$. For even external parity the internal edge bits are uniquely determined by the tree. Replace each resulting degree-one, two or three vertex by a clique on its incident ports. External matching edges represent absent subgraph edges, so the locally remaining ports are even in number and have a unique internal matching (zero or two ports). This is a weight-preserving bijection after assigning external edge weight $A_e/B_e$, internal edge weight $1$, and multiplying by $\prod_e B_e$. A planar Kasteleyn orientation, acquired by a dual-face spanning tree, has constant Pfaffian permutation/orientation sign on perfect matchings regardless of their signed numerical weights. Calibrate that sign with the explicit all-external perfect matching; taking the absolute Pfaffian would in general be incorrect. Exact rational or fraction-free Pfaffian elimination gives polynomial bit work per mode, with minor bounds controlling numerator and denominator sizes. See \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.7289}{Gobron, planar Ising Pfaffians} and \href{https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/wbln.3.pdf}{Kenyon, weighted planar dimer orientation}. All coefficients and matrix dimensions are polynomial-bit in original $N$ under the stated representation bounds. The $2^r$ modes and Walsh array are fully charged.

To reconstruct a satisfying assignment without increasing the correction rank, select a nonloop planar-core edge and test both parities by substituting $x_v=x_u+b$ and contracting that edge. Retain its weight as a constant, merge parallel factors with adjusted signs, and retain loop weights exactly. Planarity survives contraction. The correction's observation rows restrict by the same affine map, with constants retained, hence their rank never increases. When no planar edges remain, fix isolated coordinates directly. Each accepted choice reduces free dimension by one, so at most $2n$ restricted counts are needed. Do not pin a vertex with incident planar edges and pretend the resulting unary field is a zero-field planar model. Certified unconditional closure is applied initially, after every accepted deduction and at stagnation. A proved redundant equation on the satisfying set can remain an annotation with its actual guard and derivation rather than enter the weighted sum of nonsolutions: the top digit is unchanged by this choice. All nonredundant input guards enter the correction. Charge all closure, failed choices, rank updates, contractions, exact counts, reconstruction and source verification. Serial time and space are $2^r\operatorname{poly}(N)$, with $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$. Greedy edge insertion with a planarity test and Gaussian rank checking is one paid discovery policy; optimization of the core is not assumed.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Universal raw logarithmic correction rank is false]\label{lem:bd20-rank}
For a linear 4-regular 3-uniform raw NAE registry on $n$ vertices, every planar pair core omits observation rows of rank at least $(n+6)/8$. This holds regardless of signs and, for a fixed selection of omitted forms, is invariant under invertible linear basis changes.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The pair graph is simple, 8-regular, and has $4n$ edges. Every planar simple subgraph has at most $3n-6$ edges. The omitted graph $D$ therefore has at least $n+6$ edges. Its binary incidence rows have rank $r_D=\sum_K(|V(K)|-1)$ over nontrivial components. It has at most $2r_D$ nonisolated vertices, and maximum degree at most eight, hence at most $8r_D$ edges. Any correction span contains these rows. Infinite connected SAT controls exist: for odd $q\ge7$ take three parts $x_i,y_i,z_i$ over $\mathbb Z_q$ and triples $(x_i,y_{i+p},z_{i+2p})$ for $p=0,1,2,3$. Differences distinguish all pair occurrences, each vertex has degree four, and shifts connect the incidence graph. One part colored one and the others zero satisfies every triple. Thus this is a raw representation obstruction, even on easy inputs, not an unrestricted lower bound or simultaneous hard sequence. Nonlocal normalization may change the graph and escape.
\end{proof}

\section{Dual-mode support is a joint decision problem (DR20)}\label{sec:dr20}
The GD27 signed quadratic dual consumer is exact; its polynomial use still requires a paid bound on joint modes, not just local Gauss evaluation.
\begin{lemma}[Hard affine slice of a factored quadratic dual]\label{lem:dr20-slice}
For arbitrary 3-CNF $F$ on occurring variables $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n$, there is a uniformly constructible quadratic primal coefficient family $q_0,\ldots,q_n$ with supplied disjoint nine-bit primal blocks, each depending on at most four dual coordinates, for which
\[
G\left(sq_0+\sum_i\lambda_i q_i\right)\ge0,\qquad
G\left(q_0+\sum_i\lambda_i q_i\right)=2^{5m}[F(\lambda)].
\]
Thus existence of a nonzero mode in the affine slice $s=1$ is NP-complete, and its normalized exact sum is \#P-complete. This holds even when the primal zero system is trivially satisfiable with full affine hull.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For each clause of width $k=3$, let $f_j(\lambda,s)$ be its literal falsity bit homogenized by replacing the constant one by $s$. Use private primal bits $v_0,\ldots,v_k,u_0,\ldots,u_{k+1}$ and quadratic exponent
\[
Q_C=u_0s(v_0+1)+\sum_{j=1}^k u_j(sv_j+f_j(\lambda,s)v_{j-1})+u_{k+1}sv_k.
\]
The total exponent is linear in $(s,\lambda)$ and quadratic in primal bits. Summing each $u$ gives zero unless its coefficient vanishes, and otherwise gives two. At $s=1$ the conditions are $v_0=1,v_j=f_jv_{j-1},v_k=0$; the unique triangular solution exists precisely when the clause holds. Thus the block contributes zero or $2^{k+2}$. At $s=0$ all conditions on $v$ are homogeneous, hence each contribution is positive. The product over blocks gives the stated identity. Every occurring $\lambda_i$ has a monomial $u_jv_{j-1}$ unique to that occurrence; $s$ has the private monomial $u_0v_0$. The coefficient family is independent and its span contains no nonzero affine polynomial. The primal zero system has all $v$ words when $u=0$. For an isolated nonzero $u_0$, choose $v_0=1$; for an isolated $u_j$ with $1\le j\le k$, choose $v_j=v_{j-1}=0$; for an isolated $u_{k+1}$ choose $v_k=0$. These words solve all coefficient equations; their differences from $u=0$ solutions span every $u$ direction. Thus the full primal affine hull is the cube. Construction and local evaluation are polynomial; a nonzero mode is a polynomially checkable witness. The reduction is parsimonious after dividing the slice sum by the known power of two.
\end{proof}
For variable width $k$, the block uses $2k+3$ primal bits and amplitude $2^{k+2}$. The affine slice is a constraint on dual indices, not a primal guard. No reduction to decision of the unshifted primal system is claimed: it is always SAT. Even nonnegative Gauss factors, constant local volumes, an explicit common primal decomposition, and full primal affine hull do not make arbitrary joint dual support acquisition a free operation. Orthogonality gives $Z_0-Z_1=2^{A-n}\#F$ for primal systems with $q_0=0$ and $q_0=1$ respectively, other coefficients zero, where $A=\sum_C(k+2)$; this is a counting difference, not a SAT decision equivalence. An exact alternative on this slice is to consume its recovered actual clause supports directly, or apply GD27's tree contraction only under its verified overlap caps. Neither supplies universal progress. All local Gaussian work, mode acquisition, coefficient bits, actual intersection maps, guard versions, failed attempts and reconstruction must be paid. This is a restricted composition/circularity barrier, not an unrestricted lower bound, and cannot imply a simultaneous hard sequence against a portfolio that may avoid the slice entirely.

\section{Native signed cycle-space contraction and the polar-deficiency bridge (I26)}\label{sec:i26}
We attack Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} on the actual BS19/M26/GD27/DR20 chain. A successful polynomial support acquisition does not imply a polynomial signed zero test. In this section the native guard is empty; additional nonredundant guards must enter the actual factor registry.
\begin{lemma}[Exact native cycle-space count]\label{lem:i26-cycle}
Let $H$ be the bipartite incidence graph of a canonical signed NAE registry with distinct variables per owner and arities $k_j\ge2$, $n$ variables, $m$ owners, edge set $E$, $c$ components including isolates, and actual literal signs $b\in\mathbb F_2^E$. Write $C=\ker B$ for the binary cycle space of its incidence matrix $B$. For the owner legal indicator $f_j$ the unnormalized Walsh transform is
\[
\widehat f_j(a)=2^{k_j}[a=0]-(-1)^{a\cdot b_j}(1+(-1)^{|a|}).
\]
The exact native solution count is
\[
Z=2^{n-|E|}\sum_{s\in C}\prod_j\widehat f_j(s|_j),\qquad
\dim C=|E|-n-m+c.
\]
Every summand on $C$ is nonzero. Nonzero-sum decision on these signed ternary incidence inputs is NP-complete (zero testing is coNP-complete), although all supported modes form an explicitly discoverable binary linear space.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Subtract the two complementary forbidden words from the full local cube. This gives the displayed local transform, supported on every even mode and no odd mode. Fourier inversion on all owners and summation over each actual variable forces parity zero at the variable vertex; owner parity zero is forced by the transform. These are precisely the incidence cycle equations. Gaussian elimination or the graph incidence rank formula gives the dimension. Since $k_j\ge2$, the zero mode is strictly positive and every other even mode has magnitude two. The exact count identity gives a uniform reduction from signed NAE3 decision (cf.\ I21); membership in NP uses an actual native satisfying assignment, not a single nonzero Fourier mode. This is a restricted signed weight-enumerator decision equivalence, not an unrestricted runtime lower bound.
\end{proof}
In particular the M26/GD26 private OR-chain gates may be collapsed analytically to the original wide NAE owners, preserving actual occurrence maps; there is no need to enumerate internal selector rows. For a ternary owner the even mode chooses zero or one pair of its three incidences, and all variable syndromes must still match. DR20's dual slice has hard support and an easy primal system; here the entire dual support is Gaussian, but cancellation is exactly the native decision problem. Neither support discovery nor taking absolute values suffices.

\begin{lemma}[Ternary polar and rank-Hall bridge]\label{lem:i26-polar}
For width three only, let $q(s)=|s|/2\bmod2$ on $C$, let $r$ be the rank of the ambient dot product restricted to $C$, and let $P$ be the binary zero-diagonal symmetric matrix of pair-cooccurrence parity on actual variables. Put $\delta_{\rm full}=m-n+c$. Then
\[
Z=2^{n-2m}\sum_{s\in C}3^{m-|s|/2}(-1)^{q(s)+b\cdot s},\qquad
r=2\delta_{\rm full}+\operatorname{rank}P,\qquad
r\ge2\delta_{\max},
\]
where $\delta_{\max}$ is DS15's maximum rank deficiency over owner subsets. If $r=0$, DS15 constructs a satisfying assignment for every signing in deterministic polynomial time.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For ternary owners every nonzero even mode selects two edges, so the number of active owners is $|s|/2$. The polar form of $q$ is $q(s+t)+q(s)+q(t)=s\cdot t$. The radical is $C\cap C^\perp$ and has dimension $\operatorname{rank}B-\operatorname{rank}(BB^T)$: map $\ker(BB^T)$ through $B^T$. The owner diagonal block of $BB^T$ is $I_m$, the off-diagonal block is the variable-owner incidence $A$, and the variable diagonal is degree parity. Eliminate $I_m$; the Schur complement is $\operatorname{diag}(\deg)+AA^T=P$. Subtract the radical dimension from $\dim C=2m-n+c$. For an owner subset $J$, its cycle space $C_J$ embeds in $C$ and lies in the direct sum of $|J|$ nondegenerate two-dimensional even ternary spaces. Its dimension is $|J|+\delta_J$, since the joint rank of actual relative rows is the number of used variables minus their components. Its radical has dimension at most $2|J|-\dim C_J$. Its polar rank is therefore at least $2\delta_J$ and at most $r$. Maximize over $J$. If $r=0$, all the Rado conditions hold. Lemma~\ref{lem:ds15-core} finds an independent relative row per owner by paid partition/linear matroid intersection. Impose the opposite of each owner's forbidden right-hand side and solve by Gaussian elimination. The resulting actual word satisfies every owner and has a polynomial source lift.
\end{proof}
There is also direct strict positivity when $r=0$: $q$ is linear on $C$, so the sign is some character indexed by $l$. With $\rho=1/\sqrt3$, its weighted sum $\sum_{s\in C}(-1)^{l\cdot s}\rho^{|s|}$ equals $|C|\Pr(Y+l\in C^\perp)>0$ for independent Bernoulli bits with mean $(1-\rho)/2$. This identity follows by character orthogonality and full support. The witness-producing route is the already-proved DS15 terminal, not a second stronger terminal. When $r>0$, a character or invertible basis change cannot linearize the quadratic sign; this does not exclude other exact contractions. In particular the unweighted Gauss sum does not account for the occupancy-dependent magnitude $3^{m-|s|/2}$. No universal cap on $r$ or on deficiency follows.

\begin{lemma}[Gate-character grouping and its raw rank obstruction]\label{lem:i26-gates}
In the M26 circuit representation, the unnormalized Walsh factor for an unsigned AND or OR graph on input modes $a,b$ and output mode $t$ is $4[a=b=0]$ at $t=0$, and respectively $2(-1)^{ab}$ or $2(-1)^{1+a+b+ab}$ at $t=1$. Signed inputs add linear phases. Given fixed attainable nonlinear output modes, the remaining exact contraction is an affine-constrained quadratic Gauss sum. Enumerating the image of output modes on the wire-conservation space costs $2^{r_{\rm act}}\operatorname{poly}(N)$ including all signs. However if every gate has a distinct output wire and at least one non-output consumer occurrence, then the raw activation rank $r_{\rm act}$ equals the number of gates. On connected easy SAT monotone OR cycles, exponentially many of these activation groups are nonzero.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Sum the four actual gate rows with their character weights. For each fixed output activation vector, inactive input modes must be zero; on active inputs the phase is quadratic. Add exact wire-conservation equations and pin phases, solve the affine system, and use symplectic elimination on the restricted quadratic form. Each symplectic pair contributes $2(-1)^{Q(e)Q(f)}$ for the normalized form $Q$, and an orthogonal radical bit contributes two or zero. The output image rank is obtained by stacking its projection rows on the conservation matrix and subtracting the original rank. Group by group this is exactly GD27's primal quadratic sum: invert the input characters, leaving the expansion of each gate indicator $2^{-1}\sum_t(-1)^{t(z+f(x,y))}$. It is not an independent progress guarantee. For each distinct output wire, choose a non-output consumer occurrence to balance its output mode; choices on different wires are independent. This proves full raw activation rank. For even $n$, impose $(x_i\lor x_{i+1})=1$ around a cycle. Activate any subset of a fixed perfect matching of its edges. After pins, each activated disjoint pair has phase $(-1)^{(1+x_i)(1+x_j)}$ and its signed sum is two; all other bits contribute two each. Thus at least $2^{n/2}$ groups contribute nonzero terms. The source has the all-ones word and full affine hull by single-coordinate flips. This refutes universal polynomial explicit grouping in this particular representation, not arbitrary SAT algorithms or local private-chain cancellation.
\end{proof}

\section{BA20: Projected affine-cover consumption with authenticated lifts}\label{sec:ba20}
We target Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} by avoiding full support and full signed-mode enumeration. BS19/GD26/DA20 exact wide projection, GD27/I26 signed-mode consumers and DR20's joint-support hardness make a zero-preserving decision representation preferable. The following construction handles general affine-packet guards in its mathematical specification, not merely coordinate frontiers.

\begin{lemma}[Affine subtraction and suffix projection]\label{lem:ba20-proj}
For a finite binary affine flat $F=\{x:Cx=d\}$ and a forbidden affine flat $P=\{x:Ax=b\}$, $F\setminus P$ is a disjoint union of at most $\max(1,\operatorname{rank} A)$ affine flats, uniformly obtained by Gaussian elimination. For a subspace $W$ of actual linear observations, the cylindrical preimage of the projected support of $F$ on $W$ is the affine flat specified by $\operatorname{row}(C)\cap W$ with its induced right-hand sides. Both the projection and a lift of any accepted $W$-word have polynomial bit cost.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Discard inconsistent packets and test intersection. If disjoint, retain $F$; if $F\subseteq P$, delete it. Otherwise partition by the first independent packet equation that fails, retaining preceding equations; at most $\operatorname{rank} A$ such nonempty pieces occur. For the second assertion, a functional on $W$ satisfying the intersection equations agrees with the functional $d$ on $\operatorname{row}(C)$ over their intersection. It therefore defines a functional on their sum and extends to the full dual space. Gaussian elimination constructs the intersection with induced constants and an actual preimage of every accepted word. No semantic identity test is assumed.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Paid projected affine-cover decision]\label{lem:ba20-consume}
For an actual affine guard and $m$ explicitly registered forbidden packets, process any uniformly acquired order. Let $W_i$ be the span of the actual rows of the remaining packets after step $i$. Maintain a union of affine flats giving the cylindrical image of the feasible prefix on $W_i$. At each step subtract the next forbidden packet from each piece and project every surviving piece by Lemma~\ref{lem:ba20-proj}; identical pieces may be deduplicated and two distinct parallel cosets may be replaced by their union, a flat of one greater dimension. Retain the preimages and pointers. This is an exact decision procedure with a polynomial resource bound conditional on a fixed original-input polynomial cap on the number of pieces after compression at every step. The cap can be checked by a paid algorithm returning OPEN when exceeded. No bound on the dimension of the individual pieces or on the suffix rank is required.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Start with the actual guard, including certified unconditional singleton closure. A remaining packet depends only on the previous suffix observations, so a projected prefix word passing the packet has a genuine prefix extension passing it. Induction gives exactness of each projected union. Distinct parallel cosets $x+K,y+K$ have union $x+\operatorname{span}(K,y-x)$ over $\mathbb F_2$; equality of canonical equations and grouping by direction are paid structural operations. Projected pieces can overlap; do not add their cardinalities. The last suffix has zero dimension, so nonempty final support gives SAT. A lift reverses each projection by solving its preimage equations together with the actual retained $W_i$-word; a merge selects a child by membership. Restriction nodes retain their parent. Since suffix spaces are nested, each earlier lift preserves all later owners' observed values; the root lift satisfies the actual guard and every original packet. Verify the source and any separately acquired upstream lift.

At each stage acquire the affine hull of the current union by spanning all piece directions and basepoint differences. Reapply certified singleton closure against the remaining actual packets: a codimension-zero forbidden intersection is contradiction, codimension one forces its complementary equation, otherwise decline. Filter by any acquired necessary equations, preserving guards and reclose after deductions and at stagnation. This preserves all extendible prefix words; the resulting cylinder equations are still in $W_i$. No complete semantic closure is invoked. For an original-$N$ cap $L=(N+2)^a$ with fixed $a$, one step produces at most $\max(1,n)L$ pieces before compression, where $n$ is the actual free dimension. Deduplication and merges only reduce this number; any failed capped step and all scratch pieces are charged. All Gaussian bases, provenance nodes, consumer memberships, pointer accesses, guard versions and source checks have polynomial description lengths, and storing all $O(m(n+1)L)$ generated nodes and their matrices is polynomial. For example, deterministic greedy order discovery tests each remaining candidate, minimizing $\operatorname{rank}(U+U_j)+\operatorname{rank}(V_{\ne j})-\operatorname{rank}(U+V)$ with actual prefix span $U$, suffix span $V$ and candidate span $U_j$. This is polynomial discovery, not a proof of optimality or coverage. Under a fixed polynomial chart cap, each successful step decreases $\mu=1+\text{remaining packet count}$ by one with a single exact child, compatible with Theorem~\ref{thm:aggregate}; no universal bound on successful dispatch is claimed. Serial same-realization time and peak space are polynomial for a capped execution, and $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Full-support obstruction and projected escape]\label{lem:ba20-star}
For $k$ positive NAE triples $(h,a_i,b_i)$ sharing only $h$, any exact union of affine flats contained in the accepted support requires at least $\lceil(3/2)^k\rceil$ pieces, even with arbitrary directions and overlaps. Yet the projected consumer of Lemma~\ref{lem:ba20-consume} has one piece after each processed owner. There are linear SAT NAE sources and a specified prefix order on which even the projected union requires at least $\lceil(3/2)^k\rceil$ flats at a cut.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The independent relative pairs $(a_i+h,b_i+h)$ range over the three nonzero binary words; the support has $2\cdot3^k$ words. The image of an accepted affine flat in each pair is an affine flat of dimension at most one, so the joint relative dimension is at most $k$, with kernel dimension at most one. Each flat covers at most $2^{k+1}$ words. Immediate suffix projection discards private pair observations, leaving every suffix word extendible, hence one full cylinder. For the bad cut append a fresh hub $t$ and distinct private bits $u_i,v_i,z$, with suffix triples $(a_i,t,u_i),(b_i,t,v_i),(h,t,z)$. The whole source is linear and SAT, e.g. $h=t=0,a_i=1,b_i=0$ with suitable private extensions. Its suffix observation span contains every $a_i+h,b_i+h$ through $t$. Process all prefix triples first: their projected support still maps onto exactly the independent punctured pair product, so each projected flat covers at most $2^k$ of its $3^k$ relative words. This is a specified-cut representation lower bound, not an all-order obstruction, not a universal runtime lower bound, and not a claim against a solver that changes the representation or performs stronger preprocessing.
\end{proof}

\section{DS20: Simultaneous affine private-edge block contraction}\label{sec:ds20}
\paragraph{Status.} PROVED scoped, independent review pending. This combines DS15's rank-Hall reconstruction, BS14's private-direction fusion, BS19's wide projection and GD26/GD27's factored affine escape without assuming a complete semantic or signed-mode support oracle. Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} remains OPEN.
\begin{lemma}[Discoverable rank-contracting affine private-edge projection]\label{lem:ds20-private}
After absorbing the actual consistent affine guard, let $A_ix=b_i$ be the forbidden packets in an explicit affine chart, each with independent observation rows of rank $r_i$. Suppose selected free directions $v_e$ each affect one or two owners, with $\{A_iv_e:e\text{ incident to }i\}$ linearly independent for every owner $i$. There is a uniform polynomial-time algorithm to acquire a greedy maximal such collection, simultaneously eliminate its $k$ directions, and reconstruct every satisfying exterior word. The projected problem is an explicit affine-packet registry with rank mass $R'\le R-k$, where $R=\sum_i r_i$. No owner-width bound is required. Nonaffine extra consumers must be accounted for separately, not discarded.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Every selected direction is independent of the others: applying an observation map of any affected owner to a putative nontrivial dependence contradicts local independence. Complete the directions to a basis of the actual free coordinates. Form the multigraph on owners with two-owner directions as edges and one-owner directions as dangling edges. For each owner $i$, Gaussian row reduction of its independent incident columns writes its forbidden event as
\[
 E_i y=h_i,\qquad x_e=f_{ie}(y)\quad(e\text{ incident to }i),
\]
where $y$ is the common exterior coordinate word, $f_{ie}$ is affine, and $\operatorname{rank}E_i=r_i-d_i$ for incident degree $d_i$. Call the owner active at $y$ iff $E_i y=h_i$. It is satisfied if inactive or if an incident edge has bit opposite its forbidden value.
 
Each connected component containing a cycle (including parallel edges) or a dangling edge has an injection of its owners into incident edges: orient a cycle cyclically and assign each other owner a parent edge toward the cycle, or root at a dangling edge and assign each nonroot its parent edge. Set each designated edge opposite its assigned owner's forbidden bit. Distinct edges are assigned consistently, and every exterior word extends; delete this component. For a tree without dangling edges, if any owner is inactive, root there and assign each other owner its parent edge opposite its forbidden bit. If any edge has equal endpoint forbidden bits, set it opposite both and root the two resulting trees at those endpoints. Conversely, if all owners are active and every edge has opposite endpoint forbidden bits, each edge satisfies at most one owner, while a tree has one fewer edge than vertices. Thus precisely the exterior affine packet
\[
 \bigwedge_{i\text{ in tree}}(E_i y=h_i)
 \ \land\
 \bigwedge_{e=ij\text{ in tree}}(f_{ie}(y)+f_{je}(y)=1)
\]
is forbidden. Empty packets are removed; the whole space as a forbidden packet is an immediate contradiction. An isolated owner is the zero-edge case. Its rank bound is $\sum_i(r_i-d_i)+|E|=\sum_i r_i-|E|$ on a tree; for a deleted component $\sum_i r_i\ge\sum_i d_i\ge |E|$. Sum over components. All boundary bits are actual common coordinates, not independently chosen projections. The construction is for existential feasibility, not preservation of model multiplicity.

For discovery enumerate the at most $m(m+1)/2$ support sets $S$ of one or two owners. Compute $V_S=\bigcap_{h\notin S}\ker A_h$ by Gaussian elimination. Maintain each owner's span of already selected images. Within $V_S$, the directions whose image is in that span form a linear subspace. For a singleton, find a basis witness outside it. For a pair, if one basis vector escapes both subspaces, use it; otherwise find one basis witness escaping each and XOR them (each then lies in the other's bad subspace). If either witness is absent, no eligible vector exists. Repeat successful acquisitions at each support set. Failure is monotone as selected image spans grow, so an exhausted support set need not be revisited during that batch. A new direction is independent of all prior directions by the local image test. This is greedy maximality relative to the acquired collection, not maximum-cardinality optimization. In particular, when no direction is acquired the chart has no visible direction supported on one or two owners in any invertible coordinate basis.

Canonicalize each resulting packet and perform charged unconditional singleton/affine closure before and after every accepted deduction and at stagnation. The actual guard parameterization and all basis and reconstruction maps are retained. Under original-$N$ polynomial bit-size hypotheses, the number of Gaussian operations, support tests, edge assignments, output rows and lift costs in a batch is polynomial. Each successful batch strictly decreases $1+R$ for a single child, without resetting rank credit; at most the initial rank mass many successful batches are possible for this admitted phase. Include all failed acquisitions, row reduction, map composition and source verification. Same serial realization has polynomial $T,S$ and $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$; no claim for arbitrary alternation with rank-increasing adapters. The lemma requires actual affine-packet representation, not a compact unverified semantic projection.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Post-normalization visible-code gap]\label{lem:ds20-gap}
If DS15 rank-Hall extraction leaves a strict core and Lemma~\ref{lem:ds20-private} acquires no direction, then its visible linear code
$C=\operatorname{im}(x\mapsto(A_i x)_i)$ has minimum nonzero block weight at least three. The remaining decision asks for a codeword avoiding $b_i$ in every owner block, with the strict rank-Hall inequalities. This is an equivalent representation, not a proved tractable class. Fano's raw NAE registry and any sign neighbor have no one-/two-owner visible direction: a nonconstant bit cut separates $t(7-t)\ge6$ vertex pairs, each crossed triple contributes exactly two, and every pair belongs to exactly one triple. Thus at least three owners are affected, invariant under basis changes. Both labels occur and other terminals can solve them. A diagonal hard sequence for a fixed total portfolio with guaranteed paid preprocessing cannot owe superpolynomial work merely to the admitted batch phases; exclusion of such residual cores by another uniform paid method remains OPEN.
\end{lemma}

\section{MS27: Joint triple occupancy and integer support cancellation}\label{sec:ms27}
Attack Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} with a common local moment system, combining MS26 conditional closure, BA19 signed-integer balance, and the occupancy channel. The signed-mode barriers of GD27, BD20, DR20 and I26 do not justify a free exact support oracle.
\begin{lemma}[Paid support-coupled marginal certificate]\label{lem:ms27-support}
For an explicit Boolean source chart, introduce a mass for each local word on every subset of at most three variables, with zero on prohibited local words, normalization to one, and equality of overlap marginals. Every actual model under the chart guard gives a one-hot feasible solution. The rational nonnegative system and the signed integer system are each necessary. Compute the maximal support of the nonnegative system, and restrict the signed integer system to that support. Inconsistency of either test certifies UNSAT. Every coordinate absent from the maximal support is a certified local forbidden tuple under the actual guard.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Each genuine model gives a nonnegative and integral feasible vector, hence has zero in every LP-impossible coordinate. Exact rational LP maximization of each coordinate finds its possible positivity, and a convex average of the positive witnesses realizes the entire maximal support. Signed integer feasibility on that support is decidable by polynomial-bit Smith or Hermite normal forms. No converse follows: the two feasible witnesses need not be a common nonnegative integral vector. The system has $O(n^3)$ coordinates and polynomially many marginal equations. Charge construction, rational arithmetic, discovery, certificate replay, guard versions, failed probes, storage and renewed certified closure. On a fixed explicit registry the number of permanent tuple deletions is polynomial, and repeating the procedure with a final unsuccessful sweep is polynomial in the chart encoding. No reserve reset or free semantic closure is permitted. Wide constraints and arbitrary guards need exact paid scopes or must be declared safe weakenings. This does not bound unbounded nesting, arbitrary scope growth or total branching, and physical quotient transfer requires its own authentication.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Balanced triangle saturation and strict joint gain]\label{lem:ms27-fano}
For an unpinned linear positive NAE-3 source, let $d_{uv}$ denote the shared binary mismatch marginal. Each triangle $t$ has $\sum_{e\in t}d_e\le2$ in the nonnegative relaxation, with equality for each source owner. A nonnegative combination of cooccurrence triangles whose edge coefficient is constant on the three edges of each owner forces every positively weighted triangle to be tight. In particular, the Fano NAE source passes the independent nonnegative and signed integer systems but fails the support-coupled integer test.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The sum of triangle weights equals the sum of the constant owner coefficients by counting three edges on both sides. The weighted sum of triangle slacks is therefore zero, so positive-weight triangles have zero mass on both all-equal words. Fano's seven owners partition the edges of $K_7$; each edge belongs to five of the 35 triangles. Thus every triangle must be tight. In a signed integer solution after support restriction, all triangles satisfy $d_{ab}+d_{ac}+d_{bc}=2$. On any $K_5$, fix distinct $a,b$ and subtract the equations for $acd,bcd$ for each pair of the other three vertices. The differences $d_{ac}-d_{bc}$ have pairwise sums zero and hence all vanish over the rationals. Varying the vertices makes all edge values equal, necessarily $2/3$, contradicting integer marginal values.
For independent LP feasibility let $c_{uv}=-1/3$ on cooccurrence edges, zero elsewhere, and use spin marginals $p_t(s)=(1+\sum_{uv\subset t}c_{uv}s_us_v)/8$. These are nonnegative, normalized and consistent on overlaps, with the actual forbidden owner words absent. Independent signed integer feasibility follows by assigning each singleton bit moment zero, one pair product moment $-1$ per actual owner and all other pair moments zero, and triple product moments zero. Boolean inclusion-exclusion gives integral masses; the owner all-equal words have zero mass. This proves strict gain over either independent test, not over MS21's earlier Fano PSD refutation.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Raw high-girth root obstruction]\label{lem:ms27-barrier}
Every raw unpinned linear signed NAE-3 source with incidence girth at least eight passes the root support-coupled triple marginal test, with no additional LP-impossible local tuple. Such sources include arbitrarily large UNSAT instances.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Set $c_{uv}=-\eta_u\eta_v/3$ on an owner edge for its two literal signs, zero off cooccurrence edges. A nonowner triple has at most two cooccurrence edges: otherwise distinct owners form a Berge triangle, or linearity implies that the triple is itself an owner. Thus the spin formula of Lemma~\ref{lem:ms27-fano} is strictly positive on all eight nonowner words and has exactly the six allowed words positive on each actual owner. This realizes the full allowed support. Assign singleton bit moments zero. Each owner admits signed integer masses of total one with these singleton moments, using the relative unimodular simplex from BA19. Its pair product moments are independent of other owners because each pair belongs to at most one owner. Set nonedge pair moments and nonowner triple moments zero, reconstruct integer local masses by inclusion-exclusion, and retain the actual owner masses. Marginals agree and support is permitted. Hence both coupled tests pass.
For existence, choose $4n$ random triples of distinct vertices. The expected number of repeated-pair configurations and Berge triangles is bounded independently of $n$ by counting two- and three-edge patterns. Delete one edge per defect in an outcome with bounded defects, retaining $m>3n$ distinct triples and girth at least eight for sufficiently large $n$. Independently randomize literal signs on incidences. The probability a fixed word satisfies all owners is $(3/4)^m$; $2^n(3/4)^m<1$. Some signing is UNSAT. This is a symbolic raw-source family, not necessarily native degree four or four perfect partitions. No conditional-probe, higher-level, PSD, other representation or unrestricted lower bound follows.
\end{proof}

\section{RT26: Simultaneous bounded occurrence, logarithmic girth and resolution obstruction}\label{sec:rt26}
Respond to DA20 Lemmas~\ref{lem:da20-exp}--\ref{lem:da20-cap} and MS27 Lemma~\ref{lem:ms27-barrier} on the same family, not merely separate adversaries.
\begin{lemma}[Eight-partition critical family]\label{lem:rt26-eight}
There are arbitrarily large inclusion-minimal UNSAT signed NAE-3 registries on $n$ available variables, $O(n)$ owners, maximum occurrence eight, and incidence girth $\Omega(\log n)$. For some absolute $\delta>0$, every set of $1\le s\le\delta n$ owners has more than $7s/4$ incident variables. Every single-owner literal flip gives a SAT neighbor on identical scopes. The roots pass the raw MS27 support-coupled triple test, and every ordinary resolution refutation of the paired CNF has size $2^{\Omega(n)}$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Take $n$ divisible by three, eight independent uniform permutations, each partitioned into disjoint ordered triples, giving $m=8n/3$ labeled owners. For any fixed $s$ owner slots and any $u$-set of variables, the probability that all chosen owners lie in that set is the product over partitions of $(u)_{3s_i}/(n)_{3s_i}$, at most $(u/n)^{3s}$. Here $(a)_b$ denotes the falling factorial, with impossible events assigned probability zero. Put $u=\lfloor7s/4\rfloor$. As in DA20 the union bound is at most $[C(s/n)^{1/4}]^s$ for an absolute constant $C$; take $\delta$ small enough that $C\delta^{1/4}<1/2$. Splitting at $\sqrt n$ shows failure probability $o(1)$.

For a simple incidence cycle of length $2\ell$ with distinct variable labels and owner labels, choose its ordered labels in at most $n^\ell m^\ell$ ways. Within each partition, the two designated variables for each chosen owner must occupy two distinct slots in that triple. Inconsistent repeated variable requirements have probability zero; otherwise at most $6^\ell$ choices of ordered slots and probability at most $(n-2\ell)^{-2\ell}$ for each choice, by uniform permutation and independence across partitions. For $\ell\le n/4$ the expected number of such cycles is therefore at most $64^\ell$. With $g=\lfloor\log n/(4\log64)\rfloor$, the expected number for $2\le\ell\le g$ is $O(n^{1/4})$. By Markov, with probability $1-o(1)$ at most $n^{1/2}$ such cycles exist. Delete one owner from each listed cycle, retaining expansion and degree bound, and more than $5n/2$ owners for all sufficiently large $n$. Random independent literal signs on the remaining incidences give expected model count $2^n(3/4)^m<1$, so some signing is UNSAT. Extract an inclusion-minimal UNSAT owner set. This extraction is existential and is not a polynomial SAT subroutine.

Every small owner set has more than $s/2$ variables of degree one within it, by counting $3s$ incidences, so is satisfiable by recursive private-variable extension. The minimal UNSAT core has more than $\lfloor\delta n\rfloor$ owners and $\Omega(n)$ used variables (maximum occurrence eight). Removal of any owner admits a witness that violates that owner; flipping any one of its three signs makes that witness legal. Root singleton closure has no pins and the girth admits the MS27 triple-support construction for both labels. The DA20 minimum-entailing-owner measure proof applies unchanged to signed NAE: subadditivity under resolution, initial measure at most one, and the first line with measure above $\lfloor\delta n\rfloor/2$ has measure at most $\lfloor\delta n\rfloor$. Every degree-one variable of a minimum supporting set must occur in that clause, since otherwise its bit can be repaired while preserving the falsifying assignment. Width is $\Omega(n)$; Ben-Sasson--Wigderson width-size with initial width three gives exponential general resolution size. This is a restricted proof-system bound for a sparse encoded family, not an unrestricted time lower bound.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Mixed binary/ternary degree-three transport]\label{lem:rt26-split}
Replace each variable by one copy per owner incidence and impose equality on consecutive copies using signed binary NAE. This is a uniform linear-owner-size parsimonious transport to a mixed binary/ternary registry of maximum occurrence three. Every resolution refutation of the transported paired CNF yields a resolution-with-weakening refutation of the original with no more than a constant factor in line count. The same exponential resolution bound therefore holds on the transported family.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Each legal copy chain is constant, so the projection and lift are inverse. Identify every copy with its original variable in a resolution DAG. Equality axioms become tautologies; original ternary clauses become original clauses. Discard tautological lines. For a non-tautological image of a resolution child, either the images of the two parents resolve on the image pivot (possibly followed by weakening), or a parent image subsumes the child because the image pivot or its complement already occurs in a residual parent clause. If a parent becomes tautological, its complementary pair must involve the pivot image, since otherwise the child would be tautological too; the other parent then subsumes the child. Both parents cannot be tautological with a non-tautological child. Weakening maps to weakening. Hence the projected refutation is valid and size-linear in line count. The equality-chain discovery and contraction here is polynomial by explicit binary owner closure and returns the raw degree-eight chart. This is not a strict E4/B4 physical compiler or a raw four-perfect-partition ternary family; MS27 is applied after certified equalities are contracted, not directly to binary owners.
\end{proof}

\section{BH20: Protected-leaf projection and bounded-premise nonlinear width}\label{sec:bh20}
This addresses the same RT26 critical family, and extends BH19's exact forest consumer and DS20 private-direction normalization without assuming that coordinate interfaces have small affine rank. Write $s_0=\lfloor\delta n\rfloor$ for the RT26 expansion threshold. Each owner set of size $1\le s\le s_0$ has more than $s/2$ degree-one variables within it. All raw owners here are signed NAE-3 on distinct variables, optionally with one forbidden word relaxed.
\begin{lemma}[Protected-leaf exact projection and paid residual core]\label{lem:bh20-peel}
Given an explicit region $S$ and boundary $B$ containing every variable shared outside $S$ and every variable needed by the actual guards or protected external map, repeatedly remove any owner with an unprotected degree-one variable in the remaining region. The projected support on $B$ is unchanged, with a polynomial-time reverse lift. If $|S|\le s_0$ and $k=|B|$, the remaining nonempty owner core has size less than $2k$ and at most $6k$ incident variables. Its exact projected table and witnesses cost at most $2^{7k}\operatorname{poly}(N)$, where $N$ is the original input length. No recognition of the expansion promise is needed if the actual core-size cap is checked.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
A private variable admits a legal value for every fixing of its two other coordinates: the two rejected words are complementary, and relaxation only removes rejection. Record the removed owner and private variable; in reverse order the private variable occurs neither in the surviving region nor outside it and can be set to satisfy that owner without invalidating any already reconstructed owner. All protected variables are unchanged. At stagnation every degree-one variable of a nonempty core belongs to $B$, so expansion gives $|C|/2<k$; at most $3|C|$ variables occur. Enumerating the union of core and boundary variables, retaining one witness per accepted boundary word, proves the claimed bound, including reconstruction. A fixed cap $k\le C_0\log_2(N+2)$ gives polynomial work, with fixed $C_0$. Replacing $s\ge2$ owners by one projected relation strictly decreases owner count, so $\mu=1+\#\text{owners}$ pays single-child contraction for a sequence of these operations on a fixed original-$N$ capped explicit registry. Each new table and log is polynomial, and the number of steps is at most the initial owner count. This is not a common potential for arbitrary representations or branching; region discovery and all failed trials must be charged, and eligibility is not universal. Run certified closure again after every accepted projection.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Raw coordinate interface barrier]\label{lem:bh20-boundary}
On an RT26 inclusion-minimal UNSAT core, every region of $1\le s\le s_0$ owners has more than $s/2$ actual shared exterior variables. Every rooted owner-partition tree of maximum fanout $q\ge2$ and leaf regions of size at most $s_0$ has an interface of size greater than $s_0/(2q)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
A globally private variable would contradict minimal UNSAT by the preceding extension argument. Hence each degree-one variable inside a region must occur outside it, giving the first assertion. The root has more than $s_0$ owners. Descend through children of size greater than $s_0$ until none exists. The last such node has a child of size greater than $s_0/q$ and at most $s_0$ by disjoint partition and the fanout cap. Apply the first assertion. The bound concerns raw coordinate interfaces, not compressed syndrome ranks or arbitrary DAG consumers.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Complete detection of small-support pin conflicts]\label{lem:bh20-guard}
Under a consistent coordinate guard fixing $k$ variables, if a subregistry of at most $s_0$ owners has no satisfying extension, it contains a contradictory subregistry of less than $2k$ owners (no such subregistry exists for $k=0$). If the incidence girth is greater than $4k$, singleton Boolean domain closure of the entire guarded chart detects every such contradiction. For failed-literal tests use the girth threshold for $k+1$ pins.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Choose an inclusion-minimal contradictory subregistry under the guard. An unpinned private variable would allow extension of a witness for the remaining owners, a contradiction. Expansion therefore gives fewer than $2k$ owners. A simple incidence cycle in that subregistry would have length at most twice its owner count, less than $4k$, hence it is a forest under the stated girth. Domain arc consistency on a factor forest is complete: choose any surviving root value, a supporting owner row and independent child-subtree extensions recursively. For signed NAE-3, including the relaxed owner, domain arc consistency is exactly singleton forbidden-word propagation on Boolean domains. The whole chart contains every inference from the forest, so the same contradiction is detected unless another conflict is detected earlier. This proves only completeness for the indicated support scale, not semantic closure. In particular every pair word extends on a small subregistry at sufficiently large girth: any contradictory minimal subset under two pins would be a forest, and every signed NAE forest admits any two pins by filling the unique path between them, choosing each off-path third variable to satisfy its path owner and extending outward. Separate components extend independently.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Bounded-premise nonlinear coordinate width]\label{lem:bh20-width}
On the critical RT26 root, consider a semantic derivation from original owner relations in which each new relation follows from at most $q\ge2$ earlier relations. Each relation may be an arbitrary nonlinear Boolean function or circuit on its declared original-coordinate scope. A guarded conclusion is represented as an implication with all guard coordinates included in the scope. Every refutation contains a line of coordinate width greater than $\lfloor s_0/q\rfloor/2$, for $s_0\ge q$. In particular a fixed-fan-in, logarithmic-coordinate-width certificate system cannot refute this family.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Let $m(R)$ be the minimum number of source owners entailing $R$. Initial measures are at most one; tautologies have measure zero. Soundness gives $m(R)\le\sum_i m(R_i)$ for the premises. In a minimum supporting set of $s>0$ owners, every degree-one variable must belong to the declared scope of $R$: otherwise a witness satisfying the other owners and falsifying $R$ could be repaired at that variable, still falsifying $R$. If $s\le s_0$, expansion gives width greater than $s/2$. The final contradiction has measure greater than $s_0$. The first line of measure exceeding $\lfloor s_0/q\rfloor$ has measure at most $q\lfloor s_0/q\rfloor\le s_0$, proving the claim. The argument extends RT26 beyond resolution but does not bound proof size or unrestricted runtime; dense affine observations, unbounded-premise global certificates, and other exact compressed representations are not excluded.
\end{proof}

\section{DP21: Exact four-scope lift and simultaneous high-girth obstruction}\label{sec:dp21}
Attack Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} on the same raw source as MS27 and RT26, rather than increasing local scope without a strict progress proof.
\begin{lemma}[Full-support symmetric triple-to-four LP lift]\label{lem:dp21-lp}
For a complement-invariant Boolean chart with only constraints of arity at most three, suppose a consistent nonnegative triple marginal system has complete locally allowed support. It has a complement-symmetric such system (average with global complement), and admits a consistent extension to every four-set with complete locally allowed support. More generally every complement-symmetric feasible triple marginal system extends, with zero four-words exactly those whose triple restriction has zero mass in that system.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Write the symmetric triple probabilities as $(1+\sum_{i<j}c_{ij}s_is_j)/8$, where $s_i=\pm1$ and the consistent pair correlations are $c_{ij}$. On a four-set let $a_s=1+\sum_{i<j}c_{ij}s_is_j$, $p_s=\prod_i s_i$. The extension has mass $(a_s+p_s q)/16$. Put $L=\max_{p_s=1}(-a_s)$ and $U=\min_{p_t=-1}a_t$. Opposite-parity words differ in one or three bits; globally complement $t$ if needed so they differ in one bit. This preserves $a_t,p_t$. Then $a_s+a_t$ is twice the nonnegative triple numerator on their shared three bits. Thus $L\le U$. Choose $q=(L+U)/2$. Any zero mass implies equality with an attaining opposite-parity bound, hence a zero shared triple; conversely nonnegativity and marginalization force every extension of a zero triple to be zero. Different four-sets share at most three variables and hence agree on overlaps. Charge the supplied triple certificate, all rational bit arithmetic and $O(n^4)$ tables. Neither higher arities nor arbitrary unrepresented guards are covered.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Signed integer four-marginal lift on the MS27 family]\label{lem:dp21-int}
Every raw unpinned linear signed NAE-3 registry of incidence girth at least eight has consistent signed integer marginals of arity at most four, supported on locally allowed words.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Use integer multilinear bit moments $M_A$, $|A|\le4$, with $M_\emptyset=1$, $M_{\{v\}}=0$. At each owner use signed integer masses on literal words $100,010,001,110$. Their augmented incidence columns form a unimodular basis, so the prescribed literal singleton moments (the literal sign bits) and total one are achieved. Convert to actual variable moments. Owner pairs and triples are private by linearity. Initialize other moments to zero. For each owner $e$ and outsider $d$ let $P_0=\prod_{i\in e}(1-l_i)$, $P_1=\prod_{i\in e}l_i$, with $l_i=x_i$ or $1-x_i$. These have zero expectation by the chosen owner masses. The polynomial $x_d(P_0+P_1)$ has degree at most three and coefficients $\pm1$ on $x_dx_ix_j$ for each pair in $e$. The outsider is cooccurrence-adjacent to at most one vertex of $e$: two adjacencies would violate linearity or form a Berge triangle. Choose two nonadjacent vertices $i,j$; the moment $M_{\{d,i,j\}}$ has just one cooccurring pair and is private to this owner-outsider equation. Solve its unit pivot for zero expectation. Then solve $x_dP_1=0$ using the fourth moment of $e\cup\{d\}$, with unit coefficient and a unique owner by linearity. These private choices do not affect other equations. Subtraction gives $x_dP_0=0$ and both forbidden indicators also vanish multiplied by $1-x_d$. Integer inclusion-exclusion defines all local masses and enforces overlap consistency and all forbidden-word zeros. All pivots have bounded bit size here: a private pivot depends on boundedly many initial moments, not another equation's private moment. No common nonnegative integral point is claimed.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Joint barrier and original-input reserve]\label{lem:dp21-reserve}
The MS27 support-coupled test generalized to four-variable scopes passes on the very same raw degree-eight expanding minimally UNSAT families and their single-sign SAT neighbors of RT26, retaining their separate resolution obstruction. Indeed MS27's full allowed triple LP support lifts by Lemma~\ref{lem:dp21-lp}, and Lemma~\ref{lem:dp21-int} gives signed integer feasibility on that support. On a fixed explicit root registry the number of distinct possible forbidden words of scopes at most four is $O(n^4)$; $1+$ the number not yet excluded is a polynomial credit for strict permanent exclusions, not for failed or reset attempts. Here the credit does not decrease. Repeated pure symmetric LP lifts cannot provide new root cuts when the triple support is already complete. No obstruction to stronger joint systems, conditional probes, higher scopes, nonresolution transformations or the full portfolio follows.
\end{lemma}

\section{S26: Rank-one private block projection by dual dependencies}\label{sec:s26}

DS20 Lemma~\ref{lem:ds20-private} declines when every visible direction affects at least three owners; BS19's single pivot, BA20's suffix projection, GD27/I26/DR20's signed-mode acquisition barriers and RT26's joint raw obstruction motivate the following exact simultaneous contraction. This is not a native physical compiler.

\begin{lemma}[Paid rank-one private block elimination]\label{lem:s26-dual}
Parameterize the actual consistent affine guard, and apply certified rank-zero/one closure. On the free chart write coordinates $(u,z)$, where $u$ has dimension $h>0$. Suppose every live forbidden packet has private coefficient rank at most one, and all other consumers are independent of $u$ (or exactly included in the registered packets). Every private-rank-one packet can be put by row operations into the form $G_i(z)=g_i$, $a_i u=\beta_i+c_i z$, where $a_i\ne0$. Avoiding it imposes $a_i u=1+\beta_i+c_i z$ precisely when its activation equations $G_i(z)=g_i$ hold. Rank-zero packets remain. Put $b_i=1+\beta_i$. For every binary left-kernel vector $\lambda\ne0$ of the matrix with rows $a_i$, the following affine exterior packet is forbidden:
\[
  G_i(z)=g_i\quad(i\in\operatorname{supp}\lambda),\qquad
  \left(\sum_i\lambda_i c_i\right)z=1+\sum_i\lambda_i b_i .
\]
Avoiding all such packets, together with the unchanged rank-zero packets, is exactly the existential projection. Every accepted exterior word lifts by Gaussian elimination, without preserving counts.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For fixed $z$, an active owner's private forbidden value is one linear equation and its avoidance is the complementary equation. Inactive owners impose nothing. The active system is inconsistent iff some subset of active rows has XOR-zero coefficient and XOR-one right-hand side, by ordinary Gaussian elimination with tracked row combinations. Extending that subset's indicator by zeros is exactly a displayed dependency, and conversely each displayed forbidden packet certifies an inconsistent active subsystem. Inconsistent activation equations and empty affine packets may be deleted; a whole-space forbidden packet certifies contradiction. For a consistent system solve the actual active equations, reconstruct the original affine guard parameterization and verify every original owner. Conditional activations are not globally forced facts.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Discovery and acquisition cap.}
A greedy candidate private subspace is obtainable without a target solution: start at $H=0$ in the guard tangent (and annihilator of protected observations). For each owner with nonzero current image require the next direction $v$ to satisfy $A_i v\in A_iH$, a linear condition; for an image of rank zero impose no restriction. Find a direction outside $H$ in the intersection by Gaussian elimination, append it, and repeat. This preserves private rank at most one at every owner, and returns a maximal subspace for that greedy history in polynomial bit work, not an optimal one. Quotient invisible directions first, or separately eliminate them. In the checker only the simpler greedy coordinate independent-set acquisition is executed. A supplied private basis can also be verified directly.

Gaussian elimination with owner-indexed coefficient tracking supplies a row basis and fundamental dependencies. Connect owner indices appearing in each such dependency; every kernel vector is a sum of these basis dependencies, which are supported inside the resulting disjoint components. Any inconsistent activated kernel vector therefore has an inconsistent component part. In a component of nullity $k_j$ enumerate its $2^{k_j}-1$ nonzero dependencies. In a rank-one component of $m_j$ identical nonzero rows it suffices to test all $\binom{m_j}{2}$ pairs, since inconsistent equal-coefficient equations have opposite right-hand sides. This yields a pre-dispatch candidate bound $D=\sum_j D_j$, with the indicated pair shortcut. Compute its bit length and decline before enumeration if beyond a fixed original-$N$ polynomial cap. Each candidate is acquired and verified by Gaussian elimination, retaining actual row IDs and private basis. This is an exact decision relation, not sum-preserving. Canonicalize via RREF, reclose after accepted projection and at stagnation. Keep a fixed cap on current and scratch encoded representation and total provenance. Given cap compliance, the operation removes $h$ free dimensions; if the private directions are injectively visible to the registered observation map, its global rank decreases by at least $h$. One continuation is charged under Theorem~\ref{thm:aggregate} or the S23 rank reserve. Owner rank mass need not decrease. Repeated moves of this type alone have at most the initial free dimension many accepted steps; every failed candidate, log and reconstruction is charged. No reset of the original cap or arbitrary other representation growth is licensed.

\begin{lemma}[Block-distance-three escape and explicit-cover obstruction]\label{lem:s26-barrier}
There exist rank-one private projection instances on which no nonzero private direction affects fewer than three owners, yet the preceding rule eliminates a linear-dimensional private subspace with only linearly many candidates. Conversely, there are polynomial-size rank-one private block instances, all satisfiable and stagnant under single-packet affine closure, on which exact explicit forbidden-affine-packet projection onto the designated exterior requires exponentially many packets.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For the first assertion take a binary Hamming code of length $m=2^k-1$ with parity-check columns all distinct nonzero $k$-bit vectors. Its kernel has dimension $m-k$ and minimum distance three (no one or two columns sum to zero, and a column pair and their sum give three). Use a generator of that kernel for $u\mapsto(a_i u)_i$, and forbid $z_i=0,\ a_i u=\beta_i$ with arbitrary constants. The private direction supports have size at least three, while the left-kernel dimension is $k$, so at most $m$ candidates suffice. This is a supplied protected private subspace statement, not a claim that DS20 cannot exploit some exterior direction.

For the second assertion use $s\ge3$ row vectors $a_1,\dots,a_s$ consisting of a basis of dimension $s-1$ and its sum, so the sole nonzero dependency on distinct rows uses every row. Duplicate each owner twice with independent activation bits $z_{i,0},z_{i,1}$; an active copy requires $a_i u=b_i$ with $\sum_i b_i=1$. The original forbidden packets are $z_{i,j}=0,\ a_i u=1+b_i$. All have rank two, and setting all activation bits to one makes the source trivially SAT. Every nonzero private direction changes an even positive number of distinct row values, hence affects at least four owners. The exact exterior rejection relation is
\[
 \prod_{i=1}^s\{00,01,10\},
\]
since inconsistency occurs iff every distinct row is activated by at least one copy. Its cardinality is $3^s$. An affine flat contained in it has affine projection onto each pair of dimension at most one, because the projection omits $11$. Its cardinality is therefore at most $2^s$, since its pair projections jointly identify every word. Any explicit union of forbidden affine flats giving this rejection relation needs at least $\lceil(3/2)^s\rceil$ members, even allowing arbitrary affine directions and overlap. This is a designated-projection representation lower bound, not a runtime lower bound or a universal portfolio counterexample. The rejection relation itself has a short factored Boolean representation and a simple decision escape. It refutes a universal cap for this particular exact explicit projection, not every alternative representation.
\end{proof}
