Fixed $r$, polynomial numerical $W$ and $g=O(\log N)$ suffice; binary-encoded exponentially large weights do not satisfy the numerical bound but can still pass the actual key cap. \begin{lemma}[All-direction magnitude barrier with field bypass]\label{lem:dp22-magnitude}
On an unguarded complete-pair spin energy with every pair coefficient of magnitude one, every non-invisible affine direction has $\Omega(n)$ distinct absolute odd-part magnitudes. Thus no fixed BA21 magnitude cap, DS21 fixed affine rank cap, or BD21 sparse/dominance rule covers all such unchanged charts. Uniform complete-pair weights nevertheless have rational cut rank one for every order.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
A nontrivial direction toggles the crossing pairs of a cut $(A,B)$, $1\le |A|\le|B|$. For independent uniform spins on $A$, each field $f_j=\sum_{i\in A}J_{ji}s_i$ is nonzero with probability at least one half: odd sums cannot vanish; for positive even size the central binomial probability is at most one half. Some word has $t\ge |B|/2$ nonzero fields. Starting with anti-aligned suffix spins, flip these $t$ spins one at a time to get $t+1$ strictly increasing values of the odd-part sum, hence at least $\lceil(t+1)/2\rceil$ different magnitudes. Passing to any affine section preserves the set of absolute values because moving along the direction negates the odd part. DS21 supplies the rank $n-2$ and BD21 is excluded for sufficiently large $n$ by cut size and unit coefficients. The uniform matrix has constant entries, rank one. DS21's projective Steiner families furnish both source labels; the all-positive family has the rank-one bypass, while arbitrary signs need not. This excludes a move family, not all algorithms or non-surjective guard deductions.
\end{proof}

\section{RT27: All-direction magnitude and explicit Walsh obstruction}\label{sec:rt27}
\begin{lemma}[All-direction obstruction to fixed-spectrum normalization]\label{lem:rt27-spectrum}
For $n=2^k-1$, $k\ge3$, use the triples $\{a,b,a+b\}$ on nonzero vectors of $\mathbb F_2^k$, with arbitrary literal signs per owner. Each pair occurs once. The scaled violation count $Q=4E=m+\sum_{i<j}\sigma_{ij}s_i s_j$, $s_i=(-1)^{x_i}$, $|\sigma_{ij}|=1$, $m=n(n-1)/6$. In every nonglobal-complement nonzero affine direction the odd term $B$ has at least $\lceil n/8\rceil$ distinct absolute magnitudes. This is invariant under invertible affine recharts and global-complement gauge quotient.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The direction defines a nontrivial cut $(S,T)$, where $q=|T|\ge n/2$ after swapping sides. Its odd term is $B=\sum_{i\in S,j\in T}\sigma_{ij}s_i s_j$. Uniform spins on $S$ give each $w_j=\sum_{i\in S}\sigma_{ij}s_i$ a probability at least $1/2$ of being nonzero by conditioning on all but one spin. Some $S$ assignment has $t\ge\lceil q/2\rceil$ nonzero weights. Flipping the corresponding $T$ spins successively from all negative to all positive contributions gives $t+1$ strictly increasing sums. Absolute value identifies at most two, proving the bound. The absolute odd term is independent of the choice of representative of each direction orbit and is gauge invariant. Thus BA21's fixed-$K$ criterion fails for every nongauge direction when $n>8K$. BD21's crossing support is at least $n-1$, with equal absolute coefficients and no dominance. DS21's odd-mask affine-difference rank is $n-2$ (differences span the even subsets within each side). I27's offset is $-2m$. Raw singleton closure fixes nothing. No claim for nonsurjective guards or stronger prior cuts.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[All-direction explicit Walsh blowup]\label{lem:rt27-blowup}
For the unsigned subfamily every nongauge single-direction exact minimized energy has at least $2^{q-1}-1-\binom n2$ nonzero Walsh coefficients, where $q$ is the larger cut side size.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Here $B=(\sum_S s_i)(\sum_T s_j)$. In a section fixing one $S$ spin, restrict the remaining $S$ spins to $+1$. The absolute odd term reduces to $|S||\sum_T s_j|$. For even $q$, Lemma~\ref{lem:ba21-blowup} gives every even coefficient nonzero. For odd $q$, average the even-$q+1$ absolute sum over the extra spin: $\frac12(|v+1|+|v-1|)=|v|$ for odd integer $v$, retaining all even coefficients not using that spin. Restriction cannot increase support. Subtracting from the quadratic $A$ cancels at most $1+\binom n2$ coefficients. Affine bijections on the quotient preserve support size; the gauge invariant coefficients survive its exact quotient. Input length $O(n^2\log n)$, hence explicit materialization exceeds every fixed original-input polynomial cap. The factored expression remains compact, so this is not unrestricted hardness. Indeed $Q=m+((\sum s_i)^2-n)/2>0$ for unsigned $n\ge7$, a simple polynomial refutation.
\end{proof}

\section{BH21: Collective count normalization beyond every fixed magnitude cap}\label{sec:bh21}
We attack the universal eligibility question in Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} for BA21 and BD21, and connect DP01/S06 count aggregation to MS28 and BW21 actual energy/guard feedback. All claims below are scoped, independent review pending.

\begin{lemma}[Every-direction magnitude obstruction]\label{lem:bh21-spectrum}
Let a field-free quadratic spin energy be $E=C+\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}s_is_j$ with $s_i\in\{-1,1\}$ and every $J_{ij}\ne0$. Modulo the global complement kernel, every nonzero affine flip direction splits the coordinates into two nonempty sets $A,B$, with $|B|\ge |A|$ after interchange. In the section of that direction, the number of distinct magnitudes of $E(x)-E(x+q)$ is at least
\[
\left\lceil\frac{\lceil |B|/2\rceil+1}{2}\right\rceil.
\]
Thus no fixed BA21 magnitude cap is universally eligible on these raw full-support charts, even with arbitrary invertible affine reparameterization.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The difference is twice the crossing bilinear sum $\sum_{j\in B}s_j\sum_{i\in A}J_{ij}s_i$; its absolute value is constant on each flip orbit. For uniform independent $s_i$ in $A$, each inner sum is zero with probability at most $1/2$ by conditioning on all but one nonzero term. Hence some fixed $A$ word leaves $r\ge\lceil |B|/2\rceil$ nonzero coefficients. Start the remaining $s_j$ opposite to their respective coefficient signs, then reverse those $r$ spins successively. The sum strictly increases at each step, giving $r+1$ distinct real values. Absolute value identifies at most two of them. The count is invariant under a change of basis since a direction still corresponds to an actual flip and a section contains one point per orbit. This is not a claim about charts after arbitrary guards or nonlinear transformations.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Baseline-subtracted component count consumer]\label{lem:bh21-count}
For an explicit integer quadratic spin energy $E=C+\sum_i h_i s_i+\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}s_is_j$, try a baseline $\beta$ from zero and the distinct pair coefficients (including implicit zeros). Form the residual graph with edges $J_{ij}\ne\beta$. Let its connected components be $G_\ell$. For each, acquire the exact minimum local residual energy $D_\ell(t)$ subject to $\sum_{i\in G_\ell}s_i=t$, with one attaining word. This acquisition is polynomial if every component either has constant residual pair coefficient on all distinct pairs or has size at most $C_0\log_2(N+2)$ for a fixed $C_0$, where $N$ is original encoded input length. Then the global minimum and a genuine minimizing word are deterministically computable in polynomial time, irrespective of the number of components or the product of their count ranges.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Subtract the uniform baseline, using the identity
\[
E=C+\frac{\beta}{2}\bigl((\sum_i s_i)^2-n\bigr)+\sum_\ell\bigl[\sum_{i\in G_\ell}h_i s_i+\sum_{i<j\in G_\ell}(J_{ij}-\beta)s_is_j\bigr].
\]
For uniform residual coefficient $a_\ell$, the pair term is $a_\ell(t^2-|G_\ell|)/2$. For fixed number of negative spins, sorting local fields gives the minimizing linear term (select the largest fields for negative spins). For capped small components enumerate their words and retain the minimum for each count. Pins can be substituted before recognition, adding fields and constants. For the union of the first $j$ components, store $M_j(T)=\min_t[M_{j-1}(T-t)+D_j(t)]$, with $M_0(0)=0$ and infeasible entries infinite. There are at most $2n+1$ counts at any stage. Minimize $C+\beta(T^2-n)/2+M_k(T)$, and follow attaining pointers and local words. Counts only compress the baseline coupling; local residual terms are never discarded. Discovery tries at most $O(n^2)$ baselines, builds and checks components by matrix scans, and declines before any oversized nonuniform local enumeration. For each admitted trial there are $O(n^3)$ DP transitions and at most $n(N+2)^{C_0}$ enumerated words, each with polynomial verification. Integer bit lengths are polynomial by the original coefficient bounds and sums. Store polynomial tables and reverse logs; all failed trials, authenticated coefficient compilation, closure, accesses and final source verification are charged. This is a paid terminal, not a universal contraction claim. For a supplied verified bounded-rank integer baseline feature map, the same proof works with vector counts when the number of coordinates is fixed and their summed absolute ranges are polynomial in original $N$; discovery of that more general map is not asserted.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Opposite-label all-direction family.}
For $d\ge3$ use the nonzero words of $\mathbb F_2^d$, $n=2^d-1$, and triples $\{x,y,x+y\}$. Every pair belongs to one triple. In scaled energy $4E$ for NAE violation count, each owner contributes one plus three signed pair products; the sign products on each triangle equal $+1$. The monotone chart has $J_{ij}=+1$ and $C=n(n-1)/6$, so its exact minimum is $C-(n-1)/2=(n-1)(n-3)/6>0$. For the SAT chart, partition words by highest nonzero bit. Every triple has two members in its highest-bit class and one in a lower class. Negate the minority-class literal of each owner; all-zero is a source witness. Its coefficients are $+1$ within each highest-bit class and $-1$ between classes, because every pair occurs once. The preceding lemma automatically recognizes baseline $-1$ and uniform residual cliques of sizes $1,2,\ldots,2^{d-1}$. The naive count-box product $\prod_{i=0}^{d-1}(2^i+1)$ is superpolynomial in the explicit source size (which is polynomial in $n$), while the aggregate-count DP remains polynomial. Both labels defeat every fixed BA21 magnitude cap for sufficiently large $d$, and BD21 small-fanout/dominance on the raw chart, yet both admit this nonlocal bypass. The raw owner-local affine closure is stagnant: each signed NAE has full affine hull and full pair projections. These are opposite-label same-scope controls, not single-sign neighbors, not high-girth or bounded-degree families, and not a simultaneous obstruction to all available terminals. In particular the complete-graph monotone cut bound also rejects the UNSAT family. This shows why universal progress cannot be deduced from a fixed magnitude cap alone, and why failed magnitude probes should feed global structural consumers rather than branch immediately.

\section{S27: Simultaneous all-cut field and all-direction magnitude obstruction}\label{sec:s27}
\begin{lemma}[Adjacent labels with uniformly high original-coordinate cut rank]\label{lem:s27-cut}
For all sufficiently large $n=2^k-1$, signed projective Steiner NAE charts exist with opposite labels differing by one literal sign modulo whole-owner complement, such that for every disjoint $A,B$ of size at least $n/4$ the pair-energy matrix has $\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}J_{BA}>\lfloor n/100\rfloor$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Each pair occurs once among the $m=n(n-1)/6$ triples. Independently sample each of four forbidden complementary classes uniformly, and independently sample a planted registry from the three classes accepting zero. The first is UNSAT except with probability at most $2^n(3/4)^m$, by first moment; the second is SAT. Replace owners by their planted versions in a fixed order. At any stage, a specified single crossing sign has probability at most $2/3$, and two specified crossing signs from one triple have probability at most $1/3\le(2/3)^2$, since two pair products determine its class. At most two edges per triple cross disjoint sets $A,B$. Independence across owners gives probability at most $(2/3)^{ab}$ for any specific $a$-by-$b$ cross matrix. The number of sign matrices of rank $j$ is at most $\binom aj\binom bj2^{j(a+b-j)}$: choose basis rows and pivot columns, whose entries determine all others. Put $r=\lfloor n/100\rfloor$. Union bounding ranks at most $r$, at most $3^n$ disjoint pairs, and $m+1$ stages gives
\[
(m+1)3^n(r+1)2^{n+rn}(2/3)^{n^2/16}=o(1).
\]
Here $\log_2(3/2)/16>1/100$. Thus there is a path with the high-rank property at every stage and opposite endpoint labels; a consecutive pair has opposite labels and differs by one forbidden class, hence one sign modulo whole-owner complement. Existence is not efficient discovery.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Actual field-key and baseline barrier]\label{lem:s27-keys}
At a cut of rational rank $h$ with a consistent affine guard of rank $g$, full DP22 field-key acquisition with affine feasibility and equal-key min merging retains at least $2^{h-g}$ distinct field keys. On the S27 pair, every original-coordinate order or binary leaf decomposition has a cut requiring $2^{\Omega(n)}$ such keys if at most $n/4$ coordinates are pinned and remaining guard rank is at most $n/200$. Further, if $J=L+D$ off-diagonal with $\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}L\le\lfloor n/100\rfloor$, the symmetric deviation graph of $D$ has no separator of size at most $n/4$ whose remaining components all have size at most $n/2$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
At least $2^{a-g}$ prefix words extend to a guard word. Every fiber of the real field map on Boolean words has at most $2^{a-h}$ members: fixing nonpivot input coordinates uniquely determines pivot values. Min merging preserves each attained key, hence the bound. A binary leaf tree has a node with between one third and two thirds of all free leaves (follow a largest child until below two thirds); orders have a midpoint. After the stated pins both sides contain at least $n/4$ original coordinates, so Lemma~\ref{lem:s27-cut} applies. For the baseline claim, take the union $A$ of separator components with size between $n/4$ and $n/2$ (one sufficiently large component or greedy accumulation of smaller ones). The remaining $B$ has size at least $n/4$. Then $D_{BA}=0$ contradicts the rank bound. In particular low-rank baseline deviations cannot universally have bounded treewidth, by the centroid-bag balanced-separator argument.
\end{proof}
RT27 already proves all nongauge directions on these raw charts exceed the fixed BA21 magnitude cap for large $n$, also excluding BD21 sparse/dominant and DS21 fixed-rank moves. Every raw NAE owner has full affine hull. Thus the same opposite-label family obstructs the union of these raw exact-representation strategies, including the DP22 full field tables and BH21 small-component baseline escape; it is not an unrestricted lower bound, not a proof about arbitrary affine recharts after nonlocal cuts, and not a counterexample to every alternative terminal. Explicit input length is $O(n^2\log n)$. Stronger MS28/DA21/DR21 deductions, zero-specific pruning, direct witnesses, nonforest geometry and implicit consumers remain legal. \section{BS21: Exact spectral bypass and planted recovery on high-rank Steiner charts}\label{sec:bs21}
We attack S27's simultaneous raw representation obstruction, not claim worst-case progress. The signed NAE energy $Q=C+\tfrac12 s^TJs$ on $d$ free spins has integer symmetric zero-diagonal $J$, and $C\ge0$ since it is the uniform mean of nonnegative energy. Actual pair-parity equations can be substituted by signed representative spins, adding collapsed pair terms to $C$. Coordinate pins and general affine guards are not covered by this field-free adapter. Conditional facts remain under their own guard.
\begin{lemma}[Exact spectral decision certificates]\label{lem:bs21-spec}
Let $R=\max_i\sum_j|(J^2)_{ij}|$. If $4C^2>d^2R$, or if $dJ+2CI$ is positive definite, the chart is UNSAT. A row-sign word of $J^2$ is a SAT certificate only after source and guard verification. These are deterministic polynomial procedures, allowed to decline.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The symmetric matrix has spectral norm bounded by $\sqrt R$, by the induced infinity norm bound for $J^2$. Since $\|s\|^2=d$, $Q\ge C-d\sqrt R/2$. Also $2dQ=s^T(dJ+2CI)s$, giving the strict definiteness certificate. Compute matrix products and row sums exactly; test positive definiteness by Sylvester's criterion using fraction-free Bareiss leading pivots (stop at the first nonpositive pivot). Integer intermediate minors have polynomial bit size by Hadamard's bound; all operations are charged. For witness tests try the all-positive word and each row sign, breaking zero ties deterministically; lift through actual pair-parity maps and verify all source constraints. The original input size bounds $d$, coefficient bits, matrix storage, all products, elimination and verification polynomially. Owner-local pair closure enumerates each ternary owner's eight words consistent with current signed representatives, inserts any necessary pair equation, and restarts; at most $n$ joins. Run before and after each accepted cut and at fixed-point stagnation, never treat complete semantic closure as free. Imported cuts require their own acquisition and verification charges. Same-realization $T,S$ are polynomial for this capped terminal and $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$. No universal successful certificate is asserted.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Two-sided high-probability escape on the S27 endpoint distributions]\label{lem:bs21-random}
For projective Steiner triples on $n=2^k-1$, let each owner independently choose a uniform forbidden complementary class, or choose uniformly among the three classes accepting a fixed hidden word $s^*$. In the first distribution the row-sum certificate of Lemma~\ref{lem:bs21-spec} succeeds with probability $1-o(1)$. In the second a row sign of $J^2$ recovers $s^*$ up to complement with probability $1-o(1)$. Both endpoints can simultaneously have S27's all-balanced-disjoint-cut rank obstruction and RT27's all-direction magnitude obstruction.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Every pair appears in exactly one triple, $C=m=n(n-1)/6$, $J_{ij}=\pm1$. For distinct $i,j$, $(J^2)_{ij}$ is the sum of $n-2$ pair products. Except for the unique third vertex in the triple containing $i,j$, the two signs in each product come from independent owners. In the exceptional term their product equals $J_{ij}$. For uniform classes all signs have mean zero, so the sum has mean zero. In the planted case switch by $s^*$; the signs have mean $-1/3$, and hence the switched sum has mean $(n-3)/9-1/3=(n-6)/9$. Switching conjugates $J$ and its square by the same diagonal signs. At most $n-2$ independent owner choices affect each sum; changing one affects at most two summands, by at most four in total. Bounded differences gives probability at most $2\exp(-t^2/(8n))$ for deviation at least $t$. Taking $t=\sqrt{40n\log n}$ and union bounding over pairs gives probability $1-O(n^{-3})$ that all deviations are at most $t$. In the uniform case diagonal entries are $n-1$, so $R\le(n-1)(1+t)$ and $n^2R<4m^2$ eventually. In the planted case $t<(n-6)/9$ eventually, hence every off-diagonal sign equals $s_i^*s_j^*$; the positive diagonal is consistent and one row recovers the hidden word up to global complement. S27's rank union bound applies to both distributions, so intersect the high-probability events; RT27's magnitude bound is deterministic. This does not prove that the opposite-label neighboring transition in S27 has either certificate. Indeed the actual $n=15$ S27 UNSAT neighbor declines below. The distribution-specific argument supplies no universal bound or hard-instance exclusion.
\end{proof}

\section{DO22: All-sign all-direction explicit Walsh obstruction}\label{sec:do22}
\begin{lemma}[Signed complete-pair absolute-value expansion]\label{lem:do22-walsh}
For $E(s)=C+\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}s_i s_j$, $J_{ij}\in\{-1,1\}$, every nongauge affine direction on the raw unguarded chart has an exact minimized energy with at least $2^{\gamma\sqrt n}-1-\binom n2$ nonzero Walsh coefficients, for an absolute $\gamma>0$ and all sufficiently large $n$. The bound holds for all signs, under invertible affine recharts, including after global-complement quotient.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Split the actual spin coordinates into $S,T$ with $1\le p=|S|\le q=|T|$. The odd term is $B=\sum_{j\in T}s_j w_j$, $w_j=\sum_{i\in S}J_{ij}s_i$. Under uniform independent $S$ spins, each $w_j$ has second moment $p$ and fourth moment at most $3p^2$. Cauchy--Schwarz gives $\Pr(w_j^2\ge p/2)\ge1/12$; Markov gives $\Pr(w_j^2>24p)\le1/24$. The expected number of middle magnitudes $\sqrt{p/2}\le |w_j|\le\sqrt{24p}$ is at least $q/24$. A Rademacher exponential moment bound and union bound give $\Pr(\max_j|w_j|>L)\le1/48$ for $L=\sqrt{2p\ln(96q)}$. Subtracting at most $q/48$ from the expected count shows that some $S$ assignment has all magnitudes at most $L$ and at least $q/48$ middle magnitudes. No independence between the $w_j$ is required. Pigeonhole positive integer magnitudes to get a group of $t\ge q/[48(\lfloor\sqrt{24p}\rfloor+1)]=\Omega(\sqrt n)$ equal absolute weights $w\ge\sqrt{p/2}$.
Absorb their signs into the corresponding $T$ spins. Fix other $T$ spins greedily opposing the accumulated weighted sum, leaving residual magnitude at most $L$. Choose the least integer $f\ge\max(1,\lceil L/w\rceil)$ with $f\equiv t-1\pmod2$; $f\le2\sqrt{\ln(96q)}+2$. For sufficiently large $n$, $l=t-f$ is odd and $\Omega(\sqrt n)$. Fix $f$ group spins so the resulting offset $c$ has $|c|\le w$, possible since shifts range from $-fw$ to $fw$ in steps of $2w$. Fixing all $S$ spins and at least one $T$ spin gives an injective affine slice of the direction and complement quotient. There $|B|=w|\sum_{i=1}^l z_i+c/w|$. Its even symmetrization under $z\mapsto-z$ equals $w|\sum_i z_i|$ because $l$ is odd and $|c/w|\le1$.
For odd $l\ge3$, every even Walsh coefficient of $|\sum z_i|$ is nonzero. The constant is positive; for a set of size $2j>0$ take the Walsh derivative in two of its variables. The resulting function is $\tfrac12\,1_{|\sum \text{remaining spins}|=1}$. On $l-2=2h+1$ remaining spins, the sum of all size-$2j-2$ characters on a word with $h$ negatives equals the coefficient of $u^{2j-2}$ in $(1-u)^h(1+u)^{h+1}$, namely $(-1)^{j-1}\binom h{j-1}\ne0$. Its complementary layer contributes the same, and permutation symmetry makes each coefficient at that degree equal. Thus the symmetrized restriction has $2^{l-1}$ nonzero coefficients. Restriction and symmetrization cannot increase Walsh support. The even energy term $A$ has at most $1+\binom n2$ coefficients, so $A-|B|$ cancels at most that many. Affine bijections preserve support cardinality.
\end{proof}
This strengthens RT27's unsigned expansion lemma to BOTH labels of the same S27 adjacent family, irrespective of direction discovery: input length $O(n^2\log n)$, every fixed explicit coefficient cap eventually fails in the raw chart, even if BA21 is generalized beyond fixed magnitude count. It does not exclude the compact $A-|B|$ expression, requiring only the original quadratic terms and one absolute-value gate; point evaluation and minimizing-bit lift are polynomial. A uniform bound for repeated exact compact minima and their zero-feasibility consumers is OPEN. No claim for arbitrary nonsurjective guards, prior cuts, adaptive nonlocal transformations or unrestricted computation. Explicit materialization requires one record per coefficient (streaming changes space, not output work).

\section{DA22: Guarded spectral feedback and moment obstruction}\label{sec:da22}
The BS21 tests can acquire new necessary equations without assuming a supplied global witness or an external guard oracle. All statements below are restricted to signed NAE and actual pair-parity guards.
\begin{lemma}[Exact spectral descent and feedback]\label{lem:da22-feedback}
For $Q=C+s^TJs/2$ equal to four times the violation count after an exact signed pair quotient, a candidate spin word $w$ defines $L=J-\operatorname{diag}(w_i(Jw)_i)$. If $Q(w)>0$ and one principal submatrix of $L$ deleting a single index is positive definite, the chart is UNSAT. Starting from the BS21 tests and row-sign candidates, polynomially many strictly improving single-spin flips and guarded pair probes give a deterministic exact declining procedure. In particular a certified rejection of one pair value implies its opposite under the current root guard; repeat owner-local closure after each such deduction. There are at most $O(n^3)$ probes in total.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
$Lw=0$ and $Q(s)-Q(w)=s^TLs/2$. For any real vector subtract a multiple of $w$ to zero the deleted index; the quadratic form is unchanged, proving PSD. Each strict flip lowers integer energy, initially at most $4m$, so bounded descent from $O(n)$ seeds is polynomial; all zero-energy source witnesses are verified. Test principal definiteness with exact Bareiss minors. In each probe quotient one pair value, run certified local closure and the spectral tests; retain only actual guarded rejection or verified witness. A rejected value allows an unconditional join relative to the current root, reducing the number of components. There are at most $n-1$ joins and $2\binom n2$ probes per round. Closure, all failed probes, integer matrix arithmetic (polynomial-bit minors), source compilation and reconstruction are polynomial in original input length. Same-execution $T,S$ polynomial, $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$. If no progress occurs, return OPEN, not UNSAT.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Strict degree-four moment obstruction]\label{lem:da22-moment}
Suppose an UNSAT signed NAE chart admits a normalized real degree-four Boolean-spin pseudoexpectation $\widetilde E$ positive on squares of degree at most two, with $\widetilde E[Q_ep]=0$ for each owner quadratic violation energy and every polynomial $p$ of degree at most two, and $|\widetilde E[s_is_j]|<1$ for all distinct pairs. Then the unguarded procedure of Lemma~\ref{lem:da22-feedback} stagnates without any first necessary pair cut.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For either proposed parity $\epsilon=\pm1$, put $h=(1+\epsilon s_is_j)/2$. Its expectation is positive. The conditioned matrix $X_{ab}=\widetilde E[h s_as_b]/\widetilde E[h]$ has unit diagonal and is PSD: modulo Boolean equations $h=((s_i+\epsilon s_j)/2)^2$, so positivity follows for $h\ell^2$ for every linear $\ell$. Its pair correlation on the probe is $\epsilon$, and every owner has zero expected energy. Equality of unit Gram vectors up to sign implements the pair quotient. For a signed NAE owner, if two signed literals coincide, zero expected violation forces the third opposite (the owner energy is $2+2s_as_c$); if two are opposite the owner is automatically satisfied. Thus local pair joins preserve the Gram representation and no local contradiction is possible. A positive spectral lower bound, positive definite certificate or PSD slack certificate with positive minimum would contradict the zero energy trace with a PSD correlation matrix. The same argument applies at the unguarded root. No true witness exists by hypothesis. Hence all probes fail to cut. Existence of strict degree-four pseudoexpectations on a suitable asymptotic NAE family is not asserted. Random regular basic SDP failure is not such an existence theorem; see \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.05230}{Deshpande et al.}
\end{proof}

\section{GD29: Weighted observation trellises and all-sign factorization rank}\label{sec:gd29}
\begin{lemma}[Guarded min-plus observation consumer]\label{lem:gd29-trellis}
For a consistent affine guard $Gx=b$, write $x=x_0+Qy$ by Gaussian elimination. A sum of bit-encoded integer costs $c+\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(a_i y)$ (including signed Walsh characters, with affine offsets absorbed in the cost functions) can be exactly minimized and lifted given an order of its terms in $2^{O(w)}\operatorname{poly}(N)$ time and space, where $w=\max_j\dim(P_j\cap R_j)$, $P_j=\operatorname{span}(a_1,\ldots,a_j)$ and $R_j=\operatorname{span}(a_{j+1},\ldots,a_m)$. Here the representation and coefficient bit lengths must be polynomial in original input length $N$. A binary term tree admits the analogous bound with its maximum cut intersection rank.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
At stage $j$ retain the minimum prefix cost and a realizing word per functional on $B_j=P_j\cap R_j$. If $a_{j+1}\in P_j$ it is in $B_j$ and its value is fixed; otherwise a homogeneous Gaussian solve finds a direction orthogonal to $P_j$ toggling it, so both choices extend a minimizing prefix. Since $B_{j+1}\subseteq B_j+\operatorname{span}(a_{j+1})$ (write an element as $p+\epsilon a_{j+1}$ and note $p\in R_j$), the next key depends only on the old key and selected bit. Equal keys have identical attainable continuations, by gluing linear functionals on $P_j,R_j$ as in GD28. Min merging is therefore exact; retain actual witnesses by toggling only directions preserving all prior observations. At the empty final interface the retained minimum is global. Lift via $Q$ and verify at the source. There are at most $2^{w+1}$ transitions per layer. The tree variant uses the GD28 child agreement rule, minimizing additive costs rather than Boolean flags, at most $2^{2w}$ pairs per node. Gaussian work, polynomial bit arithmetic, key access and reconstruction are charged. Greedy order trials can be paid polynomially before tables are acquired, but need not find a small width. An original-$N$ cap on width and representation gives a polynomial invocation that may decline, not a universal bound or aggregate repeated-invocation credit. On the same serial execution $CM\le(T+1)S$; no physical CM measurement is claimed.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Exact all-sign weighted min-plus separation rank]\label{lem:gd29-rank}
Fix labelled observations on a consistent affine guard, partition them $A,B$, and let $d_i>0$. Set
\[
M(p,q)=\min_{Gx=b}\left(\sum_{i\in A}d_i[a_i x\ne p_i]+\sum_{i\in B}d_i[a_i x\ne q_i]\right).
\]
Rows and columns range over all independent preferred-bit words. If $U,V$ are the respective spans restricted to $\ker G$ and $w=\dim(U\cap V)$, the least $k$ permitting $M(p,q)=\min_{t\le k}(u_t(p)+v_t(q))$ is exactly $2^w$, even allowing $+\infty$ costs in the separated functions.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Condition on the shared functional after subtracting the fixed affine offsets. The regional minima glue exactly, giving $2^w$ separated terms. Choose one global realization per shared functional and take its left/right observation words as row/column indices. Diagonal entries vanish; off-diagonal entries are positive since distinct functionals cannot glue and all weights are positive. Each separated summand dominates the matrix everywhere. A summand attaining zero at two diagonal cells would have crossed entries summing to zero, impossible as both crossed entries must dominate strictly positive values. Thus one term per diagonal cell is necessary. This is the positive-weight affine-guard extension of the linear-code unweighted result in Sheshadri, \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23471}{arXiv:2607.23471}, Theorem 1; the proof here specifies the exact scope.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[All raw complete-pair term orders and trees have linear interface rank]\label{lem:gd29-complete}
For a signed complete-pair Steiner NAE registry on $n$ coordinates, retain each of the $M=n(n-1)/2$ raw nonzero labelled pair-character observations. Every binary tree of these terms and every linear order has a cut of shared observation rank at least $(\sqrt{1+8M/3}-1)/2=\Omega(n)$. This is invariant under invertible affine recharts. After imposing a consistent rank-$g$ guard, the same labelled cut has rank at least the original rank minus $g$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
There is a cut with at least $M/3$ terms on both sides: follow a larger child until its size is at most $2M/3$, or use a midpoint in an order (for the asymptotic family $M\ge3$). The two edge graphs partition $K_n$; at least one is connected, since the complement of a disconnected graph contains all cross-component edges. Their binary incidence spans have ranks $r_A=n-c_A,r_B=n-c_B$, total $n-1$, so their shared rank is $\min(r_A,r_B)$. A graph of incidence rank $r$ has at most $r(r+1)/2$ edges: sum over components of sizes $s_i$ and use $\sum_i(s_i-1)=r$ and superadditivity of the triangular number. Both sides have at least $M/3$ edges, proving the bound. An invertible linear map preserves intersections and dimensions; an affine translation only changes signs. The guard quotient kills a subspace of dimension $g$, and the image of the old intersection is contained in the new intersection, with dimension at least the old rank minus $g$.
\end{proof}
This applies to both S27 raw adjacent labels, independently of S27's original-coordinate field rank and DO22's explicit Walsh quotient expansion. Full raw observation tables, and all-sign separated messages of Lemma~\ref{lem:gd29-rank}, thus have exponential size even under arbitrary invertible affine recharts or $g=o(n)$ when retaining labelled occurrences. This is NOT a lower bound on fixed-sign decision, on cancellations or nonlocal transformations changing the registry, on implicit nonseparable functions, or on correlated NAE-owner-sign-only messages. BH21 counting and BS21 spectral/witness escapes on particular complete-pair inputs remain legitimate. Classical trellis ordering results \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/0705.1384}{Kashyap} and tree realization results \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/0711.1383}{Kashyap} give context, not a universal discovery algorithm.

\section{Regular augmented syndrome acquisition and Fano obstruction (M28)}\label{sec:m28}
\begin{lemma}[Paid regular augmented syndrome terminal]\label{lem:m28-reg}
For binary $H$, target $t$, nonnegative integral binary-encoded weights $w$, minimum weight of $Hy=t$ is computable in deterministic polynomial bit time if the binary matroid of $[H\mid t]$ is regular. Regularity is polynomially recognizable. For loopless tagged perfect matching take $H$ to be stacked binary endpoint incidence and syndrome rows, $t=(\mathbf1,\text{target})$; minimum cardinality $|V|/2$ is equivalent to a perfect matching, with witness. Weight $1+\sum_e w_e+w_f$ on edge $f$ minimizes cardinality first, then original nonnegative weight.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Gaussian consistency first; zero target is trivial. Each binary feasible support together with distinguished column $*$ is a cycle, hence decomposes into disjoint circuits, one containing $*$. Nonnegative weights permit discarding others. Conversely such a circuit gives a feasible word. Recognize regularity and acquire a TU signing $B$ of a binary standard representation by Camion/Seymour (Walter--Truemper, \url{https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.4061}). Solve exact rational LP minimizing $\sum_e w_e(u_e+v_e)$ subject to $B_E(u-v)=-B_*$ and $0\le u,v\le1$. The signed duplicate-column matrix with bounds is TU, so exact LP and paid vertex acquisition give an integral optimum. Modulo two yields a binary word of cost no larger. A circuit through $*$ has a signed dependence with coefficients $\pm1$ by Cramer's rule on independent circuit-minus-star columns and TU minors; choose sign $+1$ at $*$. It gives the reverse bound. This transfers known regular matroid circuit optimization (Aprile--Fiorini, \url{https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.08539}, Prop.\ 19, Thm.\ 20). For matching, every vertex has odd degree, so equality in the cardinality bound forces every degree one. All verification, input conversion and reconstruction are charged; no rank enumeration, exact counting or arbitrary additional quota claim.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Target augmentation matters: explicit Fano minor]\label{lem:m28-fano}
For signed NAE, put preferred XOR $p_{ij}=1\oplus b_i\oplus b_j$ on each owner triangle with forbidden word $b$ and its complement. Total disagreement cost is $m+2\,\#\mathrm{violations}$. After certified pair parity quotient, loops and opposite parallel preferences contribute a constant; retain weighted remaining edges. Let $H$ be a cycle-basis matrix of that graph. Exact residual edge errors satisfy $Hy=Hp$, with polynomial witness lift. If a remaining $K_4$ has all triangle preference parities odd, the augmentation $[H\mid Hp]$ is nonregular, irrespective of invertible syndrome rechart.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Each owner contributes one or three disagreements. Binary cycle orthogonality characterizes the cut space, and forest propagation reconstructs spins. Contract all columns outside the six edges of the specified $K_4$, retaining the target. The dual of the quotient column space is exactly the cycle space supported on the $K_4$: the annihilator of the contracted span consists of cycle vectors zero elsewhere. The three triangles through one vertex give a basis; six edge columns are three units and their pair sums, target is $111$. This is the seven-point Fano matroid, nonregular; regularity is minor closed. Not a barrier for other encodings, nonlinear solvers or actual guard quotienting.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Guarded single-column minimum-cut feedback]\label{lem:m28-cut}
In that weighted graph, if a spanning forest consistency test accepts $p$, residual minimum is zero. If toggling one edge $e=uv$ makes $p$ consistent, gauge by that solution: all preferences are equality except $e$. Minimum residual cost is $\min(w_e,\operatorname{mincut}_{G-e}(u,v))$. The constant spin attains the first option; separating endpoints attains the second. Try every edge uniformly; decline when no candidate exists. A base cost greater than $m$ certifies UNSAT. After local owner closure, try both parity guards for every current component pair with reclosure. Verified SAT gives source witness; certified UNSAT guard implies the opposite unconditional parity, merging components and triggering immediate reclosure. At most $n-1$ such joins and $O(n^3)$ guard probes, each polynomial in original $N$, including failed gauge tests, flow/cut, guard verification and lifts. Capped procedure can decline; no semantic oracle, no universal progress.
\end{lemma}

\section{DR22: Explicit strict moments and a cooperative XOR escape}\label{sec:dr22}
\begin{lemma}[Strict degree-four moment obstruction is realizable]\label{lem:dr22-moment}
There are uniformly generated, arbitrarily large UNSAT signed NAE charts satisfying all hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:da22-moment}, with adjacent SAT controls obtained by deleting one owner or flipping one literal sign. The family has a separate polynomial exact XOR recognition and decision procedure; it is not hard for the full portfolio.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Put $D=16$, $m>2D+2$. Replace each vertex $i$ of $K_m$ by a cycle on $(i,j)$, $j\ne i$, in increasing order, with cross edges $(i,j)(j,i)$. This is a simple connected cubic graph on $v=m(m-1)$ vertices. Impose $\chi_{\delta(u)}(x)=b_u$ on edge spins, with precisely one negative charge, where $\chi_S=\prod_{e\in S}x_e$. Multiplying all constraints gives contradiction. Any cut of at most $D$ edges splits at most $D/2$ cycles. If $a,b$ whole cycles lie on opposite sides, $ab\le D$ and $a+b\ge m-D/2$; if both positive, $ab\ge a+b-1>D$. One shore therefore has size at most $(D/2)(m-1)<v/4$. For $|S|\le D$ define $E[\chi_S]=0$ off the cut space, otherwise the product of charges on the unique small shore. In the moment matrix indexed by sets of size at most $D/2$, entries across cut-space cosets vanish. Within a coset choose representative $A_0$; the symmetric difference of the small shores for $A\triangle A_0,B\triangle A_0$ has size $<v/2$ and is the small shore for $A\triangle B$. Hence each block is the outer product of its signs relative to $A_0$, proving PSD. Toggling a vertex star toggles its small shore by that vertex whenever both monomials have degree at most $D$; thus $E[\chi_S\chi_{\delta(u)}]=b_u E[\chi_S]$.

Deleting at most two vertices leaves the graph connected: intact cycles join by all cross edges, and each surviving portion of a damaged cycle reaches an intact cycle. Consequently cuts supported on the union of at most two stars arise exactly from subsets of those vertices. On these scopes $E$ is the uniform local distribution satisfying their parity equations, by equality of Fourier coefficients.

In bits, each vertex parity forbids four patterns $f$. For each, let $(a,b,c)=x_{\delta(u)}\oplus f$ and introduce private $t$ with $\operatorname{NAE}(a,b,t)$ and $\operatorname{NAE}(1\oplus t,c,0)$. Existence of $t$ is exactly the clause $a\vee b\vee c$. On legal parity words choose $t=(1-a)(1-b)$, one on exactly one of the four legal words. The four private variables at a vertex select distinct such words. Replace zero by a global gauge bit and XOR all bits by that gauge; this preserves NAE and allows exact source recovery. In spin coordinates the substitution has degree at most three. Average over an independent unbiased gauge and pull back moments of target degree at most four through this substitution. Positivity follows from the source moment PSD. Each owner violation polynomial $Q_e$ vanishes on the legal vertex words, so its pullback equals itself times $(1-b_u\chi_{\delta(u)})/2$ in the Boolean ring. The pullback of $Q_ep$ for target $\deg p\le2$ has degree at most 12, and multiplication by the star adds at most three, within $D$. The moment parity identity therefore gives zero.

For strict pair moments the gauge cancels. Source bits are balanced and distinct pairs independent (no one- or two-edge cut on the two-star scopes). Each private bit has marginal $1/4$, which rules out deterministic equality or opposition with a source bit. Two private bits of one star have disjoint exceptional events. Private bits on disjoint stars are independent; adjacent stars conditionally factor given their shared edge, with each exceptional event of conditional probability zero or $1/2$. Such events cannot coincide almost surely and marginal $1/4$ excludes perfect opposition. Gauge/other-bit parity is also nonconstant. Thus every distinct pair has strict correlation. The DA22 rejection dispatch has no first pair cut despite UNSAT; local singleton closure stalls since each NAE owner has full affine hull. This does not exclude nonlocal closure.

The all-zero ungauged edge word violates only the negative vertex, and the displayed private choice violates precisely one second NAE owner. Deleting that owner or flipping its $c$ sign gives a verified SAT word. The deletion also retains the original pseudoexpectation. To escape, identify a candidate gauge and degree-two private variables, verify paired owners and four forbidden patterns of identical parity per recovered ordered triple, and check full coverage. Recovered XOR rows decide by Gaussian elimination, with witness lift; for this family odd charge directly gives contradiction. Trying every gauge and checking the actual signed registry costs polynomially in original encoding length. No strict physical tetravalent adapter is asserted.
\end{proof}
\paragraph{Scope and evidence.} This fills DA22's strict-moment existence gap but not U-PROGRESS. Exact local truth tables, 6105 all-pair marginal checks at $m=5$ (local control only), 2048 seeded checks at $m=40$ (8581 target bits, 12480 owners), exact owner-list XOR decoding and both adjacent SAT lifts passed 17809 assertions. Full SDP, portfolio, S27 raw replay, kernel and measured CM not executed. Same serial recognition/verification/solving has polynomial $T,S$, $CM\le(T+1)S$; all failed gauge guesses and lifts paid. \href{https://github.com/j15marti/pnp/commit/192e4306c6932616a63a9fb8355f9245131e4b68}{Report}, \href{https://github.com/j15marti/pnp/commit/f11016daf7d0f8cdc9230559dd6bf49acc61f550}{checker}, \href{https://github.com/j15marti/pnp/commit/89b19a936d1aa0f74972e3d2df9df6959c582235}{results}. S27/RT26 remain separate. Reclose after certified deductions. No unrestricted hardness or public proof.


\section{BW22: Exact mixed parity-island contraction}\label{sec:bw22}
\begin{lemma}[Projection without boundary enumeration]\label{lem:bw22-island}
In a mixed Boolean factor registry let $I$ be an authenticated set of parity rows. Let $B$ contain every coordinate used outside $I$ or in a retained guard. Suppose each hidden coordinate occurring in $I$ has one or two incidences in distinct rows. The existential projection of $I$ to $B$ consists exactly of one parity check per connected component of the graph of rows joined by hidden degree-two coordinates, except that a component with a hidden degree-one coordinate contributes no check. The retained check is the sum of its rows, including the right-hand sides. It is discoverable with polynomial bit work and a forest reconstruction map, independently of boundary rank.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For a prescribed boundary word, subtract its contribution from every charge. Necessity for a component without a free half-edge follows by summing the rows: each hidden edge appears twice. For sufficiency select a spanning tree in each component, put every other hidden edge to zero, and solve the tree edges leaf-to-root. The final charge is precisely the component sum. When a free half-edge exists, root the tree at an incident row and use that half-edge to absorb the final charge; other free half-edges can be zero. This proves both directions for each fixed boundary word, including actual guards supported there. Hidden coordinates absent from the registry are freely reconstructed. No enumeration of a boundary relation is needed.
\end{proof}
If every observed coordinate occurs in at most one affine row, the resulting nonempty parity supports are disjoint. By BW21 they have linear-size pure B4 pinned boundary realizations, using a $K_4$ parity gate, accounted fixed ports and signed wires. No guard on an eliminated private variable can be discarded. \section{I28: Two-component occupancy--syndrome quotient}\label{sec:i28}
\begin{lemma}[Exact parity-island matching consumer]\label{lem:i28-two}
In the mixed explicit registry of Lemma~\ref{lem:bw22-island}, suppose after guarded closure the remaining table scopes are disjoint and each exposed coordinate belongs to one table and at most one retained component check. Direct table--table wires may first be split by a fresh binary equality check. For each table $T$ and retained component $C$ define $y_{TC}$ to be the XOR of its actual ports incident to $C$. If each table meets at most two retained components, decision and witness reconstruction are deterministic polynomial time in the original explicit registry length, regardless of total boundary width.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Project each explicit table by the displayed map, retaining one original row per image. The remaining intertable constraints are exactly $\bigoplus_T y_{TC}=b_C$; BW22 gives both directions and a forest lift. Free local coordinates do not require a check. For a nonempty projected relation $R$ on $d\le2$ bits, append the private parity bit $p=\operatorname{par}(y)$ and translate by an actual even-word anchor. The resulting support consists of zero and a subset of the weight-two words on $d+1\le3$ ports. Create a vertex for each port and an internal edge for each allowed pair. Internal matching occupancy denotes one; external occupancy denotes zero. For a component check of degree $D$ use a clique on its ports, translated by an anchor of the required parity. Connect each pair of corresponding ports by a direct edge when anchor bits agree, and otherwise by a two-edge path with a private midpoint. Add one external edge from each parity-pad port to a private reservoir vertex, and a clique on those reservoir vertices, with one extra vertex if needed to make the entire graph order even. On any feasible quotient word all local even occupied subsets can be paired, all wire midpoints are covered, and the remaining reservoir vertices are even in number since all other vertices are matched. Conversely every perfect matching decodes legal local and transported words. Empty tables and odd empty checks reject. The graph has $O(L)$ vertices and $O(L^2)$ edges in explicit size $L$; ordinary deterministic matching (Edmonds, \url{https://doi.org/10.4153/cjm-1965-045-4}) supplies a decision and witness. Verify decoded original rows, forest lifts and the guard. No full boundary enumeration is needed.
\end{proof}
Actual table-row support can be checked by singleton row restriction, preserving the same component map and the footprint bound. Repeat certified closure after each infeasible-row deletion under its own guard; monotone row count gives polynomial aggregate probes, including failed probes and reverse maps. Hidden-coordinate pinning can split islands and is not automatically supported; complete semantic closure is not assumed. All discovery, graph construction, reconstruction and verification are charged. This domain has polynomial same-execution $T,S$ and $CM\le(T+1)S$. No universal availability is asserted.

\begin{lemma}[Footprint-three boundary]\label{lem:i28-three}
With arbitrary explicit local tables, footprint at most three is already NP-complete: compile 3-CNF clauses into ternary tables and variable fanout into trees of arity-three equality tables with binary equality parity rows on the wires. Fresh port identities give exactly one table incidence and one parity incidence per port. The representation is polynomial and exact. This is a decision reduction before further affine restructuring, not a bound on alternative algorithms.
\end{lemma}
For a local matching gadget with a single external edge per port, any two feasible internal occupancy words satisfy even symmetric exchange: the symmetric difference of their internal matchings contains an alternating path from each differing port to another differing port, and toggling it gives the corresponding two-bit change. On the actual BW22 imperfect ternary supports $\{0,1,2,4,7\}$ and $\{0,1,2,7\}$ the parity-pad supports (little-endian pad bit 3) are $\{0,9,10,12,15\}$ and $\{0,9,10,15\}$. They fail exchange respectively from 15 toward 0 at coordinate 3 and from 0 toward 15 at coordinate 2. Thus blind local parity-padding is not a universal matching compiler. BW22's actual component map merges the three ports into one parity contribution and escapes this obstruction. The related even-delta-matroid edge CSP result (arXiv:1602.03124) assumes explicit local relations; no free wide-table consumer is imported.

\section{BD22: Affine-table cancellation and simultaneous syndrome coordinates}\label{sec:bd22}
The actual BW22/I28 parity-island consumer can be generalized by changing the syndrome basis rather than enumerating exterior assignments. For explicit finite tables $R_i\subseteq\mathbb F_2^h$ and actual target $t$, seek $\bigoplus_i r_i=t$, $r_i\in R_i$. Include all actual guard equations in the syndrome and retain row representatives. For stacked observation matrix $A$ and actual guard $Hx=g$, quotient the observation-plus-guard coordinate space by the image of $[A;H]$, map each allowed owner word by zero extension and quotient, and take target the image of $(0,g)$. The resulting XOR condition holds exactly when the selected words and guard lift to the original variables by Gaussian elimination. This is polynomial in explicit input length; no semantic support oracle.
\begin{lemma}[Exact affine-table cancellation and paid closure]\label{lem:bd22-affine}
For each nonempty $R_i$ choose $a_i\in R_i$ and put $U_i=\operatorname{span}(R_i+a_i)$. A row $r$ may be deleted if $t+r+\sum_{j\ne i}a_j\notin\sum_{j\ne i}U_j$. Empty lists or failure of $t+\sum_i a_i\in\sum_i U_i$ reject. If $J$ is the set of affine tables $R_i=a_i+U_i$, put $W=\sum_{i\in J}U_i$, $a=\sum_{i\in J}a_i$. Cancel them by quotienting all other rows and $t+a$ by $W$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The row test relaxes all other tables to their affine hulls, so no genuine witness is lost. The XOR sum of the affine tables is exactly $a+W$, proving both directions of cancellation. Retain a preimage per quotient row and a basis of $W$ with decompositions into the eliminated spaces. Gaussian reconstruction supplies actual eliminated table rows; verify the actual guard and source. Detect affine tables by deduplicated cardinality $2^{\dim U_i}$. Repeat the certified row closure after every deduction and cancellation and at stagnation; strict row deletion or table removal bounds the number of rounds polynomially in original explicit length. Complete semantic closure is not assumed.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Common syndrome coordinate criterion]\label{lem:bd22-basis}
Suppose all surviving difference spaces have dimension at most two. Deduplicate nonzero spaces. Let $D$ contain all generators of the one-dimensional spaces and all nonzero vectors belonging to at least two distinct two-dimensional spaces. A simultaneous independent coordinate basis exists for all these spaces if and only if every two-plane $P$ has $|D\cap P|\le2$ and
\[
 |D|+\sum_{\text{distinct two-planes }P}(2-|D\cap P|)=\dim\sum_i U_i.
\]
On success, the chart has a deterministic polynomial decision and witness lift via I28, without any bound on its original component footprint.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Intersections of coordinate spaces are coordinate spaces, so all $D$ vectors are mandatory. Complete each plane with private vectors to a basis, choosing deterministically among its three nonzero vectors. A private vector is in no other plane or prescribed line, hence the cardinality of the union is exactly the displayed left side. This union spans the total space, and equality with rank makes it independent. The necessity follows from counting the distinct basis vectors needed in the same way. Translate every row by its anchor, check target membership, then express all differences and the translated target in this basis. Each table now touches at most two independent syndrome checks; apply Lemma~\ref{lem:i28-two}, including parity padding and actual row reconstruction. Gaussian operations, explicit matching graph, deterministic general matching, all accesses and lifts are polynomial in the original explicit length. This is the dual syndrome analogue of BD15's observation-coordinate recognition, not an assumed change of source variables.
\end{proof}
An exact alternating implementation has a polynomial serial reserve on eligible charts, including unsuccessful recognition, provenance, guards and reconstruction; same-execution $CM\le(T+1)S$. The local reserve does not pay an unbounded number of fallback occurrences. The finite control $R_i=\{0,1,2\},\{0,1,4\},\{0,2,4\},\{0,3,5\},\{0,4\}$ (binary integer notation), target zero, fails raw common basis but succeeds after affine cancellation by $\operatorname{span}(4)$.
\begin{lemma}[Rank-two syndrome compatibility remains NP-complete]\label{lem:bd22-hard}
General explicit syndrome compatibility with rank-two three-word tables is NP-complete even at a fixed point of the affine-hull row closure in Lemma~\ref{lem:bd22-affine}.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Compile signed NAE-3-SAT on distinct-variable triples into three allowed words on the two difference observations $(x_u+x_v,x_u+x_w)$. Duplicate each owner if needed, and apply the stacked-image quotient above with no guard. Any nonzero vector supported on just one duplicated owner's two observation positions is not in the stacked image, since its duplicate would have identical observations. Thus each projected local list has three distinct words and difference rank two. Each local word lifts to some source assignment on its triple without imposing the other NAE constraints, and all other affine hulls allow all four difference words; this witnesses every hull row test, even after projection. Hence closure is stagnant and no table is affine. Both directions of exact syndrome compatibility follow by the stacked-image identity, and the reduction is polynomial. Membership in NP is immediate. This is not a lower bound on unrestricted decision; source duplicate elimination and other nonlinear transformations are permitted.
\end{proof}

\section{BA22: Punctured-affine syndrome fusion and a distinct-owner obstruction}\label{sec:ba22}
Use the actual target and guard-inclusive stacked-image quotient of Section~\ref{sec:bd22}. A summand is an affine coset $p+U$ or a punctured coset $(p+U)\setminus\{p\}$, recorded by a basis and a hole flag. Normalize empty and singleton cases. No explicit exponential table is required.
\begin{lemma}[Exact nonaffine fusion and reverse lift]\label{lem:ba22-fuse}
Let two such summands have direction spaces $U,V$, with $I=U\cap V$ and offsets $p,q$. If both are punctured and $\dim I\ge2$, their sum is the entire coset $p+q+U+V$. If both are punctured and $I=\{0,w\}$ with $w\ne0$, their sum is exactly $(p+q+U+V)\setminus\{p+q+w\}$. If just one is punctured and $\dim I\ge1$, or neither is punctured, the sum is full. A witness for any surviving output has a polynomial-time reverse lift.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Every word of the full sum coset has $2^{\dim I}$ affine decompositions, parameterized by the intersection. Each hole eliminates at most one. When $I=\{0,w\}$, both exclusions occur in a common fiber precisely for outputs in $p+q+I$, and they coincide at $p+q$ but are distinct at $p+q+w$. This proves all identities. Compute an affine decomposition by Gaussian elimination; test it and, when available, two independent intersection translates. Three distinct candidates suffice against two exclusions; in dimension at most one test the at most two decompositions. Store both actual child descriptions, including prior restrictions, and the original row representatives. Recursive reverse lift traverses the merge tree once, then the stacked-image Gaussian solve reconstructs and verifies an original word with its guard. The claim is existential, not multiplicity preserving.
\end{proof}
Intersect a summand with the necessary coset $t+\sum_{j\ne i}\operatorname{aff}(R_j)$ before fusion, after every deduction, and at stagnation. The intersection is affine minus at most one point, so this certified hull closure stays within the representation. Normalize a punctured line to its remaining singleton; empty sets reject. Every strict restriction decreases hull dimension. Every successful pair fusion decreases table count without increasing total hull dimension. Thus $\mu=1+\#\text{tables}+\sum_i\dim\operatorname{aff}(R_i)$ decreases by at least one on every strict step, with no branching. Scan all pairs deterministically and use Gaussian intersection, sum, membership and exact hole transport. Initial explicit table recognition by cardinality and exact membership is polynomial (the hull is at most one point larger than the input table in the punctured case); thereafter maintain implicit descriptors. Dimensions are bounded by the original explicit syndrome size, number of fusions by original table count, and all scans, failed probes, archive, source map and reverse lifts are polynomial in original input length. If remaining spans are independent, the unique component decomposition decides exactly by membership. Otherwise a declined chart remains open; fallback costs still need Theorem~\ref{thm:aggregate}. For example $k$ punctured planes $\operatorname{span}(e_i,e_{i+1})\setminus\{0\}$ fuse sequentially into one rank-$(k+1)$ coset missing $\sum_{i=2}^{k}e_i$. It represents $2^{k+1}-1$ words without enumerating them.
\begin{lemma}[Distinct-owner pair-fusion fixed-point hardness]\label{lem:ba22-hard}
NP-completeness persists on linear monotone NAE3SAT registries whose unguarded stacked-image quotient has distinct rank-two punctured tables with pairwise trivially intersecting direction spaces and stagnant hull closure.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Start with linear monotone NAE3SAT (NP-complete even with each variable occurring four times, Darmann and D\"ocker, \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.04198}{arXiv:1908.04198}). For $n\ge3$ source variables $x_i$, add fresh classes $a_j,b_j$ indexed modulo $n$, and all $n^2$ positive triples $(x_i,a_j,b_{i+j})$. The Latin-square indices ensure linearity, no duplicate owners, and intersection at most one with original triples. Every source word extends by $a_j=0,b_j=1$; restriction gives the converse. Remove any two owners: the $x$--$a$ primal subgraph is $K_{n,n}$ minus at most two edges and remains connected; each $b_j$ still touches it. Hence a source word whose stacked two-difference observations vanish off at most two owners is globally constant and has all observations zero. In the quotient by the image of the stacked source map, the coordinate plane of each owner is injected and the images of distinct planes intersect trivially, since any image vector supported on at most two owner blocks must vanish. Every local allowed word survives affine-hull row closure, witnessed by a source word realizing its observation while all other owners are relaxed to their full two-dimensional hulls. No table is affine, no positive-intersection pair fusion applies and their total spans are not a direct sum (the image has dimension $3n-1>0$). The reduction and verification are polynomial, establishing the claimed NP-complete restricted domain.
\end{proof}
This strengthens BD22's duplicate-owner obstruction to distinct linear owners; it does not preserve degree four, and the padding has a cheap exposed semantic removal. It excludes neither that removal nor higher-order nonlinear cuts, matching, alternate representations or unrestricted polynomial decision.

\section{DS22: Arbitrary-rank adapted bases and punctured syndrome fusion}\label{sec:ds22}
\begin{lemma}[Polynomial common adapted basis recognition]\label{lem:ds22-basis}
For any finite family of explicitly based binary subspaces $U_i$, one can find a basis of $A=\sum_iU_i$ containing a basis of every $U_i$, or correctly reject its existence, in deterministic polynomial time.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Initialize $B=\varnothing$. Until $B$ spans $A$, start $W=A$ and scan all $U_i$ in a fixed order. Replace $W$ by $W\cap U_i$ if this intersection is not contained in $\operatorname{span}B$. Choose a basis vector $v$ of the final $W$ outside $\operatorname{span}B$ and append it to $B$. At the end verify $|B\cap U_i|=\dim U_i$ for each $i$. If any adapted basis exists, inductively maintain one $C$ containing the selected $B$. Write $v$ in $C$. Every basis vector with a nonzero coefficient lies in every $U_i$ containing $v$, since $C$ is adapted. At least one such vector $c$ is outside $B$. No rejected $U_i$ can contain a vector in final $W$ outside $\operatorname{span}B$, and $c$ belongs to final $W$ since it lies in all accepted subspaces. Hence $c$ has exactly the same subspace membership pattern as $v$. Exchange $c$ for $v$ in $C$; this preserves independence and each adapted subspace basis. Induct. The final test therefore succeeds whenever any adapted basis exists. There are at most $\dim A$ passes, each with at most $m$ Gaussian intersections and containment tests, all polynomial in the explicit basis length. No enumeration of the intersection lattice is required.
\end{proof}
The concurrently appended BA22 section (Lemma~\ref{lem:ba22-fuse}) independently establishes the same fusion identity and a stronger distinct-owner fixed-point obstruction (Lemma~\ref{lem:ba22-hard}); DS22's fusion and duplicate-based reduction are independent corroboration, not a stronger result. The substantive DS22 extensions are arbitrary-rank adapted-basis recognition and the compressed high-rank matching consumer. This extends BD22's rank-two recognition to arbitrary rank. Related adapted-basis Helly theory is described in Jafari and Kaveh, \url{https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36566}; the above exchange argument is self-contained, and novelty relative to the literature is not asserted.

\begin{lemma}[Exact compressed syndrome fusion]\label{lem:ds22-fusion}
In the actual BD22 syndrome space with target $t$, represent a table by an affine space $a+U$, optionally with one missing point $p\in a+U$. Normalize an empty table to rejection and a rank-one punctured table to its actual singleton. For two such nonempty tables $P,Q$ with spaces $U,V$ and $W=U\cap V$ nonzero, their exact XOR sum is $a+b+(U+V)$ except when both are punctured and $\dim W=1$, in which case exactly $p+q+w$ is missing, where $w$ is the unique nonzero vector in $W$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For any target $s$ in the affine sum, its decompositions are a Gaussian-computable coset of $W$, parametrized by adding the same vector to both summands. Each puncture excludes at most one decomposition. If $\dim W\ge2$, or if at most one puncture exists and $\dim W\ge1$, some decomposition survives. In the remaining case the two exclusions are distinct and both present exactly when $s\in p+q+W$ and $s\ne p+q$. This is the asserted missing point. Reconstruct by trying both fiber members if $\dim W=1$, or any three distinct members otherwise. No explicit expansion is needed.
\end{proof}
Before, after every strict deduction, and at stagnation, intersect each actual table with the necessary affine space $t+\sum_{j\ne i}a_j+\sum_{j\ne i}U_j$. This retains exactly the original table intersected with that affine space: discard a hole outside the intersection and retain a hole inside it, then normalize. Empty intersection rejects. This is a sound affine relaxation of other tables, not complete semantic closure. Recompute after each accepted restriction or fusion. The integer potential $1+\#\mathrm{tables}+\sum_i\dim U_i$ decreases with each strict restriction (rank drops) or fusion (rank drops by $\dim W$, table count by one). All state lengths, discovery scans, failed attempts, Gaussian maps, reverse fiber reconstruction, and source and guard verification are polynomial in original explicit length; no branching. If remaining spaces form a direct sum, a Gaussian solve and actual hole checks decide and reconstruct. Otherwise this dispatch can decline.

\begin{lemma}[Compressed high-rank coordinate matching]\label{lem:ds22-match}
If the spaces of the preceding compressed tables admit a common adapted basis, their exact target compatibility is polynomial-time decidable and reconstructible even at arbitrary local rank.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Acquire a basis by Lemma~\ref{lem:ds22-basis}. Translate each affine table by its anchor and each punctured table by its hole, translating the target by their XOR. A local word on $d$ coordinates is now arbitrary or arbitrary nonzero, respectively. Append one private parity pad so the internally occupied ports form an even subset of $d+1$ ports. For an affine table use a clique on these ports. For a punctured table add two compulsory internal vertices with no edge between them, each adjacent to all ports. An internal matching covering both private vertices and exactly the occupied ports exists iff the occupied set is even and nonempty: match the two internal vertices to any two occupied ports and pair the rest. Nonempty even occupancy implies a nonzero actual word since there is only one pad. For each basis coordinate use the I28 component-check clique with an extra vertex for odd required parity. A single external edge joins corresponding local and check ports; internal occupancy therefore agrees on both sides. Connect each pad port to its private reservoir vertex, make the reservoirs a clique, and add a spare vertex if needed for even total graph order. Any valid local and check choices cover all nonreservoir vertices and leave an even number of reservoirs for internal pairing. Conversely a perfect matching decodes the exact local words and target. Polynomial graph size in the explicit basis incidence length, deterministic general matching, Gaussian source lift and actual verification suffice.
\end{proof}
The matching consumer is a proved symbolic extension of I28, not an executed backend in this run. It does not cover arbitrary high-rank nonaffine tables. Fusing first reduces the pairwise-disjoint adapted case to a direct sum.

\begin{lemma}[Restricted obstruction to universal fusion]\label{lem:ds22-hard}
Deciding rank-two punctured syndrome tables with pairwise-disjoint difference spaces and stagnant necessary affine-hull closure is NP-complete.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Triplicate each signed NAE owner in BD22's stacked-image quotient. A nonzero word supported on at most two of the copy slots cannot belong to the stacked observation image, since the third identical copy forces that owner's observation to vanish (and likewise for distinct owners). Thus each local two-space is injectively projected and any pair intersects trivially. Each local allowed word is realized by some source assignment when every other owner is relaxed to its full affine hull, so none is removed by closure. Exact target compatibility is equivalent to the source NAE instance and the reduction is polynomial; membership in NP is immediate. This is only a representation-specific failure: ordinary duplicate removal can undo the manufactured redundancy. No unrestricted lower bound follows.
\end{proof}

\section{MS29: Multiway kernel-fiber syndrome fusion}\label{sec:ms29}
Attack Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} on the same BD22/BW22/I28 and S27 syndrome charts as BA22/DS22. The latest peer bottleneck is collective dependence of pairwise-disjoint difference spaces. The following result extends pair fusion, not arbitrary nonlinear support acquisition.
\begin{lemma}[Density-certified multiway fusion and polynomial reverse lift]\label{lem:ms29-density}
Let $T_i=a_i+U_i$ be explicit binary affine tables, each optionally missing one point $h_i$ of its affine space. Normalize empty and rank-one punctured tables. For the summation map $A:\bigoplus_i U_i\to\sum_i U_i$, let $K=\ker A$ and $r_i=\dim\pi_i K$. If
\[
 \rho=\sum_{i:\,h_i\ {\rm exists}}2^{-r_i}<1,
\]
then the exact XOR sum of the actual tables is the full affine sum $\sum_i a_i+\sum_i U_i$. Both recognition of this sufficient condition and reverse lifting of any target in the sum have deterministic polynomial bit complexity in explicit total basis size.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For a target in the affine sum, Gaussian elimination gives a particular decomposition and a kernel basis. Uniformly select a point in its kernel coset. The event that coordinate $i$ equals its hole is either impossible or has probability $2^{-r_i}$, because all fibers of a linear projection have equal size. The expected number of violated tables is at most $\rho<1$. For deterministic reconstruction, fix successive coefficients of the kernel basis to minimize the conditional expected number of violations. With $d$ coefficients still free, an individual hole event is empty or has exactly $2^{d-r}$ completions, where $r$ is the rank of its projected remaining kernel columns; membership and rank are Gaussian computations. The two candidate expectations average to the old expectation, and are compared by exact integer counts of polynomial bit length. When all coefficients are fixed, the integer number of violations is less than one, hence zero. This proves the support identity and paid lift without enumerating the support. The method of conditional probabilities is standard; novelty relative to general finite subspace covering theory is not asserted.
\end{proof}
For pairwise-disjoint rank-two spaces $U,V,W$ with $W$ the graph of an isomorphism from $U$ to $V$, all three kernel projections have rank two, hence $\rho=3/4$ even when all tables have holes. BA22 pair fusion and a DS22 common adapted basis both decline, but the exact multiway sum is full rank four. Disjoint copies give arbitrarily large examples.
\paragraph{Charged integration.}
Use BA22/DS22 necessary target-conditioned affine-hull restriction before, after each accepted deduction and at stagnation; try pair fusion, then the entire family and every triple for Lemma~\ref{lem:ms29-density}. Each strict restriction decreases rank, and fusing $k\ge2$ tables reduces table count plus rank sum by at least $k-1$. Each sweep has polynomially many tests (at most cubic in table count), and the original sum of ranks plus table count bounds strict changes. The admitted fixed-chart implementation charges all Gaussian acquisitions, failed tests, guards, old and new representation sizes, lift trees, conditional-expectation bit decisions, and source verification. Serial polynomial $T,S$ imply $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$ on the same realization. No reserve reset, arbitrary subgroup search oracle, free semantic closure or global aggregate guarantee. This does not by itself give a physical matching defect decrease or a uniform compiler for all strict physical states.
\begin{lemma}[All-subgroup density obstruction on distinct-owner padding]\label{lem:ms29-hard}
BA22's Latin-square padding, for $n\ge4$, excludes every density-certified fusion subgroup in the raw rank-two punctured stacked-image quotient, even if subgroup discovery is unrestricted. Necessary affine-hull closure and pair fusion also stagnate there.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Take $n$ source coordinates $x_i$, fresh $a_j,b_j$, and all $n^2$ positive NAE triples $(x_i,a_j,b_{i+j\bmod n})$. Extension by $a_j=0,b_j=1$ preserves source satisfiability, and the original source is recovered by restriction. After deleting at most three owners the $x$--$a$ graph contains $K_{n,n}$ minus at most three edges and remains connected, while every $b_j$ has a remaining incident padding triple. If the stacked two-difference observations of a source word vanish outside at most three owner blocks, all source coordinates must be equal; thus the whole observation word vanishes. Every union of at most three coordinate planes is injected into the quotient by the observation image, so each such family has zero summation kernel. Each rank-two local table has one hole and every allowed word survives necessary hull restriction, witnessed by a source word satisfying its observations with all other tables relaxed to their full hulls. Subgroups of size at most three therefore have $\rho\ge1$ (indeed each puncture contributes one); groups of at least four also have $\rho\ge1$ since each $r_i\le2$. Pair fusion is impossible and the whole family is not a direct sum. Distinct-owner linearity is preserved when the original source is linear. This is a restricted representation barrier with an exposed cheap padding-removal operation; it does not preserve strict degree four and does not exclude other inference, preprocessing or unrestricted polynomial decision.
\end{proof}
