\section{BH22: Forest-corrected hole avoidance and high-girth moment obstruction}\label{sec:bh22}
Attack Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} by strengthening MS29's collective density test, retaining exact target guards and avoiding a semantic oracle.
\begin{lemma}[Forest-corrected conditional expectation]\label{lem:bh22-forest}
On a consistent explicitly encoded affine guard $G$, let $E_i$ be affine forbidden packets and $T$ any forest on their identities. If
\[
 B=\sum_i\Pr(E_i\mid G)-\sum_{ij\in T}\Pr(E_i\cap E_j\mid G)<1,
\]
then a satisfying word of the chart can be constructed in deterministic polynomial bit time.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The integer $f(x)=\sum_i1_{E_i}(x)-\sum_{ij\in T}1_{E_i\cap E_j}(x)$ equals the number of components in the subforest induced by violated owners, zero exactly for a legal word. Gaussian consistency and rank compute every marginal and pair intersection probability exactly. A maximum-weight spanning tree (Hunter's classical upper bound, \href{https://doi.org/10.2307/3212481}{1976}) maximizes the correction and is polynomially discoverable. Fix the tree and successively choose a nonempty coordinate side with smaller conditional expected $f$; the parent expectation is the weighted average of those sides. When every coordinate is fixed, $f$ is a nonnegative integer below one, so zero. Each conditional count is a power of two or zero by Gaussian elimination, with polynomial bit length; all selected words and actual guards are verified. Failure of the strict test is a decline, not UNSAT.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Uniform all-target syndrome fusion]\label{lem:bh22-fusion}
In the notation of Lemma~\ref{lem:ms29-density}, let $r_i=\dim\pi_iK$. Choose a forest on punctured slots with every edge $ij$ satisfying $\pi_{ij}K=U_i\times U_j$. If
\[
 \sum_i2^{-r_i}-\sum_{ij\in T}2^{-\dim U_i-\dim U_j}<1,
\]
the actual sum is the full affine hull, with deterministic polynomial recognition and reverse lift.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For each target in the affine sum acquire its kernel coset. The hole probabilities are bounded above by $2^{-r_i}$; on forest edges surjectivity makes the joint hole probability exactly the stated correction for every target. Lemma~\ref{lem:bh22-forest} applies in kernel coordinates, with a fixed sufficient uniform bound. Isolated vertices need only the marginal upper bound. Arbitrary target-specific intersections cannot be used for uniform fusion without an additional proof. Store the group map and lift; a group of size at least two decreases table count plus rank mass by at least one. Reclose after each strict change. Polynomially many specified group tests and a fixed original-input reserve suffice for this admitted sequence, not arbitrary subgroup search or universal branch aggregation.
\end{proof}
For $q=2^r\ge8$, take $D=(\mathbb F_q)^q$ and $K=\{(a+\lambda b)_{\lambda\in\mathbb F_q}:a,b\in\mathbb F_q\}$. In $D/K$ the $q$ slot spaces are injective and pairwise disjoint because nonzero $K$ words have at least $q-1$ nonzero slots. Any two kernel projections are surjective. With arbitrary single holes the whole density is one and every triple has zero kernel; BA22 pair and MS29 whole/triple policies decline. The full independent-row transversal condition on kernel coordinates also fails when $q>2r$. Nevertheless any spanning tree gives $B=1-(q-1)/q^2<1$ uniformly, so the group fuses. This does not exclude larger proper density-certified groups or other peer rules. The quotient example is symbolic; the checker executes actual field-coordinate avoidance, not a full native reverse adapter.
\begin{lemma}[Moment indistinguishability of opposite-label high-girth sources]\label{lem:bh22-moments}
For a linear unguarded signed NAE-3 source with Berge girth $g$, the complete identity-indexed joint rejection probabilities of every order $j<g$ are $4^{-j}$, irrespective of signs. The DO01/DO09 critical monotone UNSAT sources have a single-sign SAT neighbor on the identical scopes; these statistics cannot distinguish those labels.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Any set of $j<g$ owners is a Berge forest. If it has $c$ components, its incidence graph has $2j+c$ incident variables; the common kernel of its relative-bit observation map is constant on each component, hence rank $2j$. Its forbidden two-bit words have joint measure $2^{-2j}$ regardless of signs. Delete one critical owner and take a satisfying word. The deleted owner must be monochromatic; negating one literal there makes that word legal. Consequently every listed statistic is identical for the critical root and this SAT neighbor. On any linear raw source the maximum tree bound is $(3m+1)/16$, failing strict eligibility for $m\ge5$. This is a data-loss obstruction to classifiers using only the indicated moments, not a lower bound for algorithms reading signs, scopes, guards or other data. The single-budget neighbor changes the rank of a hole and is not asserted indistinguishable. Growing-order explicit acquisition is not presumed polynomial.
\end{proof}

\section{RT28: Exact all-subgroup support obstruction and component-target consumer}\label{sec:rt28}
The exact support, not merely the sufficient certificates of BA22, MS29 and BH22, can prevent the proposed full or singly punctured affine normalization. We use BD22's stacked-image quotient on an actual raw signed NAE-3 chart, with empty guard.
\begin{lemma}[Complement-component rank and target consumer]\label{lem:rt28-components}
Let $H$ be a connected 3-uniform hypergraph with $n$ vertices and $m$ owners, $M:\mathbb F_2^n\to D=(\mathbb F_2^2)^m$ the relative observation map $Mx_i=(x_a+x_b,x_a+x_c)$ for owner $(a,b,c)$, and $\pi:D\to D/\operatorname{im}M$ the quotient. Each signed owner permits a three-word table $T_i$. Let $J$ be a nonempty group of $k$ owner IDs and $c_J$ the number of components on all $n$ vertices after deleting $J$ (including isolated vertices). Then
\[
 \dim(D_J\cap\operatorname{im}M)=c_J-1,\qquad
 \dim\pi(D_J)=2k-c_J+1,
\]
where $D_J$ denotes the coordinate slots supported on $J$. Membership of an actual target $t$ in $\sum_{i\in J}\pi(T_i)$ reduces uniformly and exactly to a residual on $c_J-1$ free bits, with a polynomial-time map and witness lift.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The condition $Mx\in D_J$ means $x$ is constant on every remaining component. Since $H$ is connected, $\ker M$ consists of global constants. Rank-nullity proves the identities. Reject $t$ outside $\pi(D_J)$ by Gaussian elimination; otherwise acquire a particular preimage $z_0\in D_J$. All preimages differ by $Mx$ with one bit per remaining component, modulo the global constant gauge. For each owner in $J$ impose its actual three-word condition on $z_{0,i}+Mx_i$ by substituting the component bits. This gives signed NAE or binary, unary or constant conditions when variables identify. Use actual guard-specific certified closure initially and after deductions, then decide the reduced residual; any model yields the legal tuple and verifies its target by the same source map. For $c_J=O(\log N)$ enumeration of the remaining free bits is polynomial in original encoded $N$, with discovery, all scans, target check and lift charged. For $c_J=1$ the tuple is unique. No claim of polynomiality for arbitrary $c_J$; full-group target zero recovers the original SAT problem, and a legal partial tuple is not an unconditional original model.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Exact all-subgroup fusion obstruction]\label{lem:rt28-no-fusion}
If every nontrivial vertex cut of $H$ crosses at least eight original owners, then for \emph{every} signing and \emph{every} group $J$ with $k\ge2$, the actual sum $S_J=\sum_{i\in J}\pi(T_i)$ is neither an affine coset nor an affine coset minus a single point. Its affine hull has dimension $r=2k-c_J+1$, and for $k\ge3$ its complement within that hull contains more than $2^{r-1}$ points.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The slot map is injective on each owner and on each pair since deletion of fewer than eight owners cannot disconnect the graph. Each three-word table affinely spans its two-space, so the sum affinely spans $\pi(D_J)$. By counting the $3^k$ legal tuples, its density is bounded by
\[
 \frac{|S_J|}{2^r}\le 2^{c_J-1}(3/4)^k.
\]
For $c_J=1$ the map is injective, hence density $(3/4)^k$ and at least seven missing words for $k\ge2$. For $c_J\ge2$, each component has at least eight original crossing owners, all deleted; a triple is counted at most three times, giving $8c_J\le3k$. Consequently the density is at most $\frac12(2^{3/8}3/4)^k<1/2$ (since $2^3 3^8<4^8$). Also for $c_J=1$, $k\ge3$ gives density below $1/2$. Since $r\ge13k/8$ for $k\ge2$, the missing-point count grows exponentially in $k$ (superpolynomial in original $N$ when $k=\Omega(n)$ and $N$ is polynomial in $n$).
\end{proof}
In particular no sound BA22 pair, MS29 multiway or BH22 forest-certified full/single-hole fusion can succeed on any such raw group, even with omniscient subgroup selection. The actual support has the wrong shape. Initial necessary hull restrictions are stagnant because each individual relative word extends to a source word when every other owner is relaxed to its entire local hull. The global slot spaces are pairwise disjoint but not a direct sum (total kernel dimension $n-1$), so DS22 common adapted basis declines. Min owner cut itself is polynomially recognizable: replace each triple by its three pair edges, retaining multiplicities; a crossing triple contributes precisely two cut edges, so weighted global mincut gives twice the owner-cut number. This is not a claim against compact nonlinear support expressions or target-specific queries; Lemma~\ref{lem:rt28-components} is one such bypass.
\begin{lemma}[Unpadded simultaneous opposite-label family]\label{lem:rt28-family}
There exist arbitrarily large identical-scope signed NAE-3 SAT/UNSAT neighbors differing in one literal, with degree at most 36, linear number of owners, minimum owner cut at least eight, Berge girth $\Omega(\log n)$, and every owner subset of size at most $\delta n$ satisfying $|V(S)|>7|S|/4$ for a fixed $\delta>0$. The UNSAT member has no constant-size UNSAT subregistry and its standard two-clause NAE encoding requires general resolution size $2^{\Omega(n)}$. Both labels obey Lemma~\ref{lem:rt28-no-fusion}.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Begin with 36 independent uniform partitions of $n_0$ vertices into triples ($3\mid n_0$), or $12n_0$ owners. For $s$ selected slots and $u=\lfloor7s/4\rfloor$ fixed vertices, the probability that all selected triples lie in the set is at most $(u/n_0)^{3s}$ by sampling without replacement in each partition. Union bounding over slot and vertex choices gives $[C(s/n_0)^{1/4}]^s$ for an absolute $C$. For sufficiently small fixed $\delta$, summing through $\delta n_0$ tends to zero: split at $\sqrt{n_0}$ and bound the two geometric tails separately. The expected number of incidence cycles of length $2\ell$ is at most $C_0^\ell$ for $\ell=O(\log n_0)$, for a fixed $C_0>1$: select $\ell$ distinct variable IDs and owner slots, choose their two prescribed positions in each triple ($6^\ell$ choices), and bound the probability of prescribed entries by $(n_0-2\ell)^{-2\ell}$ across the independent partitions. Incompatible prescribed entries have probability zero. For $g=\lfloor\log n_0/(4\log C_0)\rfloor$, Markov's inequality permits at most $\sqrt{n_0}$ short cycles with probability tending to one. Delete one owner per short cycle, preserving expansion and leaving Berge girth greater than $g$.
Recursively split any remaining vertex block along a nontrivial cut crossed by at most seven remaining owners, deleting those crossing owners. There are at most $n_0-1$ splits, hence at most $7(n_0-1)$ further deletions. The final blocks retain more than $4n_0$ owners for large $n_0$, so some block with $n$ vertices and $m>4n$ owners has minimum cut at least eight. Its $m>\delta n_0$ by expansion (otherwise $n>7m/4$), and $n\ge m/12$ by the degree bound. Thus $n=\Omega(n_0)$, and all claimed inherited properties hold. This block is not obtained by padding an existing contradictory core.
Choose random independent literal signs; expected satisfying assignments $2^n(3/4)^m<1$, so an UNSAT signing exists. Choose a SAT signing by avoiding a fixed assignment's relative words. Along a sequence flipping one literal at a time between the signings there is an opposite-label transition on identical scopes. Neither the sign-boundary acquisition nor the asymptotic generator is claimed to be efficiently implemented. Every small owner set has more than $|S|/2$ degree-one variables by $2|V(S)|-3|S|>|S|/2$ and is satisfiable by recursive private-variable peeling. As in RT26, the minimum original-owner support of a resolution clause is subadditive; any refutation passes through a clause with support between $\delta n/2$ and $\delta n$ (up to rounding). Each degree-one variable of a minimal supporting set must appear in that clause, otherwise its owner could be repaired in a falsifying assignment by changing that private variable, contradicting minimality. Width is therefore $\Omega(n)$. The \href{https://doi.org/10.1145/375827.375835}{Ben-Sasson--Wigderson width-size theorem} gives exponential general resolution size. BH22's raw moments through orders below girth are identical across these neighbors. Minimal UNSAT is not asserted, nor a lower bound for alternating nonresolution reasoning, changed guards or arbitrary SAT.
\end{proof}

\section{DP23: Ordered predecessor fusion and fixed-scope aggregate obstruction}\label{sec:dp23}
Attack Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} by combining BH22 forest acquisition with higher-order signed hole intersections on actual guards, rather than enumerating all targets.
\begin{lemma}[Ordered predecessor certificate]\label{lem:dp23-order}
On a consistent explicit affine guard $G$, order affine forbidden events $E_i$ and choose sets $P_i$ of at most $w$ earlier event IDs. Define
\[
 f(x)=\sum_i 1_{E_i}(x)\prod_{j\in P_i}(1-1_{E_j}(x)).
\]
If $\mathbb E[f\mid G]<1$, a legal word is constructible in deterministic polynomial bit time for fixed $w$. A paid acquisition policy with $w\ge1$ never worsens the BH22 maximum-tree certificate.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The integer $f$ is nonnegative and vanishes exactly on legal words: the earliest violated event contributes one. Each expectation is an inclusion-exclusion sum of at most $2^w$ Gaussian-counted affine intersections. Fix the order and predecessor lists during reconstruction; successively choose a nonempty coordinate side of no larger conditional expectation, using the exact weighted average identity. The final integer is below one and hence zero. Verify the original events and guard. Acquire a maximum-weight spanning tree as in BH22, orient from a root and traverse parent-first. The singleton parent lists give the BH22 bound; independently minimizing each term over sets of at most $w$ earlier IDs cannot increase it. The number of Gaussian counts is $O(m^{w+1}2^w)$ for fixed $w$, plus $O(nm2^w)$ during lifting, each on explicit polynomial-size systems. No optimal ordering or free semantic closure is claimed. Related known probability bounds are cherry trees and multitrees (\href{https://doi.org/10.1287/moor.26.1.174.10596}{Bukszar and Prekopa 2001}, \href{https://doi.org/10.1017/S0001867800010880}{Bukszar 2001}); novelty of the probability inequality is not asserted.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Uniform third-order fusion beyond forests and kernel transversals]\label{lem:dp23-field}
In the punctured-table sum setting of MS29, suppose each kernel projection onto $\{i\}\cup P_i$ is surjective onto the corresponding product of slot spaces. If $\sum_i p_i\prod_{j\in P_i}(1-p_j)<1$, where $p_i=2^{-\dim U_i}$, the sum is its entire affine hull and every target has a paid polynomial reverse lift for fixed $w$. There is a family on which whole-group MS29 density, BH22 forest, pair/triple fusion and full kernel independent-row transversals decline, but $w=2$ certifies full fusion.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Every target fiber is a translate of the summation kernel, so the specified projections give independent uniform words and the displayed bound uniformly. Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:dp23-order} in kernel coordinates. For $q=2^r\ge16$, quotient $(\mathbb F_q)^{q+1}$ by the dimension-$3r$ binary kernel of evaluation words $(a+b\lambda+c\lambda^2)_{\lambda\in\mathbb F_q}$ with additional infinity coordinate $c$. Any three distinct slot projections are surjective by interpolation, including infinity. A nonzero evaluation word has at least $q-1$ nonzero slots, hence each union of at most three slots injects in the quotient. Puncture every slot at any one word. Whole density is $(q+1)/q>1$, all pair probabilities $q^{-2}$, and the best forest bound is exactly one. No full independent-row transversal of the kernel dual exists since $q+1>3r$. For any order choose predecessor counts $0,1,2,\ldots,2$ and put $p=1/q$. The new bound is $p+p(1-p)+(q-1)p(1-p)^2=1-p+2p^2-p^3<1$. This is a uniform support identity, not just a single-target witness. No claim that every larger proper subgroup declines, or that synthetic slot ranks preserve strict physical degree.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[All-order fixed-width raw obstruction]\label{lem:dp23-girth}
On a raw signed linear NAE registry of Berge girth $g>w+1$, every ordered predecessor certificate with at most $w$ earlier IDs per event has expectation at least $(m/4)(3/4)^w$. Thus every fixed $w$ fails eventually on both labels of the RT28 unpadded family, regardless of ordering or acquisition. In this independence range, strict success requires $w>\log_{4/3}(m/4)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
BH22 gives joint rejection probabilities $4^{-j}$ for all $j<g$, so each term has exact expectation $(1/4)(3/4)^{|P_i|}$. Sum the lower bounds. RT28 additionally excludes full/singly punctured affine fusion for every nontrivial raw group, regardless of certificate. Neither result excludes signed cuts, conditioning, nonlocal target consumers or unrestricted SAT decision.
\end{proof}
\paragraph{Aggregate and collaboration.}
Use certified guarded impossible/full-hole and rank-one opposite-row closure or necessary affine-hull restriction before acquisition, after accepted changes and at stagnation. For a fixed polynomially enumerated set of group candidates, each admitted fusion of at least two slots decreases the original table count plus sum of ranks by at least one. Necessary strict affine-hull restrictions decrease rank. Keep original owner IDs, guard, and disjoint merged-group lift tree. Each candidate scan and each reverse lift has polynomial bit cost for fixed $w$; no reserve reset, free complete closure, arbitrary subgroup or growing-width search oracle. Serial same-realization polynomial $T,S$ imply $CM\le(T+1)S$. Failure of the bound is a decline. Universal coverage and aggregate branching remain OPEN.

\section{S28: Exact local guard quotient and guarded predecessor obstruction}\label{sec:s28}
DP23's ordered predecessor bound and RT28's high-girth family leave open whether arbitrary dense affine guards can systematically rescue the fixed-width certificate. The following result gives a paid exact statistical quotient and rules out a simple sublinear-rank rescue on unchanged raw charts.
\begin{lemma}[Local guard quotient]\label{lem:s28-local}
For a consistent affine guard $G$ with coefficient row space $R$ of rank $g$ and RHS functional $b$, let $U_i$ be the span of the two relative NAE observation rows of owner $i$. Fix $w\ge1$ and put
\[
 U_J=\sum_{i\in J}U_i,\qquad L=\operatorname{span}\bigcup_{1\le |J|\le w+1}(R\cap U_J).
\]
The guard $G_L$ retaining $b|_L$ induces exactly the same uniform local observation distributions as $G$ on every such $J$. A basis of $L$ is discoverable in polynomial time for fixed $w$, and its union of variable supports $H$ has size at most $3(w+1)g$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For each $J$, $L\cap U_J=R\cap U_J$ by inclusion in both directions. Under a uniform affine guard the stacked observation image is uniform on an affine space, defined by precisely those linear combinations of its rows lying in the guard row space with RHS given by the induced functional. The equal intersections and RHS imply identical images and distributions. Enumerate all $O(m^{w+1})$ owner sets and compute the intersections by Gaussian elimination, choosing a basis of their span from the resulting generators. Each generator is supported on at most $3(w+1)$ source variables and there are at most $g$ basis vectors. Equivalently enumerate at most $2^{2(w+1)}$ combinations of the local rows per subset. Dense equations may cancel, so inspecting only the weights of supplied rows is not sound. The quotient preserves statistics, not the full solution set: retain $G$ for decisions, conditional-expectation reconstruction, and all deduction provenance.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Guarded fixed-width score obstruction]\label{lem:s28-guard}
For a raw signed NAE chart with $m$ owners, maximum occurrence degree $\Delta$, and Berge girth greater than $w+1$, put $D=3(\Delta-1)$ and $C_w=3(w+1)\Delta\sum_{j=0}^{w}D^j$ with $D^0=1$. For any consistent affine guard $G$ of actual rank $g$, either at most $w$ owner holes cover $G$ (a polynomially testable guarded contradiction for fixed $w$), or every DP23 ordered predecessor score of width at most $w$ satisfies
\[
 B(G)\ge \max(0,m-C_w g)2^{-2w-2}.
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
In the owner overlap graph the maximum degree is at most $D$; by Lemma~\ref{lem:s28-local} at most $C_wg$ owners lie within distance $w$ of an owner touching $H$. For any other owner $i$ and predecessor set $P$ of size at most $w$, the component of $i$ in the graph induced by $J=\{i\}\cup P$ avoids $H$. The incidence union of $J$ is a forest by girth, so its $2|J|$ relative observation rows are independent: the rank is the number of incident variables minus the number of components, namely $2|J|$. Any combination of these rows belonging to $R$ is in $L$ and supported in $H$. Contributions from distinct overlap components have disjoint variable support. Thus the contribution from the component of $i$ is zero and row independence makes its coefficients zero. There is no induced affine dependence involving the two $i$ observations, which are therefore jointly uniform and independent of the predecessor observations on $G$. Its forbidden relative word has probability $1/4$. Unless a set of at most $w$ predecessor holes covers $G$, the probability of their simultaneous avoidance is positive and at least $2^{-2w}$ (uniform image on at most $2^{2w}$ words). Each remote term is thus at least $2^{-2w-2}$, all other terms nonnegative. Sum. Test the small-cover alternative using exact inclusion-exclusion and Gaussian counts over all such sets.
\end{proof}
For fixed $w,\Delta$, $m\to\infty$ and $g=o(m)$, this bound rules out strict score success on either label of RT28's raw high-girth family unless the small-cover test already rejects the guard. For $m>2^{2w+2}$, score success requires $g>(m-2^{2w+2})/C_w$. This refers to actual rank after deductions, not branching depth; high-rank necessary facts could be discovered cheaply by other methods. No claim for modified nonlinear scopes, arbitrary adaptive algorithms, or all post-guard fusion. An unordered predecessor score can obey this bound without being a SAT certificate; the DP23 earliest-event argument needs an acyclic order.
\paragraph{Aggregate ledger and evidence.}
Run impossible/full-hole and rank-one opposite-row closure on actual $G$, restart after strict deductions and at stagnation. For fixed $w$, Gaussian acquisition, all small-cover probes and statistic computations are polynomial in original $N$, with polynomial storage. For a strict ordered score use DP23's paid reconstruction on full $G$, not $G_L$. Same-execution serial $CM\le(T+1)S$. No growing-width or repeated-branch budget is granted. Actual S27 n7/n15 labels verified under raw/dense/single-pin guards, tested scores identical; separate seven imported DA22 cuts reject n15 UNSAT by closure, not independent proof of acquisition. The n7 UNSAT unordered score $0.984375<1$ explicitly falsifies treating cyclic predecessor minimization as a witness certificate. Six planted loose-cycle controls verify remote independence, dense cancellation and renewed closure. No new shared coverage, measured speed gain, high-girth generator, generic component-target replay, full native/solver/kernel/TeX or measured CM. \href{https://github.com/j15marti/pnp/commit/f13ec6d51fc1891862b6beae5f4f65a3f4c84346}{Report}; \href{https://github.com/j15marti/pnp/commit/fba0eea2f3d9999fedd99e3743faea42b25ccc6c}{checker}; \href{https://github.com/j15marti/pnp/commit/85a552c6e4b38d4dfb988dbe57ee0360af87d8c4}{results}.

\section{BS22: Owner-closed affine factors and aggregate guarded rank credit}\label{sec:bs22}
Attack Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} using the actual observation spaces rather than a Cartesian product of compatibility messages. This complements GD29, DS22 and DP23, and is an exact declining dispatch, not a universal solver.
\begin{lemma}[Canonical owner-closed direct-sum factors]\label{lem:bs22-factor}
After certified guard substitution and rank-zero/rank-one packet closure, write $U_i$ for the observation rowspace of each nonconstant live owner and $V=\sum_i U_i$, $r=\dim V$. A polynomial-time Gaussian and union-find algorithm discovers the unique finest owner partition whose group spans form a direct sum. Feasibility is the AND of the group decisions, and feasible group words glue by a polynomial source lift under the actual guard.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Choose a basis $B$ of $V$ from actual owner rows. Express each row in $B$, and union all basis indices appearing in any row of a single owner. Each resulting component uses only its disjoint subset of $B$, and each basis element belongs to an owner there, so the group spans are exactly the spans of those subsets. For any other direct-sum owner partition, each basis row belongs to one group, the basis partitions accordingly into bases of the group spaces, and unique row expansions cannot cross groups. Thus the constructed partition refines every such partition; no semantic equivalence test or enumeration of owner subsets is used. Assign the actual functional on each component from its witness. Their direct sum extends to a functional on the full free-coordinate dual, giving a source assignment by Gaussian elimination and inverse guard substitution. Check all source owners. The underlying fundamental-basis matroid component algorithm is standard; see Aprile and Ronco, \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23624}{arXiv:2611.23624}; here owners additionally impose the must-link condition.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Paid guard-to-AND aggregate rule]\label{lem:bs22-credit}
Let $r>0$ be the live observation rank. For a rank-$k$ guard subspace in $V$, condition on each of its $2^k$ bit words, run certified closure and Lemma~\ref{lem:bs22-factor}, skipping proven contradictions and deciding no-owner sides locally. This is an exact OR of ANDs. If the positive child ranks $r_{bj}$ satisfy
\[
 \sum_{b,j}r_{bj}^{c}\le r^{c}-1
\]
for fixed $c\ge2$, it is an admitted expansion in Theorem~\ref{thm:aggregate} with $\mu=r$. A sufficient condition for $k>0$ is $\max r_{bj}\le\alpha r$, $2^k\alpha^{c-1}\le1$, for fixed $\alpha<1$. A nontrivial unguarded factorization also strictly contracts.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Each consistent branch has residual rank at most $r-k$ since the independent guards lie in $V$; further affine closure and deleting satisfied owners cannot increase rank. Within a branch ranks add. Thus the balanced sufficient condition gives an upper bound $2^k(\alpha r)^{c-1}(r-k)<r^c$. For unguarded direct factors use strict superadditivity of positive integer powers $c\ge2$. No-child cases are local terminals, not rank-zero unpaid child nodes. Glue only within the selected guard, as in Lemma~\ref{lem:bs22-factor}. For fixed $k$, searching a polynomial list of candidate independent guards, including the actual owner-row list for $k=1$, and testing this inequality costs polynomially per occurrence in original $N$: at most original owner count, polynomial-size row masks/offsets, at most $n$ strict necessary affine additions with reclosure, Gaussian basis discovery, all failed trials, and explicit source lifts. A fixed rank leaf cap gives an exact paid terminal. For a fixed admitted policy there are at most $n^c$ positive-rank occurrences by telescoping; serial same-realization $T,S$ polynomial, $CM\le(T+1)S$. If no admitted move exists return OPEN. No claim of complete candidate acquisition over all affine guards.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Both-label obstruction to actual-row squared-credit dispatch]\label{lem:bs22-steiner}
On every raw signed complete-pair Steiner NAE registry with $n\ge31$, the policy using only rank-zero/rank-one packet closure, unguarded direct-sum factorization and one actual pair-row guard with squared rank credit cannot make a first contraction (assuming leaf cap below $n-1$).
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The root observation rank is $R=n-1$; every partition of its owners gives complementary edge graphs on $K_n$, at least one connected, hence at least one span has rank $R$. There is no nontrivial direct sum. Every actual pair row belongs to a unique owner triangle. Under either value, that owner is either satisfied or forces exactly one additional independent pair equation within that triangle. The resulting guard has rank $g\in\{1,2\}$ and its nonzero vectors belong to that owner's plane. Every other plane has zero intersection with it because its three nonzero vectors are distinct labelled pair rows. All other owners stay full rank, no further rank-one closure applies, and neither branch rejects. The affected owner is removed. The remaining graph $K_n$ minus the three triangle edges is connected, so its observation rank after restriction is $r=R-g$. For any bipartition of remaining owners, add the three missing edges to the first edge graph. One of the resulting complementary graphs is connected. The corresponding original span thus has rank at least $R-3$, and its restricted rank is at least $r-3$. For any bipartition of direct-sum components one side therefore has mass at most three. Since $r>9$, some component has rank at least $r-3$: if all components had rank at most three, greedily accumulating mass just above three would leave mass above three; otherwise the complement of a component of rank above three must have mass at most three. Each of the two guard branches thus has a child of rank at least $n-6$. Their squared credit alone is at least $2(n-6)^2>(n-1)^2$. All specified candidates decline regardless of signs. This does not exclude other guard subspaces, other exponents, stronger closure, DA22/BS21 direct certificates, or unrestricted SAT decision.
\end{proof}

\section{Sign-sensitive incidence cycle code and the absolute-tail obstruction (DO23)}\label{sec:do23}
\begin{lemma}[Exact cycle code and first sign-sensitive coefficient]\label{lem:do23-cycle}
For an unguarded signed NAE3 registry on $n$ variables and $m$ distinct-owner triples, let $H$ be the bipartite incidence graph with signs $\eta_e\in\{-1,1\}$. Let $\mathcal C$ be its binary cycle space (all even edge sets), $k(C)=|C|/2$, $\eta(C)=\prod_{e\in C}\eta_e$, and $V$ the number of violated owners on a uniform source word. Then
\[
Z_\eta(z)=\mathbb E(1-z)^V=\sum_{C\in\mathcal C}\eta(C)(-z/4)^{k(C)}(1-z/4)^{m-k(C)}.
\]
The exact source model count is $2^n(3/4)^m P_\eta$, where $P_\eta=\sum_C\eta(C)(-1/3)^{k(C)}$. Flipping one incidence $e$ negates precisely the terms containing $e$. If $e$ is not a bridge and $2g_e$ is the shortest cycle length through $e$, all coefficients of the difference $Z_{\eta'}-Z_\eta$ below degree $g_e$ vanish; its degree-$g_e$ coefficient is $-2(-1/4)^{g_e}$ times the signed number of shortest cycles through $e$. This signed count is uniformly computable in polynomial bit time. On the unsigned baseline the coefficient is nonzero. A bridge flip preserves the solution set up to a polynomially acquired variable switching map.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For independent uniform spins $s_v$, a rejection indicator is $(1+\sum_{u<v\in i}\eta_{iu}\eta_{iv}s_us_v)/4$. Expand the owner factors $1-zI_i$: at most one pair is selected per owner, and spin summation keeps exactly even variable degrees. Every even incidence subgraph has owner degree zero or two, so the expansion is bijective, with the claimed weights. An even subgraph containing $e$ contains a simple cycle through $e$; at minimum cardinality it is exactly such a cycle. Delete $e$, run BFS, and propagate signed path sums along the shortest-path DAG; multiply by $\eta_e$. Counts have polynomial bit length (at most $(n+m)!$ paths). Cancellation at the leading degree is possible on general signed charts; a zero signed count is not a proof of equivalence. More generally two signings with identical cycle products differ by a coboundary, acquired on a spanning forest and checked on the non-tree edges. Switch source variables and owner signs accordingly; an owner-wide flip does not affect NAE. This is gauge equivalence, not a complete semantic key for arbitrary charts.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Absolute-tail obstruction on the RT28 unpadded family]\label{lem:do23-tail}
Let $A=\sum_C3^{-k(C)}$ and $A_e=\sum_{C\ni e}3^{-k(C)}$. Then $A\ge2^{m-n+1}$ and for every nonbridge $e$,
\[
A_e\ge \frac{A}{1+3^{g_e}}\ge \frac{2^{m-n+1}}{1+3^n}.
\]
On the connected RT28 scopes with $m>4n$, min owner cut at least eight and degree at most 36, every incidence is nonbridge. Let $q=2^{1-n}(4/3)^m$, the minimum positive complement-pair count quantum in $P_\eta$ units. For any signing and any literal flip, the absolute omitted mass of the difference $P_{\eta'}-P_\eta$ after materializing at most polynomially many individual cycle terms is exponentially larger than $q$. Hence polynomial individual-term truncation with an absolute-tail error budget below one count quantum is not a universal exact label-change evaluator on these opposite-label scopes.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The positive expansion $A=\mathbb E\prod_i(1+\tfrac13\sum_{u<v\in i}s_us_v)$ has factors either $2$ or $2/3$. The two constant spin words give the bound. XOR with a shortest cycle through $e$ bijects even sets excluding $e$ to those containing it, increasing $k$ by at most $g_e$. This proves $A_e\ge3^{-g_e}(A-A_e)$; a simple cycle uses at most $n$ distinct variable vertices. A bridge would separate nonempty variable sets with at most one crossing owner, contradicting the RT28 mincut. The sign-flip difference has absolute term mass $2A_e$. Its ratio to $q$ is at least $2(3/2)^m/(1+3^n)$, exponentially growing at $m>4n$; $q$ itself grows exponentially there. Removing $p$ individual terms removes at most $2p$ absolute mass. Thus any polynomial $p$ leaves the claimed tail. This holds for both signs of the actual adjacent labels; it excludes neither signed grouping and cancellation nor other decision-specific bounds. No unrestricted time lower bound, sampling impossibility, or simultaneous obstruction against arbitrary transformations follows.
\end{proof}
\paragraph{Constructive escape and charged implementation.}
Even edge sets factor over biconnected blocks, since every simple cycle lies in one block and each block choice gives an even edge set. The signed enumerator therefore factors multiplicatively. For a fixed cap $\beta_B\le C\log(N+2)$ on every block cycle rank, acquire blocks and cycle bases, enumerate each block independently in polynomial time, and multiply exact rationals with polynomial bit lengths (denominators divide $3^m$). For a witness, a block spanning tree has bags of size at most two; add one endpoint of each non-tree edge to every block bag, then glue at articulation bags. The incidence CSP has variable domains two and owner domains six, with binary edge equality; bounded-width DP and reverse lift are polynomial for this cap. Coordinate pins are allowed in the DP, arbitrary dense guards are not free. Reclose initially, after each accepted deduction and at stagnation; keep guard provenance and do not use the unguarded cycle identity on transformed charts without a proof. Charge graph discovery, failed caps, bit arithmetic, DP memory, all accesses, source verification and reconstruction in the same realization; $CM\le(T+1)S$ for a serial polynomial admitted run. No universal block-rank bound or aggregate reserve reset. The block DP is a proved implementation bound, not executed here.
\paragraph{Executed common controls.}

S27 n7 shortest cycle order 3, signed count 8, models 0/10; n15 order 3, signed count 10 from 24 paths, models 0/4. \section{GD30: Guarded signed Fourier transfer and exact all-sign count rank}\label{sec:gd30}
Attack Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} using DO23's signed cycle grouping and BS22's actual owner interfaces, while preserving S28's full guard. This supplies a paid exact evaluator, and falsifies a universal all-sign signed separable count-interface shortcut even when cancellation and negative factors are permitted.
\begin{lemma}[Exact guarded signed syndrome transfer]\label{lem:gd30-transfer}
After certified closure, let a consistent affine guard have $d$ free coordinates $y$, and let the remaining bounded-rank avoidance owners test $A_i y\ne p_i$ with independent rows of rank $d_i$. Put $D=\sum_i d_i$ and $h_i(0)=2^{d_i}-1$, $h_i(k)=-(-1)^{k^\top p_i}$ for $k\ne0$. The exact number of source words on this guard is
\[
 C=2^{d-D}\sum_{\sum_i A_i^\top k_i=0}\prod_i h_i(k_i).
\]
For a supplied owner ordering or binary tree of maximum shared observation rank $w$, this count and a source witness when positive can be acquired in $2^{O(w)}\operatorname{poly}(N)$ bit time and space, with bounded owner rank. In particular a fixed logarithmic cap gives a paid polynomial terminal.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Expand each acceptance indicator in the binary character basis and sum over all free words; character orthogonality gives the displayed identity. For a prefix $I$, retain a signed integer sum $T_I(s)$ of products of its Fourier weights with total syndrome $s$, only for $s\in U_I\cap U_{\bar I}$, where $U_I$ is the span of its observation rows. A discarded syndrome cannot be canceled by any suffix. Initialize $T_\varnothing(0)=1$, convolve with the next owner's at most $2^{d_i}$ weights, add all contributions to a key before dropping exact zero coefficients, and intersect with the next suffix span. On a binary tree combine children by XOR of syndrome keys and retain only the parent interface; the same orthogonality applies. There are at most $2^w$ keys per interface, at most $2^{2w}$ pairs per binary merge, and the integer magnitudes are bounded by $\prod_i\sum_k|h_i(k)|\le 2^{O(D)}$. Gaussian row acquisition, exact arithmetic, scaling, lookups, temporaries and verification have the stated bounds. BS22 direct factors have interface zero; multiply their unscaled scalar messages with the single global dimension factor. DO23's unguarded signed incidence expansion is the rank-two special case. For a witness, use GD28's positive feasibility gluing on the same actual decomposition and guard and verify the source word, with a separately charged pass. Alternatively use independently capped conditional counts; any declined conditional query must cause the witness-producing variant to decline, since quotient width need not decrease. No complete semantic closure oracle is used. A sign-specific sparse actual-work cap can admit cancellations at larger nominal width, but universal success of such a cap remains OPEN.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Exact all-sign count flattening rank]\label{lem:gd30-signrank}
Fix the original two relative observation rows of each signed NAE owner and any consistent affine guard, retaining all original independently variable local forbidden-word labels (even if an owner rank drops after restriction). Partition the owners into $A,B$, let $U,V$ be their restricted row spans and $w=\dim(U\cap V)$. Let $M(p,q)$ count source solutions on the guard when the independent rank-two forbidden-word tuples on the two sides are $p,q$. Then
\[
 \operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q} M=2^w.
\]
The same equality holds over any field of characteristic other than two or three. Thus an exact separable sum $\sum_{j=1}^k u_j(p)v_j(q)$ over the rationals or reals requires $k\ge2^w$, even allowing negative factors and arbitrary computation within each side.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Retain the original two Fourier coordinates of each owner rather than simplifying as a function of its sign. The local Fourier weights are $3$ at zero and $-1$ elsewhere, times the character of its forbidden word; the affine guard offset contributes another nonzero sign character. Applying invertible Walsh transforms separately on $p,q$ yields, up to a nonzero scalar, a matrix with entry $a(k_A)b(k_B)$ when $L_A k_A=L_B k_B$, zero otherwise. Here $L_A,L_B$ sum the restricted observation rows, and every $a,b$ is a nonzero product of powers of three and signs. Group rows and columns by their respective syndrome images. Each shared syndrome gives one nonzero outer-product block, disjoint from every other block; all unmatched blocks are zero. There are $2^w$ shared syndromes. Hence the transformed rank is exactly $2^w$, unchanged by inverting the transforms. The sum-product separation bound follows from matrix rank, and the syndrome factorization attains it. For general local functions with Fourier zeros, count only shared syndromes attained by a nonzero-weight index on both sides.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Both-representation obstruction for raw complete-pair scopes]\label{lem:gd30-raw}
On the raw complete-pair Steiner NAE registry, every binary owner tree has a cut with all-sign count flattening rank $2^{\Omega(n)}$, invariant under invertible affine recoding. A consistent rank-$g$ guard reduces that cut's shared observation rank by at most $g$, as long as the original labelled owner registry is retained.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
A binary tree admits a cut containing between one-third and two-thirds of its owners, hence of its $M=n(n-1)/2$ distinct pair observations. For complementary graphs on the complete graph at least one is connected (if one is disconnected, all cross-component edges lie in the other). Its row span is the entire relative-coordinate span. The other has at least $M/3$ edges, and any graph of row rank $t$ has at most $t(t+1)/2$ distinct edges by the component rank formula and convexity. Therefore $w\ge(\sqrt{1+8M/3}-1)/2=\Omega(n)$. Invertible linear changes preserve intersection rank; quotient by a guard row space of rank $g$ decreases the intersection rank by at most $g$, by the subspace dimension identity. Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:gd30-signrank}. This excludes a universal all-sign separable count interface for unchanged raw scopes, including switching to the signed dual cycle representation. It does not exclude fixed-sign scalar arithmetic circuits, nonlinear registry changes, decision-only methods or other algorithms; in particular it is not a lower bound on SAT computation.
\end{proof}

\section{DA23: Strict high-degree moment obstruction with exact affine escape}
\label{sec:da23}
\begin{lemma}[DA23-A: exact parity-block escape]\label{lem:da23-block}
A simple connected cubic graph with edge bits $u_e$ and vertex charges $b_v$ can be represented by eight signed ternary NAE owners per vertex, four private bits per vertex and one common phase $z$. The compiled registry projects exactly to the affine system $x_{e_1}+x_{e_2}+x_{e_3}+z=b_v$ over $\mathbb F_2$, where $x_e=u_e+z$. The particular compiled family has a uniformly polynomial recognition, decision and reverse-lift algorithm.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For each of four forbidden triples $f$ at a vertex, the clause on relative bits has literals $\ell_i=u_{e_i}+f_i$. Encode it by
$\operatorname{NAE}(x_{e_1}+f_1,x_{e_2}+f_2,y_f)$ and
$\operatorname{NAE}(y_f+1,x_{e_3}+f_3,z)$.
Relative to $z$, choose $y_f+z=(1-\ell_1)(1-\ell_2)$ in Boolean notation. If all literals vanish the first owner forces the private relative bit to one and the second fails; otherwise the displayed witness satisfies both. Conjunction over forbidden triples gives the asserted parity. The cubic graph has even vertex count; the sum of its vertex equations cancels every edge and phase. Odd total charge is UNSAT, even total charge is solvable by incidence Gaussian elimination. Recognition counts occurrences, identifies private degree-two variables whose two owners have four other distinct IDs, groups four such pairs on identical exterior IDs and verifies the 256-word joint tables, coverage and privacy. In this family the external star sets are distinct and external degrees exceed two. Only exactly authenticated groups may be replaced; an arbitrary guard mentioning a private bit must remain or be included in projection. Necessary affine equations may always be retained. Polynomial bit work, failed tests, source verification, reverse lifts and reclosure are charged.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[DA23-B: strict real moment obstruction, not a portfolio obstruction]\label{lem:da23-moment}
There are arbitrarily large odd-charge instances of Lemma~\ref{lem:da23-block} with real Boolean pseudoexpectations of degree $\Omega(v)$, where $v$ is the number of graph vertices, annihilating each owner violation quadratic times all degree-eligible polynomials and satisfying $|\widetilde E[S_iS_j]|\le 1/2$ for distinct physical spins. In particular they meet the strict degree-four hypothesis of DA22-B. The DA22 pair-probe spectral closure alone stalls on these UNSAT instances, but DA23-A decides them in polynomial time.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Use simple 3-vertex-connected cubic graphs of edge expansion $h>0$, which exist at arbitrarily large sizes by the random regular graph expansion and connectivity theorems of Kolesnik--Wormald (2014) and Wormald (1981). For relative edge spin monomials $\chi_T$, $|T|\le D$, define the moment as $\prod_{v\in A}(-1)^{b_v}$ if $T=\delta(A)$ for the unique smaller cut side $A$, and zero if not a cut. Choose $2D/h<v/2$; every such small side has size at most $D/h$. For monomials of degree at most $D/2$, nonzero moment entries correspond to cosets of the cut space. On each coset block signs multiply consistently: symmetric difference of two small sides is still smaller than half the graph. Each block is rank-one signed Gram, proving positivity. On any set of at most $D$ edges, cut subsets form a subgroup with a consistent sign character, hence these moments are the Fourier moments of a genuine uniform affine law. Any vertex star contained in that set obeys its charge.
Choose an independent uniform spin $Z$, put $S_z=Z$, $S_e=ZX_e$ and $S_y=Z(1-2(1-\ell_1)(1-\ell_2))$ with $\ell_i=(1-(-1)^{f_i}X_i)/2$. Substitution of physical degree $d$ uses relative degree at most $2d$; take $D=2d$ and even $d$ with $4d/h<v/2$. Squares reduce to two sums of squares by averaging $Z$. An owner quadratic multiplied by a degree-eligible monomial has support contained in its three-edge star plus at most $2(d-2)$ other edges; the genuine local affine law enforces that charge and the exact lift, so its expectation vanishes. Boolean identities hold by construction.
Distinct raw edge bits are unbiased and independent by 3-edge-connectivity. Each relative private bit is a chosen two-edge word indicator of probability $1/4$, and distinct indicators at one vertex are disjoint. For two different vertices, their complement is connected; cuts supported in the union of the two stars arise only from subsets of these two vertices, up to complement. The two-star local law is therefore uniform under the two charges. Holding one selected pair fixed, flipping the two nonshared edges of the other vertex (or suitable two edges if disjoint) preserves both charges and changes at least one tested bit of the other pair. Thus their joint indicator probability is at most $1/8$. Raw/private, phase/private, private/private and raw/raw spin correlations are consequently bounded in absolute value by $1/2$. The global phase cancels in every pair. The lifted degree is linear in graph order. Apply DA22-B to conclude restricted stagnation, then DA23-A for the affine escape.
\end{proof}
\paragraph{Scope and executed controls.} This is not a linear-hypergraph or physical degree-four family (the phase is high-occurrence); it is not an obstruction to the full portfolio, nor an unrestricted lower bound. Even a high-degree real moment barrier may coexist with easy GF(2) projection. On immutable S27 raw $n=7,15$ opposite-label charts and separate DA22 first/all-seven actual guards, singleton and at-most-three-owner exact local pair closure were compared: all four raw and first-cut charts OPEN, seven-cut chart rejects in both. No incremental common coverage. No global pseudo matrix, asymptotic generator, generic extractor/Gaussian implementation, independent upstream cut acquisition, full native/portfolio/kernel or physical cumulative memory run. Fixed-width declining closure has at most $n-1$ strict rank increases and polynomial aggregate work, space and $CM\le(T+1)S$. \section{BW23: Single-copy native compilation and pin-free dual-rail parity escape}\label{sec:bw23}
This addresses the genuine synchronization cost in I21/BW20 and supplies a native lift for DA23-A, not a universal terminal or a proof of Obligation~\ref{obl:progress}.
\begin{lemma}[Single-copy signed NAE compiler]\label{lem:bw23-single}
For an explicit signed NAE-3 registry with $m$ owners and actual occurrence counts $t_v>0$, there is a uniform exact linear-graph-size reduction to simple closed signed E4/B4 networks, with no pins, using precisely
\[
 k=\sum_v(\lceil t_v/2\rceil-1)
\]
E4 vertices, versus $\sum_v(t_v-1)$ for the duplicate-owner I21 construction with BW20 wires. Both source directions have polynomial lifts. The count is optimal for separate padded all-equal occurrence transports, not for arbitrary reductions.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Use one B4 per owner, with signed literal ports $a,b,c$ and private fourth port $d$. Integer balance is exactly NAE on $a,b,c$, and $d=2-a-b-c$, hence $d=a+b+c$ over $\mathbb F_2$. Let $s$ be the XOR of all literal signs. For even $t_v\ge2$ use the I21 signed E4 occurrence path with $t_v$ exposed stubs (a wire for two). For odd $t_v\ge3$ use the path with $t_v+1$ stubs; the spare carries $x_v$. For $t_v=1$, use the actual literal port as the spare and account for its sign. Connect all $d$ ports and the odd-occurrence spares to one parity block, of charge $s$ XOR the signs of singly occurring literals. Its arity $m+\#\{v:t_v\text{ odd}\}$ is even, since $\sum t_v=3m$. The parity is redundant: summing $d=a+b+c$ over all owners gives $\sum d=s+\sum_{t_v\text{ odd}}x_v$. Thus every source word satisfying the owners extends through the collector by Lemma~\ref{lem:bw21-affine}'s pin-free even parity block, constructed by a chain of $K_4$ gates (two-port case by BW20's wire). Conversely decode source bits from the occurrence paths or their single literal, and each B4 verifies its original owner. Empty source is a trivial SAT terminal. Replace every wire, including a possible loop between distinct ports, by a private $K_5-pq$ balance gadget from Lemma~\ref{lem:bw20-wire}; the two new endpoints are distinct, so simplicity and degree four hold. All graph objects, port maps, deterministic construction and lift are linear in occurrences up to identifier and indexing overhead. Each padded independent equality transport needs at least its exposed arity divided by two minus one E4s by Lemma~\ref{lem:bw20-sync}; the path attains this. No multiplicity preservation claimed. For guarded charts retain actual guard maps, and consume signed pair equations via the BW21 quotient before recompiling; arbitrary guards cannot be dropped.
\end{proof}
In particular $k\ge3m/2-n_{\rm active}$, so on RT28's raw unpadded $m>4n$ family this compiler still uses $k>5n$. This is not an effective tag-rank lower bound, nor an obstruction to alternative solvers or other encodings. Merely enumerating all genuine E4 choices cannot establish a universal polynomial reserve for this construction.
\begin{lemma}[Pin-free dual-rail realization of graph-incidence XOR]\label{lem:bw23-rails}
For an explicit loopless graph-incidence system $\sum_{e\ni v}u_e=b_v$ over $\mathbb F_2$, there is an exact strict simple signed B4-only compilation of linear graph-object size, with no E4, fixed ports or shared phase, and polynomial source lifts. Isolated nonzero-charge vertices are rejected directly; zero-charge isolates are removed.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Represent each edge variable as the XOR of two rails. At a vertex of degree $d>0$, introduce a pure even-parity B4 block on $2d$ ports, using the same even block construction as above. Offset one local rail by $b_v$ and all others by zero. For each original edge, connect corresponding rail ports at its two endpoints with signs equal to the XOR of their actual local offsets. Thus the corrected rails agree along each edge and their XOR defines $u_e$. The local even constraint says exactly $\sum_{e\ni v}u_e=b_v$. Conversely take the two corrected rails $(0,u_e)$ and add actual local offsets; every even local word extends constructively. Use BW20 wires to ensure simplicity and verify all ports. The number of block and wire objects is $O(|E|+|V|)$. The system is a paid pure-balance matching terminal, or solve it directly by forest elimination as in BW22. For DA23-A substitute $u_e=x_e+z$; the relative vertex equations have exactly this graph-incidence form. For the unguarded chart choose $z=0$ on reconstruction and obtain the four private bits by DA23-A's formula, checking both signed NAE owners per forbidden word. Actual guards on phase or private bits must be honored separately, not silently projected away. High-occurrence XOR variables are not covered by this rail compiler.
\end{proof}

\section{DR23: Robust nonlinear bundle lift and authenticated quotient escape}\label{sec:dr23}
\begin{lemma}[Uniform low-rank guard robustness]\label{lem:dr23-robust}
Fix integers $k,w\ge1$. For every explicitly encoded Boolean CSP $F$ of arity at most $w$, replace each bit by a disjoint bundle of $L=2k+1$ bits and decode by majority $M$. Each source owner is replaced by the list of full-word forbidden packets on its physical scope, rejecting exactly when its decoded source tuple is rejected. The construction uses at most $m2^{Lw}$ packets, $Ln$ variables, and polynomial encoded length and bit work. For every consistent affine physical guard $Ay=b$ of rank $r\le k$ and every source word $x$, its majority fiber intersects the guard. Thus the guarded compiled problem projects exactly onto the source solution set.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Start with the repeated-bit lift $y_0$ of $x$. Since the guard is consistent, solve $A\delta=b+Ay_0$ using $r$ independent columns of $A$, setting other coordinates of $\delta$ to zero. At most $r\le k$ bits are flipped, so every majority is unchanged. Gaussian elimination and direct source/guard verification are polynomial. Without guards each source word has $2^{2kn}$ preimages by complement symmetry of the odd majority. The fixed-$k,w$ packet enumeration and source map are paid; no bound uniform in increasing $k$ is asserted.
\end{proof}
For any satisfiable source subregistry, its physical model set has full affine hull (one repeated model and each single-bit flip). If the source is inclusion-minimal UNSAT with $m$ owners, every packet collection supported in fewer than $m$ original owners is satisfiable under every consistent rank-$\le k$ guard, and under rank-$<k$ guards has no new necessary affine equation: an independent equation can be contradicted by extending the guard by one row. This holds for dense affine recodings. Connected odd-charge graph Tseitin has arbitrarily many critical vertex rows (the only row dependency is their sum). In particular this fixed-width linear-packet-size lift strengthens the type of guard robustness in DO15 without a Cartesian product of owners. Both consistent children of any affine split within rank $k$ retain the entire source solution set; a positive credit depending only on the unchanged quotient cannot satisfy strict aggregate contraction for that split. This is neither an arbitrary-potential obstruction nor a lower bound for algorithms recognizing the nonlinear quotient. Count equality under guards is not claimed.
\begin{lemma}[Strict moment lift beyond proper affine-block extraction]\label{lem:dr23-moment}
Conditional on the underlying relative-edge pseudoexpectation construction in Lemma~\ref{lem:da23-moment}, the majority-three lift of odd-charge cubic expander Tseitin is an UNSAT rank-nine packet family with a real degree-$\Omega(v)$ pseudoexpectation, zero distinct physical pair correlations, and no nontrivial affine deduction from any proper collection of source vertex blocks.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For each edge independently choose a random spin triple $R_e$ uniformly from words with at most one negative spin. Set $Y_{ej}=X_eR_{ej}$ where $X_e$ is the original relative-edge spin. The majority of the triple is $X_e$. For fixed $R$, substitution preserves Boolean identities and never increases monomial degree; averaging the underlying pseudoexpectation over $R$ preserves normalization and positivity on degree-eligible squares. For each rank-nine violation indicator times an eligible monomial, the relative support lies within the vertex star and at most $D-9$ other edges; the genuine local affine law on at most $D$ edges from DA23 enforces the charge, making the product zero. Distinct edges have zero correlation in DA23; distinct coordinates of one $R_e$ have zero pair correlation by its four-word uniform law. Hence all distinct physical pairs have zero correlation. Every proper collection of vertex rows is solvable and the preceding lemma gives full affine hull. This transfer is to rank-nine avoidance packets, not DA22's quadratic ternary NAE domain or strict physical tetravalence. No new independent proof of DA23's underlying expansion lemma is claimed.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Recognizable nonlinear quotient]\label{lem:dr23-quotient}
For these explicit full-word registries with distinct source scopes and distinct source-variable incidence signatures, there is a polynomially discoverable exact majority quotient, with paid reverse lift for empty or consistent rank-$\le k$ physical guards. In the graph parity case this gives a complete polynomial decision terminal.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Group and deduplicate packets by actual scope, collect variables with identical incidence signatures over grouped scopes, verify classes of size $L$, that scopes are unions of these classes and have size at most $Lw$. Enumerate each constant-size truth table and verify it is constant on every fiber of its tuple of majority labels. This certifies the exact quotient conjunction and accounts for every packet. For graph parity, verify each recovered relation is one parity equation, then use Gaussian elimination and Lemma~\ref{lem:dr23-robust} for reconstruction. Arbitrary recovered CSPs still require paid source solving. Reject/decline failed recognition or higher-rank guards unless separately handled. Do not assume source signatures distinct universally, discard an arbitrary guard, or reset the original-$N$ reserve. Discovery, all failed tests, exact table checks, closure and lift are charged; on the graph domain serial polynomial time/space give $CM\le(T+1)S$. The odd-charge family is therefore not a simultaneous portfolio obstruction.
\end{proof}

\section{Exact parity closure of regular optimal faces (M29)}\label{sec:m29}
This strengthens the paid affine closure consumer of Lemma~\ref{lem:m28-reg}; it does not prove universal progress (Obligation~\ref{obl:progress}).
\begin{lemma}[Binary affine hull of a TU optimal face]\label{lem:m29-tu}
Let $D$ be totally unimodular with $d$ columns, $b$ integral, and $P=\{z\in[0,1]^d:Dz=b\}$ nonempty. Let $F$ be the face minimizing a rational linear objective, $z_0$ an integral optimal vertex, and $J$ the coordinates taking both values zero and one on optimal vertices. Then
\[
\operatorname{aff}_{\mathbb F_2}(F\cap\{0,1\}^d)
=z_0+\{h:\operatorname{supp}(h)\subseteq J,\ D_Jh_J=0\bmod 2\}.
\]
This hull and, optionally, polynomially many actual optimum vertices spanning it are uniformly computable in polynomial bit time.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Exact rational LP and paid vertex selection acquire $z_0$ and the coordinate extrema on $F$. LP duality expresses $F$ by imposing bound equalities on $P$, hence imposing all fixed coordinates suffices. Inclusion forward is immediate. Choose a full-rank square minor of $D_J$; its determinant is $\pm1$. Fundamental integer kernel vectors have nonpivot entries forming standard unit vectors, pivot entries in $\{0,\pm1\}$ by Cramer's rule and TU. Their reductions span the binary kernel. For nonempty $J$, sum $k\le2d$ integral optima realizing both extrema for each free coordinate into $a$. Every free coordinate lies between $1$ and $k-1$. For every fundamental vector $h$, both $a$ and $a+h$ are integer points of $kF$. Every such point $s$ decomposes into $k$ integral points of $F$: choose an integral point in $F$ with additional bounds $\max(0,s_i-(k-1))\le z_i\le\min(1,s_i)$, feasible fractionally via $s/k$ and integral by TU. Then $s-z\in(k-1)F$; induct. Thus $h$ is a difference of sums of actual optimal vertices. Modulo two it lies in the span of their differences from $z_0$. Empty $J$ is immediate. All arithmetic, at most $O(d^2)$ decomposition LPs plus polynomial vertex-extraction overhead, witnesses and kernel computations are polynomial in encoded length. This is a direct TU integer decomposition argument, cf.\ Gijswijt (\url{https://doi.org/10.1137/S089548010343569X}).
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Complete affine identities of regular syndrome optima]\label{lem:m29-syn}
Under Lemma~\ref{lem:m28-reg}, all valid affine binary identities on minimum-weight feasible words are obtainable uniformly in polynomial time, without enumerating all optimum words. In particular, for the cardinality-only objective and a feasible tagged perfect matching, this gives the complete affine hull of all compatible matchings.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Use $D=[B_E,-B_E]$, $b=-B_*$ and the objective $w^\top(u+v)$. Every optimum binary word, together with the distinguished target column, is a binary cycle. Decompose it into disjoint circuits and orient their signed TU dependencies (entries $\pm1$) with sign $+1$ on the target; this constructs an integral split optimum of equal cost, including zero-cost cycles and the zero-target loop. Conversely the linear binary image $u+v\bmod2$ of an integral split optimum is feasible with cost no larger and hence optimal. Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:m29-tu} and project its binary hull; orthogonal complement gives every affine identity. A secondary weight objective would restrict identities to weighted optima, not all compatible matchings. A certified source map is required for any further feedback. An affine hull is not exact support: three parallel unit-cost edges with target odd endpoints have optimal words $100,010,001$, whose affine hull contains the nonoptimal $111$. Retain guards and reclose after every accepted deduction; independent affine rank increases are bounded by the number of chart variables. Charge recognition, unsuccessful probes, exact LP, verification, basis witnesses, provenance and lifts; the same serial realization has polynomial $T,S$ on this domain and $CM\le(T+1)S$. No semantic closure oracle, count claim, universal regularity or universal dispatch follows.
\end{proof}

\section{BD23: Signed balanced-deletion normalization and complete optimal affine feedback}\label{sec:bd23}
Attack Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} by combining M28's exact signed mismatch energy, M29's optimum affine hull, DA22's guard-specific feedback and GD30's charged composition. This is an exact declining dispatch, not a universal normalization proof.
\begin{lemma}[Paid signed balanced-deletion discovery]\label{lem:bd23-mod}
For a loopless graph with binary preferred edge parities $p_e$ and positive binary-encoded weights, a set $X$ is a balanced-deletion modulator if $G-X$ admits all its preferred edge equations. For a given integer cap $k$, such an $X$ of size at most $k$ can be found, or its nonexistence certified, deterministically in $3^k\operatorname{poly}(N)$ bit time and polynomial peak space.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Use vertex-prefix iterative compression, as in the unsigned odd-cycle transversal method of Reed--Smith--Vetta (\url{https://doi.org/10.1016/j.orl.2003.10.009}). After adding a vertex the prior modulator plus that vertex is a modulator of size at most $k+1$. If compression is necessary, enumerate each old modulator vertex as deleted, kept at zero, or kept at one. Reject incompatible edges within the kept old vertices. The graph outside the old modulator admits a BFS-acquired gauge making every remaining edge require equality. The kept old vertices impose binary demands on their outside neighbors in this gauge. A feasible additional deletion is exactly a vertex separator of the two demand classes, including vertices with both demands. Split each outside vertex into input and output with unit-capacity arc, replace each undirected edge by opposite directed output-to-input arcs of capacity $n+1$, and attach demand-zero inputs to a source and demand-one outputs to a sink at capacity $n+1$. A cut of capacity at most $k$ minus the already-deleted count uses only split arcs and precisely separates the demands. Conversely a valid deletion gives such a cut; surviving components take their demanded value or an arbitrary value if undemanded. Every possible new modulator with a balancing assignment appears in an enumerated old-vertex mode. Verify the returned set by parity BFS. Failure on a prefix excludes a size-$k$ modulator for the entire graph, not SAT. Each prefix has at most $3^{k+1}$ modes and polynomial exact maxflow work; serial enumeration and all failed attempts are charged.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Exact signed optimum and entire optimum affine hull]\label{lem:bd23-hull}
Given a verified balanced-deletion modulator $X$ of size $k$, the minimum weighted mismatch, a minimizing assignment, and the complete binary affine hull of all minimizing assignments are uniformly obtainable in $2^k\operatorname{poly}(N)$ bit time and polynomial peak space. In particular the procedure does not require regularity of the target-augmented cographic matroid.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For each of the $2^k$ actual assignments of $X$, account for internal mismatches as a constant. Gauge the remaining graph to equality penalties. Edges to fixed vertices of $X$ contribute unary nonnegative costs, encoded by arcs to source or sink; each equality penalty is an undirected capacity. An exact minimum cut gives the optimal value in the mode. For a maximum flow let $S_0$ be the residual source-reachable set and $T_0$ the vertices that reach the sink. All minimum source sets are precisely residual-forward-closed sets containing the source and excluding the sink, by flow conservation and saturation of the cut (Picard--Queyranne, \url{https://doi.org/10.1007/BFb0120902}). Each $S_0\cup\operatorname{reach}(v)$ for $v\notin S_0\cup T_0$ is another optimal source set. Their differences from $S_0$ span the free residual strongly connected component indicators: in reverse topological order of the condensation, subtract the indicators of the strict successors from a reachability vector over $\mathbb F_2$. Every other optimum cut differs from $S_0$ by a union of these free components, giving exactness of the affine hull. Each mode thus supplies at most $n+1$ actual optimal assignments spanning its hull. Undo the gauge and retain the actual mode values. Keep only globally minimum modes, adding both their internal differences and the differences of their anchors to one Gaussian span; a lower discovered value resets that span, with all past work charged. No inference valid solely in a single mode is applied unconditionally.
\end{proof}
For signed NAE after actual pair-parity guards, perform certified repeated-component closure first; quotient by the resulting pair equations, retain constant loop and opposite-parallel-edge costs, and use the exact M28 mismatch identity $m+2\,\#\mathrm{violations}$. A minimum of $m$ gives a source witness and the entire affine hull of satisfying words; a larger minimum refutes this guard. Transport hull directions and anchors through the actual affine source lift. Necessary equations are guard-relative and can feed other terminals, with immediate reclosure. This does not handle an arbitrary external affine or nonlinear guard without a separate exact adapter. A fixed cap $k\le c\log_2(N+2)$, with original input length $N$ and fixed $c$, gives a deterministic polynomial serial reserve for discovery, all flow modes, binary arithmetic, hull acquisition, verification, source reconstruction, failed caps and at most $n$ strict affine rank increases with reclosure. On the same serial realization $T,S$ are polynomial and $CM\le(T+1)S$. No unbounded fallback occurrences are paid.
\begin{lemma}[Nonregular escape and raw simultaneous obstruction]\label{lem:bd23-obstruction}
There are connected graphs with nonregular augmented cographic target, arbitrarily large minimum mismatch, but a balanced-deletion modulator of size two. Conversely the raw S27 high-cut-rank opposite-label complete-pair registries of Lemma~\ref{lem:s27-cut} require a balanced-deletion modulator of linear size.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Glue $b$ all-inequality $K_4$ blocks along a common edge, otherwise disjoint. The M28-Fano minor is present. Deleting the two shared endpoints leaves $b$ disjoint single edges. The optimal mismatch is $\min(b+1,2b)=b+1$: equal shared endpoints pay one common mismatch and at least one per private pair, while distinct shared endpoints pay at least two per block; both bounds are attained. For S27, if the balanced induced remainder has at least $2\lceil n/4\rceil$ vertices, choose two disjoint subsets each of size $\lceil n/4\rceil$. Consistency of all pair preferences on this remainder makes their cross-sign matrix a rank-one outer product of vertex signs, contradicting Lemma~\ref{lem:s27-cut} for sufficiently large $n$. Thus $|X|>n-2\lceil n/4\rceil$. This excludes a universal logarithmic raw modulator even for opposite labels, not other source encodings, nonlocal nonlinear transformations, post-cut residuals or unrestricted decision.
\end{proof}
