\section{Proper-group zero-target hardness on a known-SAT ambient chart (I29)}
\label{sec:i29}
\begin{theorem}[Target-only acquisition is NP-complete even on a positive SAT ambient chart]\label{thm:i29}
In RT28's relative-slot quotient, deciding $0\in\sum_{i\in J}\pi(T_i)$ is NP-complete even for a specified proper group $J$ of a connected positive linear tripartite NAE hypergraph of bounded occurrence and minimum owner cut at least eight, with an explicit ambient satisfying assignment supplied.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Use the positive linear degree-four NAE-3SAT hardness of Darmann, D\"ocker and Dorn (arXiv:2412.03395). Connect its components by neutral triples on consecutive component representatives and a fresh variable per triple: any two endpoints extend, and each representative receives at most two extra occurrences. Order the source owner triples. For each variable $v$ construct three disjoint classes $A_v,B_v,C_v$, each of size $L_v=8\max(1,t_{v,0},t_{v,1},t_{v,2})$, where $t_{v,k}$ counts occurrences in role $k$. Use internal owners $(A_{v,i},B_{v,j},C_{v,i+j\bmod L_v})$ for all $i,j$, none in $J$. For each source triple create eight owners in $J$ with endpoints in its three variable clouds, in their respective roles, using separate dedicated ports for every occurrence and copy. All ambient owners are positive. Every internal pair is unique by the Latin-square construction and every external pair is unique by dedicated ports. The entire graph is tripartite, with supplied ambient SAT word $A=1,B=C=0$, connected and of maximum occurrence at most $49$. Size is linear in the source length in graph objects at the stated degree cap.
 
A cut splitting any cloud cuts at least $L_v$ internal owners: its internal pair graph is $K_{L_v,L_v,L_v}$, and for a smaller side of cardinality $1\le s\le\lfloor3L_v/2\rfloor$ at least $s(2L_v-s+1)\ge2L_v$ pair edges cross. Exactly two pair edges cross per crossing triple. A nontrivial cut consisting of whole clouds crosses at least eight copies of a source owner by connectedness. Thus RT28's mincut hypothesis holds.
 
Let $D$ be the ambient two-bit slot space, $Mx$ the relative observations at all owners, and $\pi:D\to D/\operatorname{im}M$. A tuple supported on $J$ lies in $\ker\pi$ iff it equals $Mx$ with zero relative observations on all internal owners. This is equivalent to $x$ being constant in each connected cloud. Legality on $J$ is then precisely the original source NAE formula on those cloud bits, with every source solution extending. The global complement is the only kernel of $M$. Membership is in NP by supplying the supported tuple and $x$ and checking all slot equations and legal words. All source construction and verification costs are polynomial. The ambient satisfying assignment is not a target witness: the non-$J$ owners are relaxed to zero relative observations in the fiber, not simultaneously required to be legal.
\end{proof}
For a signed source, take a particular $z_0$ supported on $J$ equal there to the source relative forbidden word, and use target $\pi(z_0)$ instead of zero. The same proof with $z=z_0+Mx$ preserves the signed source. Actual source pair guards are imposed on the constant-cloud bits under their own provenance; they are not ambient semantic facts. Each raw target owner on distinct cloud variables has full local affine hull, so singleton affine and pair closure cannot acquire a new equality at the raw root. This does not exclude stronger closure. RT28's exact logarithmic component consumer remains correct but no unconditional polynomial extension to arbitrary target components follows even from known ambient satisfiability, positive signs, or target zero. M29's exact optimum affine hull is not an exact support oracle. This is a polynomial reduction, not an unrestricted time lower bound or an obstruction to a portfolio bypassing such queries. BW23 native compiler transfer was not executed here.
 
The executed checker on BS22/S27 actual source IDs (commit \texttt{0100a1421a264b657dc9b7f3a257dbd07dc06a44}) and separate DA22 first/seven pair guards checked 458558 assertions, 131328 component words, 284 pair-closure scans and 14 physical target lifts. Raw source counts $0/10$ and $0/4$ give target tuple counts $0/5$ and $0/2$; all raw and first-cut cases remain OPEN by local closure, seven cuts reject. All ambient colorings, physical pair uniqueness, complement components and internal cut inequalities checked. Checker and results commits \texttt{5e3402767b1924547eec210b081e0a4fa5a15b38} and \texttt{29ec79566f571c5c001e7d1f33861e7a4966c9ea}. These are finite reference enumeration, not generic quotient Gaussian construction, independent upstream proof replay, native matching, full portfolio or kernel verification. Under a fixed original-input logarithmic component cap, construction, failed recognition, guarded closure, scans, storage, witness verification and lifts are polynomial with same-execution $CM\le(T+1)S$; no universal cap or strict aggregate credit follows. Theorem~\ref{thm:aggregate} remains conditional and Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} OPEN.


\section{Rank-one private fibers and guarded parity coverage (BA23)}\label{sec:ba23}
This attacks Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} using BA22's collectively dependent slot planes, GD30's paid consumers and I29's distinction between ambient words and target words. Point membership, whole-image coverage and existential exterior search are distinct computational tasks.
\begin{lemma}[Exact affine one-bit existential projection]\label{lem:ba23-elim}
After authenticated affine guard parametrization and certified singleton closure, choose one free direction $z$ and complementary coordinates $y$. A forbidden packet touching $z$ has an exact Gaussian description $A_i y=b_i,\ z=\ell_i(y)$ with an affine bit $\ell_i$. Keep all static packets, and replace touching packets by all consistent affine packets
\[
 A_i y=b_i,\quad A_j y=b_j,\quad \ell_i(y)+\ell_j(y)=1\quad (i<j).
\]
The resulting avoidance chart is exactly the existential projection of the original chart onto $y$. With $s$ static and $t$ touching packets the output has at most $s+\binom{t}{2}$ packets; each pair packet has rank at most $r_i+r_j-1$ when its parents have ranks $r_i,r_j$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Gaussian elimination isolates the private bit from every other packet equation. For a fixed exterior word, each activated touching packet excludes exactly one of the two possible bits. Both lifts fail iff a static packet is violated or two activated packets exclude opposite values. The pair equations express precisely that condition. Inconsistent intersections are empty and canonical duplicates may be discarded. For a projected witness test both bits in the archived parent chart and reconstruct the actual guard by Gaussian back-substitution. This is an affine generalization of Davis--Putnam existential elimination, not a universal tractability claim. The formula also applies to a dense direction after a paid invertible basis change.
\end{proof}
For example, take $k\ge3$ independent two-bit slots $(a_i,b_i)$ avoiding $(0,0)$, and quotient their direct sum by the single vector that flips every $b_i$. The images of any two slot planes have trivial intersection (a nonzero kernel vector touches all $k$ slots), but the full family is dependent. In the representative $b_k=0$, the exact projected exclusions are $a_i=a_j=0,\ b_i+b_j=1$. Thus a collective nonaffine fusion requires only quadratically many rank-three packets, despite failure of every BA22 pairwise intersection probe. With an original-$N$ cap $L=(N+2)^a$ on packet counts, each probe costs $O(L^2\operatorname{poly}(N))$ bit operations; scan a basis of at most $n$ candidate directions, charge all failed probes, reclose after each move and retain $O(nL\operatorname{poly}(N))$ archive bits. The potential $1+$ remaining free dimension strictly decreases and there are at most $n$ successful moves. Same-execution time and peak space are polynomial, $CM\le(T+1)S$. No proof that any direction passes the cap on every residual.
\begin{lemma}[Rank-one private-fiber point membership]\label{lem:ba23-fiber}
In coordinates $(y,z)$ with an arbitrary-dimensional private affine parameter space, suppose the private coefficient matrix of every packet has rank at most one after actual guard parametrization. For any supplied exterior word $y$, exact lift existence and a witness (or an inconsistency certificate) are polynomial-time computable.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Rank-zero packets are direct exterior tests. In a rank-one packet row reduction yields exterior activation equations and one private equation $\lambda_i z=\ell_i(y)$. If activated, avoiding the packet requires $\lambda_i z=1+\ell_i(y)$; otherwise no private constraint is imposed. Solve all activated rows simultaneously by Gaussian elimination. Inconsistency has a row-sum certificate. Neither independent activation choices nor all private words are enumerated. Any actual mixed guard must first be parametrized and the rank hypothesis rechecked.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Hard consumers despite polynomial point membership]\label{lem:ba23-consumer}
Full exterior coverage of the rank-one-private-fiber language is coNP-complete, and existence of some liftable exterior word is NP-complete, even with single-literal activations and rank-two avoidance packets after paid closing-parity substitution.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For coverage, reduce 3-CNF $F(y)$ with clauses $C_j$, $j=1,\ldots,m$, $m\ge2$. Introduce $z_0,\ldots,z_m$. For each literal $L$ in $C_j$ require $z_{j-1}+z_j=0$ when $L$ is true, and impose $z_0+z_m=1$. Each implication excludes exactly one rank-two affine packet. Apply the closing parity by Gaussian substitution, leaving private rank one and total rank two. For fixed $y$, active zero edges connect endpoints iff every clause has a true literal. In that case closing parity contradicts connectivity; otherwise assign distinct bits to endpoint components. Consequently no lift exists iff $F(y)$ holds, and full exterior coverage iff $F$ is UNSAT. Noncoverage has a polynomial certificate by the preceding lemma. For existential feasibility instead use a separate private length-three path for each source clause, with zero edge activated iff the corresponding literal is false, and opposite parity between the endpoints. This path has a lift exactly when at least one activation is absent, i.e.\ the clause is true. The disjoint paths therefore project exactly onto the source satisfying set. Substituting the closing parities leaves rank-two packets and no singleton deductions. The construction, lifts and verification are uniform polynomial. Neither reduction establishes an unrestricted lower bound or excludes a solver bypassing these consumer tasks.
\end{proof}
\paragraph{Executed scope.} Immutable BS22 source checker \texttt{0100a1421a264b657dc9b7f3a257dbd07dc06a44}, actual S27 owner IDs and separate raw/first/all-seven DA22 guards. At nominal cap 1024, singleton closure plus minimum projected packet count over coordinate directions decides n7 raw root/neighbor (counts 0/10; moves 5/4; peak 8/7; SAT witness 7); n15 raw (0/4) OPEN after four moves (peak 407/404), first-cut OPEN (321), seven-cut UNSAT by initial closure. 100 seeded mixed controls 76 SAT/24 UNSAT; finite one-bit projection reference checks and actual source lifts, 84379 assertions, 1692288 Gaussian acquisitions, 1052 closure scans, 245369 pair probes, 1053 direction probes, 38 cap declines, 221552 reference words, 108 lifts. Active path coverage criterion checked against original source truth, not an independent general Gaussian fiber backend. Checker uses finite 32-bit masks. No independent DA22 cut acquisition, native reconstruction, whole portfolio/kernel or measured physical CM. \section{DS23: Exact signed three-boundary contraction and cooperative escape}\label{sec:ds23}
Attack Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} by combining BD23's paid signed balanced-deletion consumer, M28's NAE mismatch identity, DS21 exact energy projection, BS22 decomposition and actual pair-guard closure. This is a declining exact graph dispatch, not universal progress.
\begin{lemma}[Exact bounded-boundary signed component contraction]\label{lem:ds23-contract}
Let a signed graph have objective $K+\sum_e w_e [x_u\oplus x_v\ne p_e]$ with explicitly encoded nonnegative rational weights. Let $C$ be a nonempty component after deleting at most three vertices, with actual exterior neighborhood $B$. If $G[C]$ has a balanced-deletion modulator of size at most $k$, a uniformly acquired signed quadratic on $B$ replaces $C$ and all incident edges, preserving the exact minimum conditional on every exterior word. Acquisition costs $3^k\operatorname{poly}(N)$, including up to $8\cdot 2^k$ local flow modes and witness records. A supplied or acquired actual pair-parity guard may first be quotiented; arbitrary dense affine or nonlinear guards and absolute pins are not covered.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Include all edges incident to $C$ in the local objective, leaving exterior-only edges unchanged. Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:bd23-mod} to $G[C]$. In each actual boundary word $b$ and each modulator mode, gauge the remaining interior to equality penalties, as in Lemma~\ref{lem:bd23-hull}; boundary edges become unary costs, so exact mincut obtains the local optimum. Minimize across modes and store one actual interior witness per $b$. If $f(b)$ is the local minimum, simultaneous global complement gives $f(b)=f(\bar b)$. In its Walsh expansion on at most three Boolean coordinates every odd-degree coefficient vanishes, so only constant and pair terms remain. For each pair coefficient $c_{ij}=2^{-|B|}\sum_b f(b)(-1)^{b_i\oplus b_j}$ use a mismatch edge with weight $2|c_{ij}|$, preferred parity $1$ for $c_{ij}>0$ and $0$ for $c_{ij}<0$, and constant $-|c_{ij}|$. Combine these with the Walsh constant. The replacement is precisely the local minimum for every actual exterior word; the stored boundary-indexed witnesses give both threshold directions and reverse reconstruction. No enumeration of all interior assignments is required. This generalizes the familiar three-leg spin elimination to a paid whole-component mode consumer; cf.\ Boettcher--Davidheiser (\url{https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.77.214432}).
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Paid aggregate contraction]\label{lem:ds23-credit}
With original encoded length $N$, fixed $c$, and cap $k\le c\log_2(N+2)$, all attempts at the preceding rule and BD23, iterated with the certified optimum-necessary closure below, take deterministic polynomial bit time and peak space, with exact reverse lift on completed cases. There are at most $n$ strict contractions or merges. Failure at a fixed point is OPEN.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Enumerate deletion sets of size zero through three and their connected components, computing the actual neighborhood. There are $O(n^4)$ candidate interiors per round. Charge all failed BD23 acquisitions and flow modes. Each accepted contraction removes at least one vertex. Normalize loops and opposite parallel edges into constants, retaining nonnegative mismatch weights; same-sign edges add. Initially, after each transformation, and at stagnation, acquire a feasible graph word, e.g.\ zero, whose mismatch cost without constant is $U$. If any edge has weight $w>U$, every optimum obeys its preferred parity, because all other terms are nonnegative. Merge its endpoints with that parity and record a reverse map, repeating until no such certified equation is found. This is a paid incomplete closure, not all semantic information. Start actual NAE sources with guarded singleton/repeated-component closure; M28's threshold is $m$ (mismatch $=m+2$ times violations). Every SAT word attains this lower bound, so optimum-necessary graph equations preserve SAT. Earlier SAT-necessary source closure need not preserve the original UNSAT optimum; do not claim that stronger identity.
Initially use a common rational denominator of polynomial bit length. Each Walsh computation uses a denominator factor at most eight and the local optimum is between zero and the total incident weight. The absolute total of weights and constants grows at most by a fixed factor per accepted step, so exact rational bit lengths are polynomial after at most $n$ steps. There are at most $O(n^2)$ normalized edges; at most eight boundary-indexed interior witnesses per step, plus maps and temporary flow state. Per-occurrence work and all failed trials are polynomial for the fixed original-$N$ cap; the potential $1+\#\text{active vertices}$ strictly decreases on accepted transformations with one child, and the final lift is polynomial. The same serial realization gives polynomial $T,S$ and $CM\le(T+1)S$. This does not imply the universal hypothesis in Theorem~\ref{thm:aggregate}.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Genuine linear NAE family escaping the global modulator cap]\label{lem:ds23-fano}
For every $q\ge3$ there is a same-scope SAT/UNSAT signed linear NAE pair whose raw mismatch graphs require a balanced-deletion set of size at least $3\binom q2$, yet admit a discoverable polynomial sequence of Lemma~\ref{lem:ds23-contract} with local cap three and final BD23 cap one.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For each pair of $q$ terminals $u,v$, take a fresh positive Fano plane minus line $\{0,1,2\}$, identifying points $0,1$ with $u,v$ and retaining five fresh private vertices. Distinct modules meet in at most one terminal, hence the registry is linear. The retained mismatch graph has an all-inequality private $K_5$ in each module, requiring deletion of at least three private vertices to balance it, disjointly across modules. A $K_q$ minor is present and raw minimum degree is at least four. The six retained clauses can be satisfied exactly when the deleted triple is monochromatic: a coloring satisfying all seven would have precisely seven monochromatic pairs, whereas every two-coloring of seven points has at least nine. Conversely color the deleted triple alike and the other four oppositely. Thus the minimum boundary cost is six when $u=v$ and strictly larger when $u\ne v$. Each five-vertex private region with boundary $\{u,v\}$ is discoverable by enumerating boundary pairs, components and the actual constant-size module pattern. Deleting three of its private vertices balances its interior. Lemma~\ref{lem:ds23-contract} replaces it by a positive equality penalty and constant six, without changing the other modules. Repeat on all modules. The final equality graph is balanced. Flipping the signs of terminal $v$ in all its occurrences in just one module changes that edge preference to inequality, retaining the positive penalty and raw modulator obstruction. For $q\ge3$ it is inconsistent with the remaining equality path; the final modulator has size one, and both labels are exactly decidable. This proves a uniform paid family-specific schedule, not universal success of arbitrary greedy order or absence of other cheap terminals.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Limits of quadratic boundary contraction]\label{lem:ds23-limit}
A balanced unit equality star with four boundary vertices has projected cost $f(b)=\min(|b|,4-|b|)$ whose four-character Walsh coefficient is $1/4$. It cannot be represented exactly by a constant-plus-pair energy on the same four boundary variables. Moreover, for raw complete-pair S27 high-cut-rank families in Lemma~\ref{lem:bd23-obstruction}, every deletion of at most three boundary vertices leaves one connected interior, and adding those boundary vertices to a local balanced-deletion set gives a global set. The raw linear modulator bound therefore also excludes universally logarithmic local modulators for this dispatch. Factored auxiliary consumers and nonlocal post-cut transformations remain eligible; neither fact is an unrestricted lower bound.
\end{lemma}

\section{MS30: Overlap-aware collective syndrome fusion}\label{sec:ms30}
Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} remains OPEN. Strengthen MS29's kernel-fiber density bound, preserving the actual syndrome interface and guard. The probability inequality is the classical Hunter spanning-tree bound; the application below gives a uniform full-support certificate and paid reverse reconstruction, not a general SAT algorithm.
\begin{lemma}[Forest overlap certificate and deterministic lift]\label{lem:ms30-forest}
For explicit punctured affine tables $T_i=(a_i+U_i)\setminus\{h_i\}$ (holes optional), let $K$ be the kernel of the summation map on direct-sum local coefficients. For a target in the affine sum let $B_i$ be the event that local value $i$ equals its hole on the uniform affine fiber $c+K$. If a forest $F$ on punctured owners satisfies
\[
 \beta_t=\sum_i\Pr(B_i)-\sum_{ij\in F}\Pr(B_i\cap B_j)<1,
\]
a legal target decomposition can be found in deterministic polynomial bit time. The best forest for this bound is obtained by maximum-weight spanning forest with edge weights $\Pr(B_i\cap B_j)$. Failure of the strict inequality is a decline, not UNSAT.

Write $r_i,r_{ij}$ for the ranks of one/two-block projections of $K$. Use $\Pr(B_i)\le 2^{-r_i}$ and set $w_{ij}=2^{-r_{ij}}$ if $\sum_{\ell\notin\{i,j\}}U_\ell=\sum_\ell U_\ell$, else $w_{ij}=0$. If a maximum-weight forest on these uniform weights satisfies
\[
 \beta=\sum_{i:\,h_i\text{ exists}}2^{-r_i}-\sum_{ij\in F}w_{ij}<1,
\]
then the exact sum of the tables is their full affine sum, with a polynomial reverse lift for every target.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For each point of the fiber, $Q=\sum_i1_{B_i}-\sum_{ij\in F}1_{B_i}1_{B_j}$ counts connected components of the induced forest on violated owners. It is a nonnegative integer and zero exactly when no hole is selected. Thus $\Pr(\bigcup_iB_i)\le {\mathbb E}Q$. Each event or pair intersection is a linear system on kernel coordinates; probability is zero if inconsistent, otherwise $2^{-r}$ for its rank $r$. With the forest fixed, successively fix free kernel bits, choosing the child of no larger conditional expectation (the two children have equal measure). Compute both conditional values exactly with the same linear tests. At the end $Q<1$ and hence $Q=0$. Replay all local values and the target. The complement-span equality ensures that assigning the two holes leaves a feasible decomposition for every target in the affine hull; hence the stated intersection probability is exact on every fiber. Otherwise zero is a valid lower bound. The uniform certificate implies the target-specific one with the same forest. No target enumeration is needed.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Strict gain and a forest-certification obstruction]\label{lem:ms30-field}
For $q=2^r$, $r\ge3$, take the $q$ spaces $U_t=\{(x,tx,t^2x):x\in\mathbb F_q\}$ in $\mathbb F_q^3$, punctured at zero, viewed as binary spaces. The full MS29 union bound equals one, every pair and triple is independent, but the uniform forest certificate is $1-(q-1)/q^2<1$. For $q=4$, add the space $U_\infty=\{(0,0,x)\}$. Every subgroup fails the uniform forest criterion, and the full target-specific forest bound equals one for every target even though some targets are feasible.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Any three finite columns form an invertible Vandermonde matrix; the same holds with the infinity column and two distinct finite columns. In the first construction, deleting any two leaves at least three spaces spanning the ambient space, so $r_i=r$, $r_{ij}=2r$, and the forest subtracts $(q-1)/q^2$. This is a strict improvement over MS29's full-plus-triple search policy, not necessarily a search of all intermediate groups. In the five-space case, groups of size at most three are independent; groups of four have kernel dimension two over $\mathbb F_2$, density one, and no uniform pair credit because two remaining spaces cannot span the rank-six ambient space. The full five have $\beta=5/4-4/16=1$; all single and pair hole events have the same probabilities on every target fiber. At target zero the kernel has dimension two over $\mathbb F_4$. The five nonzero coordinate functionals have distinct one-dimensional kernels by pair projection surjectivity; their five lines cover the kernel, so zero is impossible. A feasible target exists by choosing any nonzero coefficient per table. No claim about other methods or unrestricted complexity follows.
\end{proof}
\paragraph{Charged integration.}
For $m$ tables there are $O(m^2)$ pair projection/complement-span Gaussian tests, polynomial bit dyadic arithmetic and forest selection. Conditional lift has at most $\sum_i\dim U_i$ bit steps and $O(m)$ linear event tests per step. In an explicit original-$N$ polynomially capped chart, testing full and all triple groups is polynomial per sweep. Every accepted full-support fusion of group $J$ decreases MS29's $\Phi=1+m+\sum_i\dim U_i$ by $|J|-1+\dim K_J$. The admitted serial execution has polynomial $T,S$ and $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$, but no universal progress follows, nor any permission to treat a conditional target witness as a full-support fusion.

\section{RT29: signed optimum-signature contraction}
\label{sec:rt29}
\begin{lemma}[Exact signed boundary mimicking by optimum signatures]
Let an explicit signed mismatch-energy graph have nonnegative rational weights and no absolute pins or unaccounted nonlinear guards. For a region $C$ with actual boundary $B$, $b=|B|\ge1$, let $x^j$ be a paid exact minimizing word for each of the $q=2^{b-1}$ boundary words with first coordinate zero, including all edges incident to $C$. Then an exact signed quadratic replacement with at most $2^{q-1}$ active vertices including $B$ exists, and is constructible from these words in polynomial time in their total length. It preserves each boundary minimum and permits explicit reverse lifting.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Give vertex $v$ signature $(x_v^j+x_v^0)_{j=0}^{q-1}$ over $\mathbb F_2$. Group equal signatures and choose a representative $r$ in each group, preferring a boundary vertex. Distinct boundary vertices have distinct signatures, since all representative boundary words occur. Substitute $x_v=y_r+x_v^0+x_r^0$, adjusting edge signs, absorbing loops and normalizing opposite parallel edges. Each chosen minimizing word and its complement obey these relations. For each boundary word the resulting optimization is a restriction of the original and contains an original minimizer, so the two minima coincide. Lift by substitution. The first signature coordinate is zero, giving the claimed bound. These chosen relations are optimum-preserving restrictions, NOT necessary equations on every feasible or optimal word. They cannot be exported as unconditional deductions or reused under arbitrary later guards.
\end{proof}
For $b=0$ one paid optimum solves the detached region. Given a local balanced-deletion modulator of size $k$ (BD23), at most $2^{b-1+k}$ exact mincut modes acquire the witnesses, with gauges and fixed boundary/deletion vertices charged. Thus the method is polynomial under fixed $b+k\le c\log_2(N+2)$ and polynomial candidate discovery. Enumerating all boundary sets is polynomial only for fixed boundary width, not automatically for growing width. Actual signature grouping never enumerates all possible signatures. Accept only strict active-vertex decrease; it is guaranteed if $|C|+b>2^{2^{b-1}-1}$. In at most $n$ accepted reductions, fixed-width boundary discovery, all failed probes, exact rational arithmetic, source/guard verification, closure and reverse maps are polynomial in original $N$ on this restricted dispatch. Total absolute nonnegative weights do not increase by signed substitution and normalization (absorb constants separately); common denominators and stored lifts are polynomial. Same-realization $CM\le(T+1)S$. Reclose initially, after accepted restrictions and at stagnation; SAT-necessary source closure may change nonzero raw optimum but preserves the decision threshold. Decline if actual guards are not covered. Universal acquisition is open.
\begin{lemma}[Four-port complementary signed-graph family]
For $t\ge5$ terminals attach a disjoint private triangle to each four-subset of terminals: equality edges $ab,bc$ of weight three, inequality $ac$ of weight one, and all twelve unit equality attachments from its three private vertices to its four terminals. The raw balanced-deletion modulator is at least $\binom t4$, and deletion of at most three vertices leaves a connected graph. Nevertheless local signature contraction with $b=4,k=1$ followed by a global balanced consumer solves the threshold $\binom t4$. Reversing all three attachment signs to one terminal in one module gives an opposite-label graph on identical scopes, solved by the same contraction and a final modulator of size one.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Each disjoint frustrated triangle needs at least one deletion. After at most three deletions each surviving private vertex retains a terminal neighbor, and each surviving terminal pair has at least $3\binom{t-2}{2}$ internally disjoint two-edge paths. Thus the standalone DS23 at-most-three-boundary dispatch cannot peel a proper component, and its large interior requires a large modulator. The all-zero bound is at least $\binom t4>3$, so no raw edge is dominant by the DS23 rule. If the boundary has Hamming weight $h$, each private vertex pays at least $\min(h,4-h)$ externally; uniform private bits attain this bound and internal cost one, whereas a nonuniform triangle pays at least three internally. All local minima therefore have uniform private bits. Signature contraction gives a single auxiliary center with weight-three attachments and constant one. Its projected four-character coefficient is $3/4$, so direct boundary-only quadratic projection is impossible. Enumerating four-sets and their components finds the modules in polynomial time. The quotient has $t+\binom t4$ vertices, originally $t+3\binom t4$. The unmodified graph is balanced after contraction. The flipped module has the same formula with one boundary coordinate complemented; other modules force all terminals equal at threshold, which conflicts with the flipped module. Uniform terminals attain threshold plus three, and every nonzero boundary penalty is at least three. Deleting the flipped terminal balances the quotient. This is strict complementarity versus the specified standalone dispatches, not an unrestricted hardness claim, a strict native source compiler, or a general greedy-order theorem.
\end{proof}

\section{Exact critical-density affine hole fusion (BH23)}\label{sec:bh23}
\begin{lemma}[Cactus-corrected affine avoidance]\label{lem:bh23-cactus}
On a consistent affine guard $G$ over $\mathbb F_2$, let $E_i$ be the forbidden affine events and $H$ a supplied simple cactus graph on their identities. Put
\[
Q(x)=\sum_i1_{E_i}(x)-\sum_{ij\in E(H)}1_{E_i\cap E_j}(x)
+\sum_{C\text{ simple cycle of }H}1_{\cap_{i\in V(C)}E_i}(x).
\]
Then $Q$ is nonnegative integer-valued and zero exactly on accepting words. If $\mathbb E_G Q<1$, deterministic polynomial witness acquisition follows.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The induced graph on violated owners is again a cactus. Its cycle rank is exactly the number of simple cycles retained in full. The displayed expression is therefore its connected-component count, including isolated vertices. A cactus has linearly many edges and cycles, whose lists can be obtained by block decomposition and verified by checking that each block is an edge or a simple cycle. Every term, including an arbitrarily long cycle intersection, is one affine linear system. Gaussian elimination evaluates the exact dyadic expectation, also under an additional coordinate pin. The current expectation is the weighted average of the nonempty pinned fibers; retain a nonempty fiber of expectation below one, and repeat until a complete word remains. Its integer component count must be zero. Discovery of the fixed full cycle and maximum-weight tree is polynomial; optimal cactus search is not assumed. Charge every rank, pin, bit operation and source verification. Failure of a strict bound alone is OPEN.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Exact critical-density cover and uniform fusion]\label{lem:bh23-critical}
Suppose $q=2^r$, $r\ge1$, and there are exactly $q+1$ holes, each of codimension $r$ within $G$, with each pair of linear observations having joint rank $2r$. Avoidance is UNSAT if and only if the full affine intersection is nonempty of codimension $2r$. Otherwise the full-cycle certificate gives a polynomial constructive SAT lift. Every strict tree certificate declines.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
All single and pair probabilities are respectively $1/q$ and $1/q^2$, independent of their offsets. The full cycle gives $B=1-q^{-2}+\Pr_G(\cap_iE_i)\le1$. If the intersection is inconsistent or has rank greater than $2r$, the strict inequality gives the witness by Lemma~\ref{lem:bh23-cactus}. Otherwise the full intersection has size $|G|/q^2$; it is contained in every pair intersection of the same size, so they are equal. The union consists of this common core and disjoint remainders, of size $|G|/q^2+(q+1)(|G|/q-|G|/q^2)=|G|$. The maximum-weight tree has $q$ edges and expectation exactly one. All eligibility tests and the simultaneous intersection cost polynomial in explicit input length, not in the number of possible subsets.
For a group of punctured affine tables use the kernel of the sum map as linear direction of the target fiber. The single, pair and full observation ranks are independent of the target; apply the preceding criterion to each target in the affine sum. Full rank above $2r$ gives uniform full support. At full rank $2r$ the excluded targets are exactly the affine image of the coefficient slice fixing all hole blocks; compute this image by elimination. When all tables are punctured with one hole each, the slice is a single coefficient vector, hence the group is replaced exactly by a full or single-hole affine sum. If unpunctured blocks are present the excluded affine image need not be a point; keep the general packet. The pure group replacement strictly decreases $1+\#\text{tables}+\sum_i\dim U_i$ since sum dimension is at most the sum of input dimensions. Reverse lifts use actual target and paid conditional expectation. This is a uniform exact rule on the entire admitted group, not just certification of one target. Original-$N$ caps apply. The whole registry and polynomially listed groups can be tested; arbitrary subset discovery or universal applicability is not established.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Raw linear NAE cactus barrier]\label{lem:bh23-obstruction}
For an unguarded linear signed NAE-3 registry of $m\ge6$ owners, every simple cactus correction has expectation greater than one, regardless of signs or chosen cactus.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Every single and distinct pair violation probability is $1/4$ and $1/16$ by linearity of the hypergraph (at most one shared variable). A cactus has at most $3(m-1)/2$ edges, as every cycle adds at least two new vertices per extra cycle edge above a spanning forest. All cycle terms are nonnegative. Thus $\mathbb E Q\ge m/4-3(m-1)/32=(5m+3)/32>1$. This defeats the restricted raw certificate even using arbitrary long intersections, not nonlocal transformations, affine guards or unrestricted algorithms. It applies to DO01 opposite labels alike.
\end{proof}

\section{BS23: compressed affine intersection counts and their limit}\label{sec:bs23}
\begin{lemma}[Paid signed intersection dictionary]\label{lem:bs23-map}
Let $G$ be the actual affine guard and $E_1,\ldots,E_m$ forbidden affine events on $n$ Boolean coordinates. Maintain a dictionary of nonempty canonical affine systems with integer coefficients, initially $c_G=1$ (an inconsistent guard rejects). On processing $E_i$, copy the dictionary and for every old entry $A$ subtract $c_A$ from the key $A\cap E_i$, skipping inconsistent intersections; erase zero coefficients. Then
\[
1_G\prod_{i=1}^j(1-1_{E_i})=\sum_A c_A1_A
\]
after step $j$. For an arbitrary additional affine guard $H$, exact count equals $\sum_{A:A\cap H\ne\varnothing}c_A2^{n-\operatorname{rank}(A\cap H)}$. This supplies both decision directions, coordinate self-reduction and source verification, and a paid complete affine hull on the admitted domain.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Multiply the current indicator identity by $1-1_{E_i}$ and use $1_A1_E=1_{A\cap E}$. Canonical augmented RREF tests equality and consistency of affine flats; no semantic equivalence oracle is needed. Integrate the identity over the actual guard $H$. For a positive count, query each coordinate pin and retain a positive-count branch. For the hull, start with a model and compute a basis of equations defining the span of the models already acquired. Query each complementary equation; a positive count supplies a witness outside that span and increases its dimension. When all are zero the span is exactly the affine hull. At most $n+1$ rounds and $O(n^2)$ count queries plus polynomially many witness queries suffice. Export only guard-valid equations and repeat certified closure after accepted deductions.
\end{proof}
Impose a fixed original-$N$ cap $B=(N+2)^c$ during dictionary construction, including intermediate insertions. Each coefficient has $O(m+1)$ bits by the subset expansion, and each counting accumulator has $O(m+n+\log(B+1))$ bits. Gaussian elimination, deterministic dictionary lookup (even linear scans), failed probes, verification, guard handling, reconstruction and storage have polynomial aggregate bounds in $N$ on this capped dispatch; same-execution $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$. An aborted map is OPEN, not a decision. Apply certified rank-one closure before building and at stagnation; complete hull is not assumed free. With BS22's exact direct-sum factorization in absorbed guard coordinates, count each independent factor and multiply, including $2^{\dim G-r}$ for invisible directions, where $r$ is the summed observation rank. Gaussian reconstruction combines witnesses. No multiplication across a shared nontrivial separator. This avoids Cartesian enumeration but does not establish universal progress.
\begin{lemma}[All-sign exponential flat-key obstruction]\label{lem:bs23-packing}
A raw linear signed NAE-3 registry with $t$ vertex-disjoint owners has at least $2^t$ nonzero keys in its final signed intersection dictionary, regardless of signs or owner order. In a complete-pair Steiner triple system on $n$ points, $t\ge n/9$ is guaranteed by greedy packing.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For each subset $S$ of the packed owners, their forbidden events intersect in a nonempty flat $A_S$. Within each selected triple its relative bits are fixed; each triple and each unselected vertex has an independent flip bit. Distinct $S$ have distinct flats. Any other owner meets each selected triple in at most one vertex, so its three bits lie in distinct independent flip groups; its forbidden event cannot contain $A_S$. Therefore only the subset $S$ itself contributes to the key $A_S$, with coefficient $(-1)^{|S|}$. With $m=n(n-1)/6$ and vertex degree $d=(n-1)/2$, a greedy packed triple removes at most $3d-2$ owners, so $t\ge m/(3d-2)\ge n/9$. Thus the raw map requires superpolynomial size in the explicit encoded length $O(n^2\log n)$. The bound is on this dictionary, not on arbitrary indicator representations or SAT decision. The raw complete-pair observation space is connected, so unguarded BS22 direct-sum decomposition does not bypass this particular bound; nonlocal cuts and other terminals may.
\end{proof}
\paragraph{Executed evidence.}
Actual BS22/S27 immutable arrays in commit \texttt{0100a1421a264b657dc9b7f3a257dbd07dc06a44}, separate raw/first/seven DA22 guards. n7 root/neighbor counts 0/10 with peak completed map 37/43; n15 root/neighbor/first exact reference 0/4/0, map declines at transient size 12001 under cap12000; seven-cut root rejects by rank-one closure. 100 seeded affine controls (71 SAT, 29 UNSAT), 1263 assertions, 160123 intersections, 502897 row additions, 1526 closure scans, 584 count queries. Greedy packing generator through n255 yields 85 disjoint owners there. No complete hull implementation, upstream DA22 proof replay, full native/portfolio, TeX/kernel or measured CM. \section{Shrinking affine frontier densities and all-order obstruction (DP24)}\label{sec:dp24}
\paragraph{Status.} PROVED scoped; independent review pending. This section targets Obligation~\ref{obl:progress}, not an unrestricted lower bound or closure. It combines DP23/BH23 affine avoidance with GD30 signed transfer and I29 target interfaces.
\begin{lemma}[Exact affine-flat frontier density and reverse lift]\label{lem:dp24-frontier}
Given an explicit ordered affine-hole registry $E_i=\{x:A_ix=b_i\}$, actual affine guard $G$, and linear target $Lx$, let $B_i$ be an independent row basis of the span of $L$ and all observation rows of holes $j>i$. There is a deterministic exact signed-affine density transfer with polynomial bit work and witness reconstruction whenever all intermediate dictionaries fit a fixed polynomial cap in original input length. It can decline otherwise.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Apply certified unconditional closure before transfer, retaining actual guards and source lifts. Inconsistent guard rejects. Write $P_i B_{i-1}=B_i$. The hole $E_i$ is observable on $B_{i-1}$, as an affine flat $H_i$ (possibly empty or full). Let $f_i(y)$ count original guarded words avoiding the first $i$ holes with $B_i x=y$. Represent this nonnegative density as $\sum_X c_X1_X$ with signed integer coefficients and distinct nonempty affine flats. Initially the density is the indicator of $B_0G$ times $2^{\dim G-\dim B_0G}$. For each term replace it by $c_X(1_X-1_{X\cap H_i})$, omitting empty terms; then push along $P_i$. Pushforward of $1_X$ is $2^{\dim X-\dim P_iX}1_{P_iX}$. Canonicalize by affine row reduction and aggregate coefficients, removing zeros. These identities prove the invariant by induction; the final frontier is the target. Counts of any affine restriction are obtained by summing coefficients times exact powers of two for the intersection dimensions.
Given a final word of positive density, reverse the layers: the sum of $f_{i-1}$ on its inverse image under $P_i$ outside $H_i$ is positive. Greedily fix previous frontier bits, evaluating this sum under each pin by two affine intersection counts per term. Nonnegative true densities ensure one positive side. Lift the resulting $B_0x$ in $G$ by Gaussian elimination and verify against original source. No recompilation or new decision query per bit is required. All coefficients have magnitude at most $2^{n+m}$ by expanding the original subset sum and bounding each intersection fiber by $2^n$. Cap every dictionary, including partial accumulation, at $K=(N+2)^c$ for fixed $c$. Each step costs $O(K\operatorname{poly}(N))$ deterministic bit work; forward and reverse cost respectively $O(mK\operatorname{poly}(N))$ and $O(mnK\operatorname{poly}(N))$, storing $O(mK\operatorname{poly}(N))$ bits. Count all failed order probes (polynomially capped), guards, maps, retention, closure, reconstruction and verification. Stage potential $m-i+1$ pays admitted sequential transfers; it does not prove universal admission. Same serial realization gives $CM\le (T+1)S$. Reclose after necessary deductions and at a decline before branching; prefix density is not itself a necessary source deduction.
\end{proof}
\paragraph{Scope.}
This is exact target \emph{count} representation, not automatic cheap universal target support/coverage. If final density is constant plus a polynomial list of point corrections, compare the constant and actual exception counts to discover exact support; a full or singly punctured affine result can be fused with the DP23 original rank-mass reserve. General support compilation remains open. Dropping observations still used by later holes is unsound: holes $x=0,x=1$ versus duplicate $x=0$ have the same individual projected fiber densities on an unrelated variable $y$, but zero versus one accepting $x$ per $y$. The classical complement-count identity for affine arrangements is in Bj\"orner and Ekedahl, \href{https://people.kth.se/~bjorner/files/SAq.pdf}{Subspace arrangements over finite fields}, Prop.~3.2; no novelty is claimed for inclusion-exclusion.
\begin{lemma}[All-order raw signed-affine dictionary obstruction]\label{lem:dp24-all-order}
On projective Steiner triples over the nonzero vectors of $\mathbb F_2^r$, $n=2^r-1$, the specified raw frontier expansion has $2^{\Omega(n^{1/4})}$ distinct nonzero canonical terms at some prefix of every owner ordering, for every literal sign pattern. There are SAT and UNSAT patterns on these same scopes. This statement is restricted to equal-affine-flat aggregation in this exact expansion.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The first $k=\lfloor n/4\rfloor$ owners remove exactly $3k$ edges from the complete pair graph; the suffix remains connected since $3k<n-1$ for sufficiently large $n$. Relative observation rows of the suffix span the complement quotient, so projection to any frontier through this prefix is injective on complement-invariant affine flats (each is a union of global complement cosets). Raw rank-two singleton closure does nothing.
Let $d$ be maximum variable degree within the first $k$ owners. If $d\le\sqrt{k}$ a greedy disjoint matching has at least $k/(3d)$ owners. If $d>\sqrt{k}$ take the $d$ star arms at a maximum-degree variable. Every nonstar owner contained in their vertex union uses three distinct arms: linearity excludes the center and two leaves in a single arm. Choose arms independently with probability $p=\sqrt{d/(3k)}$, then delete one arm for each fully selected nonstar owner. Expected remaining size is at least $dp-kp^3=2dp/3=\Omega(k^{1/4})$. Thus in either case there exists a subset $S$ of at least $\Omega(k^{1/4})$ owners forming a matching or such a star.
For each $J\subseteq S$ the simultaneous signed forbidden equations define a consistent affine flat $X_J$ of rank $2|J|$: disjoint triples or star arms add two independent relative rows each. No other prefix hole is implied by $X_J$. In the matching case any other owner has its vertices in distinct equality components by linearity. In the star case no other owner is entirely in the one nonsingleton component by arm selection and linearity, so it has an independent relative observation. Consequently any subset $T$ of prefix holes with intersection $X_J$ must be contained in $J$, and rank forces $T=J$. In inclusion-exclusion its coefficient is exactly $(-1)^{|J|}$, and frontier projection preserves distinctness and nonzero coefficient, with the uniform complement fiber factor if that direction is dropped. Thus all $2^{|S|}$ terms survive at stage $k$, independently of order or signs. In particular, a fixed polynomial cap in $N=O(n^2\log n)$ cannot cover this dispatch. This is not a lower bound for arbitrary alternative signed representations, nonlinear preprocessing or SAT algorithms.
For positive NAE every legal triple has exactly one same-color pair; the number of same-color pairs in any two-color partition is at least $(n-1)^2/4$, exceeding the number $n(n-1)/6$ of triples for $n>3$. Hence UNSAT for $r\ge3$. Flipping one literal in each triple yields an all-zero satisfying assignment on the same scopes. DP22 rank-one quadratic normalization escapes the all-positive family, so these are not simultaneous whole-portfolio obstructions.
\end{proof}
\paragraph{Executed evidence.}
SAME immutable BH23 checker at \texttt{3d90192dc3ae734db7a3ba5dd7e40c9b2dae7224}, actual S27 source arrays and distinct DA22 guards. Connected NAE sunflower with $p=2,4,8,12$ arms: static intersection terms $2^p$, shrinking frontier peak one, exact counts $2\cdot3^p$, both anchor lifts. 177706 row reductions, 37857 transitions, 63668 projections, 449 closure passes, 65856 assertions, 136616 reference words, 3102 count/lift queries. Small masks and BigInt coefficients; no general row-basis implementation, uniform support backend, upstream certificate replay, asymptotic all-order execution, native/full portfolio, TeX/kernel or measured CM. \section{S29: Selector-masked hull acquisition and the decision/closure firewall}\label{sec:s29}
This addresses U-PROGRESS (Obligation~\ref{obl:progress}), BS23's complete hull consumer (Lemma~\ref{lem:bs23-map}) and the M29 optimum-hull dispatch. A decision terminal must not automatically be charged as complete semantic forced-information closure.
\begin{lemma}[Promised satisfiable, locally full, codimension-one hull acquisition]\label{lem:s29-hull}
Let $F(x)$ be a signed NAE-3 formula on $n$ bits, represented by rank-two forbidden affine packets $E_i$, and let $G$ be an actual consistent affine guard. Add $k+1$ fresh bits $z$, $k\ge2$, and let $p(z)=\sum_j z_j$ over $\mathbb F_2$. Replace $E_i$ by the packet $E_i\cap\{p=1\}$, keeping $G$ exactly. This polynomial construction has a known satisfying word and a known affine basis of models spanning $H=G\times\ker p$. Its solution hull equals $H$ if $F\wedge G$ is unsatisfiable, and $G\times\mathbb F_2^{k+1}$ otherwise. For empty guard, every coordinate projection of size at most $k$ is full in both cases. Recognizing proper hull, even under these promises, is coNP-complete; hence deterministic polynomial complete hull acquisition would imply $\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The exact solution set is
\[
(G\times\ker p)\ \cup\ ((\operatorname{Sol}(F)\cap G)\times\{z:p(z)=1\}).
\]
Gaussian elimination on $G$ constructs a basepoint and affine basis of $H$, all of whose words are models. Relative to the ambient guard $H$ is a hyperplane, so one model outside it makes the hull full. Conversely, absence of such a model is precisely unsatisfiability of $F\wedge G$. On raw inputs an assignment on at most $k$ coordinates leaves a selector bit free; choose it to make $p=0$ and extend arbitrary other coordinates. Each raw packet has rank three, so rank-one packet closure alone gives no deduction. The reduction from NP-complete signed NAE-3 (empty guard) to nonproper hull is uniform, even for fixed $k=2$; general $k$ polynomial in original size is also permitted since the dense parity row is written explicitly. Nonproper hull has a polynomial certificate consisting of a full relative affine basis of checked models, or one outside word with the supplied basis. Hence proper hull is coNP-complete on this promise. If a proper hull exists its only independent extra equation is $p=0$. No literal backbone or bounded-coordinate marginal detects it when $k\ge2$. This is a barrier to demanding complete semantic information, not to deciding these wrapped formulas, which are trivially satisfiable.
\end{proof}
There is a projected signed NAE-3 variant with known optimum zero for the usual sum of violation indicators. Encode selector parity by binary XOR gates (four 3-CNF clauses each), and each gated NAE by two 4-literal disjunctions, split each 4-OR with one private auxiliary into two 3-ORs. A 3-OR on relative bits is NAE4 with a common reference bit $r$; NAE4$(a,b,c,r)$ is equivalent on projection to $\exists t:\mathrm{NAE}(a,b,t)\wedge\mathrm{NAE}(\neg t,c,r)$. Indeed if $a=b$ the first fixes $t=\neg a$, and if $c=r$ the second fixes $t=c$; these conflict exactly when all four inputs agree. Each local auxiliary can be lifted by gate evaluation or constant-size search. Project to original relative source and selector bits; the exact hull dichotomy persists, and a zero-energy witness and projected spanning basis lift in polynomial time. This does not establish the analogous promise on the full auxiliary hull or a strict wheel-only adapter. Any native E4/B4 transfer must use and charge the authenticated adapter and projection.
\begin{lemma}[Paid outside-span consumer]\label{lem:s29-consumer}
Given a checked affine basis of models spanning $H$ within a residual's actual affine guard, a complete hull can be acquired using only exact guarded decision/witness queries, not exact counting. If $H$ has relative codimension one, one outside-hyperplane decision suffices to determine whether it is the complete hull.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Find by Gaussian elimination equations defining $H$ relative to the guard. Query the original residual with the complement of each defining equation separately. A positive result supplies a verified model outside $H$, increasing its dimension; if all reject, every model is in $H$, so its hull is exactly $H$. Repeat at most $d$ rounds for ambient dimension $d$, using $O(d^2)$ affine decision queries and, if necessary, at most $d$ extra coordinate queries to reconstruct each positive witness. A declined query remains OPEN. Closure is paid initially, after guard imposition, after each accepted deduction and at stagnation. In the masked example only a certified rejection of the odd-selector query licenses exporting $p=0$ within $G$. No conditional result is promoted to an unguarded fact.
\end{proof}
If an admitted terminal only needs a single model, it may return the known model immediately instead of demanding the harder hull. For admitted queries, charge all discovery, failed calls, Gaussian elimination, source verification/lifts, consumer access, guards and DAG retention under the original-$N$ cap. Polynomial query count does not give polynomial answer cost. On a serial admitted procedure $T,S$ are polynomial when the individual charged calls are, and $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$. No universal such call bound has been established. U-PROGRESS, universal SEM/CLOSE and unconditional COST remain OPEN.

\section{Disk-planar four-port switching and the dual-matching escape (DO24)}\label{sec:do24}
\begin{lemma}[Paid planar signed-pair terminal with cofacial pins]\label{lem:do24-dual}
Replace each signed NAE-3 owner on distinct actual bits by its three signed literal pair costs, charging one for each equal literal pair. The cost is $m+2V(x)$ where $V$ is the number of violated owners. Given a certified plane embedding of the resulting multigraph, its minimum and an original minimizing word are polynomially computable. The same holds with an actual fixed boundary word on distinct cofacial ports in a disk embedding.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Write preferred pair parity $d_e$ and defect $y_e=x_u+x_v+d_e$ over $\mathbb F_2$. Defects are attainable exactly when their parity around each face equals that of $d$: face cycles span the cycle space, and $y+d$ then integrates along a spanning tree. In the dual graph these defects are precisely $T$-joins for the odd-frustration faces. For nonnegative integer weights, solve a minimum $T$-join by shortest path distances and deterministic minimum-weight perfect matching of the even terminal set. The symmetric difference of matched paths attains the optimum since each $T$-join decomposes into terminal paths and cycles. Bridges contribute twice to the face parity and can be satisfied independently; handle connected components separately. Reconstruct actual bits and verify original owners. For cofacial pins, add a reference vertex with noncrossing exterior spokes of penalty larger than the total original finite edge weights; specify parity relative to the reference, then orient its bit to zero. Every requested boundary word extends to some bit assignment (not necessarily a satisfying one), so all spokes are obeyed by an optimum. All bit costs, verification, shortest paths, matching and lifts are polynomial. The fixed/logarithmic boundary enumeration cost is polynomial under a fixed original-$N$ cap. Arbitrary affine guards or noncofacial crossing pin chords are not covered.
\end{proof}
This standard planar Ising route bypasses the DO23 absolute cycle-tail obstruction, and can feed RT29 optimum-signature contraction even when the local balance-deletion modulator is large. A certified strict shrink and charged region discovery remain necessary. See Moret (1988), \href{https://doi.org/10.1145/49097.49099}{Planar NAE3SAT is in P}, and Gobron, \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.7289}{arXiv:1312.7289} for related Pfaffian evaluations (not used as an implemented backend).
\begin{lemma}[Four-port disk switching firewall]\label{lem:do24-switch}
Let finite local energies be invariant under simultaneous complement of all their arguments, with a disk-embedded primal interaction graph (each local scope induces a clique). Four distinct actual ports lie in cyclic order $1,2,3,4$ on the disk boundary. Write $E(a)$ for the minimum conditioned on the boundary word $a$ and $Z(a)$ for any boundary partition sum of nonnegative complement-symmetric local product weights on that graph. For unit bits $e_i$ and $b=a+e_2+e_4$ (binary addition),
\[
 E(a)+E(b)\ge\min\{E(a+e_2)+E(a+e_4),E(a+e_1)+E(a+e_3)\},
\]
\[
 Z(a)Z(b)\le Z(a+e_2)Z(a+e_4)+Z(a+e_1)Z(a+e_3).
\]
The latter includes exact feasibility counts. In particular no such network of any size realizes the crossing relation $x_1=x_3,\ x_2=x_4$ by projection, or by a common minimum on its valid words and strictly higher energy on every invalid word.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Take ordered assignments $x,y$ with words $a,b$. Swapping the two words on a connected component of their induced disagreement graph preserves their total energy and product weight, since the disagreeing arguments of any local factor belong to one component. If ports $2,4$ are disconnected in that graph, swap the component containing port $2$; the output words are $a+e_2,a+e_4$. Otherwise complement $y$, preserving its energy/weight. The new disagreement graph is induced on the complementary vertex set. It cannot contain a path joining ports $1,3$, because that path and the original $2$--$4$ path would be vertex-disjoint paths joining alternating endpoints in a disk, contrary to Jordan separation. Swap the new component containing port $1$; the words are $a+e_1,a+e_3$. Taking minimizers proves the first inequality. For the second, each output class is injective: the disagreement set is unchanged by a swap, so reverse the indicated component swap, and in the second class complement $y$ back. The output boundary pairs are distinct, and summing nonnegative products proves the claim. At $a=0000,b=0101$, a crossing relation has positive counts on both inputs and zero counts on all four outputs, a contradiction. The same words contradict the minimum inequality if all valid words have the same strict global minimum. Fixed bit gauges transfer the result to signed crossing parities.
\end{proof}
The switch itself is a linear graph traversal plus original-factor verification given two assignments; finding either assignment is charged. The lemma covers signed planar ternary incidence networks by local triangle replacement, but not arbitrary native four-port factors with nonplanar primal interaction, external noncomplement-symmetric pins, arbitrary dense affine guards, or nonlocal reductions changing actual ports. It refutes local exact planarization into the dual-matching terminal, not unrestricted SAT. Passing the inequality does not certify planarity. Boundary minima/count acquisition on nonplanar inputs is not free. Related planar switching literature: Lis, \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.12131}{arXiv:2009.12131}; the proof here is direct.
\paragraph{Executed identical-source checks.}

\section{GD31: Exact affine-quadratic messages and paid representation switching}\label{sec:gd31}
This addresses U-PROGRESS (Obligation~\ref{obl:progress}), GD30's signed Fourier transfer, DP24's shrinking affine frontier and BS23's capped affine intersection dictionary. It retains S29's decision/closure firewall and DO24's separate planar matching consumer.
\begin{lemma}[Closed real affine-quadratic atom algebra]\label{lem:gd31-atom}
An atom $c[Gx=b](-1)^{Q(x)}$, with dyadic scalar $c$ and squarefree Boolean polynomial $Q$ of degree at most two, has polynomial-size representation. Products, affine restriction and summation over any private coordinates map single atoms to single atoms or zero, uniformly in polynomial bit time in the representation and coefficient sizes. Structural equality up to a scalar is decidable by canonical row reduction and phase reduction. For two atoms on the same support with coefficients $c$ and $\pm c$ and phase difference an affine form $L$ on that support, their sum is a single atom.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Intersect affine supports and add phases modulo two for products. Row-reduce the support, substitute pivot coordinates into the phase, reduce $x_i^2=x_i$ and absorb its constant into the sign of the coefficient. On the resulting full free cube the squarefree polynomial is unique. This supplies a structural key, not complete semantic equality of sums. To sum over $x_i$, if a support equation involves it, solve that equation and substitute into all others and the phase. Each permitted exterior word has exactly one private extension. Otherwise write $Q(x_i,y)=R(y)+x_i L(y)$ with affine $L$. The exact sum is $2c[G'y=b][L(y)=0](-1)^{R(y)}$. Iteration gives the general projection. All affine and quadratic transformations use polynomial bit operations and at most quadratically many coefficients. For the last assertion, factor out $c(-1)^Q$; the sum equals $2c(-1)^Q[L=0]$ for equal coefficient signs and $2c(-1)^Q[L=1]$ for opposite signs, intersected with the common support. Check the affine-difference condition after restriction. Individual atom support equations are not unconditional facts of a sum.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Capped mixed flat/phase frontier]\label{lem:gd31-mixed}
For a rank-at-most-two forbidden packet $E=\{\ell_1=b_1,\ell_2=b_2\}$, its Boolean indicator is $q_E=(1+\ell_1+b_1)(1+\ell_2+b_2)$ over $\mathbb F_2$ (rank-zero and rank-one cases are handled by closure or repeated equations). Exact avoidance has the two expansions
\[
1-[E]=\frac{1+(-1)^{q_E}}{2}.
\]
Maintain a signed dictionary of the preceding atoms with a common power-of-two denominator; either expansion can be multiplied in, followed by projection of all coordinates absent from every remaining owner. Any polynomially charged choice between the two exact results preserves the conditional count on the actual frontier. A fixed original-input cap $K=(N+2)^a$ on retained atoms gives a polynomially charged consumer, possibly declining. A nonzero final count permits paid coordinate self-reduction, with closure and source verification, provided each requested query also succeeds within the cap.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Initialize the actual affine guard as one atom and run paid rank-one closure first, after each accepted necessary deduction and at stagnation. Each owner expansion emits at most two atoms per input atom. Sum only private coordinates; every projection of a single atom emits at most one. Group by canonical keys and cancel exact zero coefficients after complete accumulation. Trying both expansions uses at most a fixed multiple of $K$ scratch entries; each trial is charged, including a declined trial. A general binary composition may instead emit $K^2$ products, charged before a retained cap test. Integer numerator absolute mass for the sequential rank-two realization is at most $2^{m+n}$ from at most $m$ doubling expansions and $n$ bit summations; the denominator is at most $2^m$. Thus coefficient lengths, row/phase canonicalization, guard handling and all accesses are polynomial in original $N$ for an admitted count query. A positive count licenses choosing a conditional fiber only after its paid exact count; any decline is OPEN, not contradiction. Reconstruction may use at most $n$ conditional count queries, and verify the resulting source word. This does not bound complete semantic hull acquisition or guarantee successful queries. Polynomial time and peak space on the same admitted serial execution imply $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$. No universal cap success is proved.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Dense fixed-sign Walsh message with a two-atom exact bypass; raw phase-key obstruction]\label{lem:gd31-separation}
Let $Q=\sum_{i=1}^k u_iv_i$ on $2k$ Boolean coordinates. The nonnegative Boolean compatibility function $f=(1+(-1)^Q)/2$ is a two-atom sum, but every Walsh coefficient is nonzero. It is the exact private-variable marginal of a polynomial-size ordinary 3-CNF with unique circuit extensions. Conversely, for a raw linear signed NAE-3 registry before any projection or other fusion, the phase-only subset expansion has $2^s$ distinct nonzero canonical phase keys after $s$ owners, in every order and under every signing.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The unnormalized transform of each pair phase is $\sum_{u,v}(-1)^{uv+au+bv}=2(-1)^{ab}$. Multiplying gives a nonzero coefficient of magnitude $2^k$ at every mode; the constant part of $f$ only adds at the zero mode, with the same sign. Encode the ANDs $u_iv_i$, their XOR sum, and its zero output by uniquely extendible Boolean circuit gate CNFs of width at most three. The private marginal is exactly the indicator $f$. This is not a proof of inexpensive acquisition of the two atoms from an arbitrary circuit, nor a strict native compiler. For the second assertion, the quadratic part of the violation polynomial of a signed NAE owner on distinct bits $a,b,c$ is $ab+ac+bc$. Linearity of the hypergraph ensures each of these pair monomials occurs in no other owner. Hence all subset sums differ in their quadratic parts, even modulo affine phases, and cannot merge by the raw canonical key before projection. All coefficients have nonzero magnitude in the unprojected expansion. This says nothing about mixed flat/phase expansions, nonlinear cancellation, projection, atom fusion, matching, or other exact consumers. Neither representation bound is an unrestricted lower bound.
\end{proof}
Related established work includes Cai, Guo and Williams, \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.00942}{Clifford Gates in the Holant Framework} (more general affine signatures); the real signed subcase above is proved directly.

\section{Guarded planar Walsh consumers and all-basis patch-rank firewall (DA24)}\label{sec:da24}
Combine DO24 planar matching, GD30 signed Fourier transfer, and S29 paid outside-span consumers on the same actual source coordinates. Attack Obligation~\ref{obl:progress}; no universal conclusion follows.
\begin{lemma}[Exact guarded planar histogram and affine lift]\label{lem:da24-hist}
Let $E_0(x)$ be an authenticated nonnegative integer pair energy on a certified planar graph on $n$ binary variables. Let $L$ have independent binary rows of rank $r$, with the affine translation absorbed into the following functions. Let $h(Lx)$ be a nonnegative integer correction and $g(Lx)$ a Boolean guard, each evaluable in polynomial original-$N$ bit time, and assume the sum of the core energy upper bound and correction upper bound is polynomial in $N$. The complete guarded energy histogram is deterministically obtainable in $2^r\operatorname{poly}(N)$ bit time and space. A word at any nonempty target energy and its entire model affine hull are obtainable in $2^{r+1}\operatorname{poly}(N)$ bit time and space.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Put $B=2^{n+1}$ and $F(y)=\mathbf1_{g(y)}B^{h(y)}$. Compute its integer Walsh transform $\widehat F(a)=\sum_y(-1)^{a^Ty}F(y)$ over all $r$-bit words. Then
\[
Z=\sum_x\mathbf1_{g(Lx)}B^{E_0(x)+h(Lx)}
=2^{-r}\sum_a\widehat F(a)\sum_x(-1)^{(L^Ta)^Tx}B^{E_0(x)}.
\]
Digits of $Z$ in base $B$ give all exact nonnegative histogram counts without carries. Signed intermediate terms are not decision labels.

For the inner character $c=L^Ta$, let the pair weight on parity $b$ be $w_e(b)=B^{E_e(b)}$. Write $A_e=w_e(0)+w_e(1)$ and $D_e=w_e(0)-w_e(1)$. Expanding the product and summing spins gives
\[
2^{n-|E|}\sum_{S:\partial S=c}\ \prod_{e\notin S} A_e\prod_{e\in S}D_e.
\]
If $c$ is odd on a core component the sum is zero. Otherwise construct a forest edge set $T$ with $\partial T=c$ by parity propagation. The change $S\mapsto S\mathbin{\triangle}T$ makes the sum an even-subgraph sum with $A_e,D_e$ interchanged on $T$. This works at signed or zero weights, with no division by an edge weight.

For explicit polynomial reduction to weighted planar dimers, replace each degree-$d$ vertex in its embedding disk by a path of $d$ ports in cyclic order, each with one original incident edge; put $A=D=1$ on path links. The new internal edge selection is uniquely determined by the old incident subset if its parity is even. Every resulting vertex has degree at most three. Replace each by a clique on its incident ports. An external port edge is in the perfect matching iff the corresponding edge is absent from the even subset; the remaining ports, zero or two, match uniquely inside the clique. Give the external matching edge weight $A_e$ and allocate $D_e$ to exactly one endpoint port; internal matching edges carry the product of allocated port factors. This yields precisely the required product for every even subset. The expanded graph is planar and has linear size in the core edge count. The all-external perfect matching is a combinatorial sign reference, even when its numerical weight is zero. Construct a planar Pfaffian orientation and calibrate its common combinatorial matching sign by that reference, not by an absolute value (signed sums can be negative). The classical planar Pfaffian theorem applies to arbitrary edge weights by polynomial identity; exact pivoted Pfaffian arithmetic has polynomial bit length by minor bounds. All embedding, orientation, forest, Walsh, and exact signed arithmetic costs are charged. See Gobron \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.7289}{arXiv:1312.7289} and Cimasoni \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.3158}{arXiv:1004.3158} for planar Ising/dimer background. Isolated variables are accounted for in the original spin sum.

For witness acquisition at a nonempty target, select any remaining core edge and substitute one of its two parity values, contracting that edge. Test its target count by the same procedure; retain a positive mode. Contraction preserves planarity, loop costs become constants, and the observation map is transported by the affine substitution without increasing rank (reduce its rows and substitute in $h,g$). At most $n$ such steps leave an edgeless core; enumerate the observation words and solve the actual affine lift by Gaussian elimination. Verify the reconstructed word against the original target and guard. For the complete target hull, apply S29's outside-span queries with only one extra affine row per query, reconstructing witnesses by this contraction procedure. Each strict enlargement increases dimension, with at most $O(n^2)$ paid queries. No cumulative guard-rank growth from independent probes.
\end{proof}
For signed NAE the pair mismatch target is $m$, since energy is $m+2V$. First run certified necessary closure on the actual SAT guard, after every accepted deduction and at stagnation; a histogram of the original energy under the original guard must not absorb merely SAT-necessary equations. The theorem permits arbitrary dense and noncofacial affine guards if the joint correction/guard rank is small; it also permits a supplied nonplanar edge patch of small incidence rank. At $r\le C\log_2(N+2)$ with fixed $C$, the admitted phase, including verification, failed probes, hull acquisition, and reconstruction, is polynomial on one serial realization, with $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$. The planar representation must be acquired and authenticated at separately charged cost.
\begin{lemma}[Universal raw planar-plus-observation shortcut fails]\label{lem:da24-firewall}
Suppose a real quadratic binary-character energy on $n$ actual bits has a nonzero coefficient at every pair character. If it has a pointwise representation as a planar pair energy plus any function of $r$ binary affine observations on these same coordinates, then $r\ge n-4$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The Fourier support of a function of affine observations lies in their binary row space $U$, regardless of the function's form. Each pair $uv$ absent from the planar core must therefore have $e_u+e_v\in U$. Let $H$ be the graph of absent pairs. Their incidence vectors have span dimension $n-c(H)$, including isolated components in $c(H)$. Hence $c(H)\ge n-r$. Picking one vertex from each component yields a clique in the planar core because no intercomponent pair is absent. A planar graph has no clique of size five, so $c(H)\le4$. This proves the claim. Gauge translations preserve Fourier support. A two-hub planar core with all hub-to-leaf edges and the hub edge achieves rank $n-3$ on complete pair support by folding all leaf pairs into one observation subspace.
\end{proof}
This is a firewall even for nonlinear correction functions and arbitrary observation bases; raw complete-pair S27 opposite-label charts meet its hypotheses. It does not exclude changing coordinates, auxiliary representations, nonlocal decision transformations, post-guard contractions, or a general nonplanar exact consumer. Universal acquisition of a polynomial reserve is still open.

\section{Budgeted planar affine quotient and all-two-hub obstruction (M30)}\label{sec:m30}
\begin{lemma}[Exact planar budget hull and exceptional syndrome quotient]\label{lem:m30-budget}
Let $E=E_C+E_X$ be a field-free binary pair energy with nonnegative integral costs and total energy upper bound $W$ polynomial in the original encoded length $N$. Suppose the core graph $C$ is verified planar, with all actual source bits including isolates retained, and $\ell\le\min_x E_X(x)$ is certified. For threshold $K$, let $S=\{x:E_C(x)\le K-\ell\}$. There is a deterministic polynomial-bit-time algorithm to reject empty $S$ or acquire its exact binary affine hull $A=x_0+V$, with actual witnessed generators. If $B$ contains all exceptional endpoint XOR rows and actual affine guard rows, the entire guarded decision $E\le K$ and witness reconstruction cost at most $4^r\operatorname{poly}(N+W)$ with $r=\operatorname{rank}(B|_V)$, excluding separately charged core/bound acquisition. This uses the actual core support, not its hull as a replacement.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For each connected planar core component with at least three vertices, combine parallel edge factors (retaining provenance), embed and augment its simple graph to a plane triangulation by neutral edges. Each face becomes a triangle of matching ports, with external links joining corresponding ports of adjacent faces. Exactly one or three external links per face are selected, with a unique internal matching. Interpret external selection as an uncut primal edge, so cut parity on each triangular face is even. Face boundaries span the cycle space; these are precisely primal cut vectors, each lifting to two complementary words. Subdivide each external link by two vertices, so the two outer edges selected encode the uncut case (weight $f_e(0)$ on one outer edge), and the middle edge alone the cut case (weight $f_e(1)$). Both modes unique. Thus the planar weighted dimer polynomial gives $\sum_x\prod_e f_e(x_u\oplus x_v)$ after multiplication by two per component. Smaller components are direct. Use the known unweighted all-zero-cut matching to calibrate the global sign of a planar Pfaffian orientation, keeping that sign even for negative or zero factors. This is a constructive version of the triangulated expanded dual (Schraudolph and Kamenetsky, \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/0810.4401}{arXiv:0810.4401}; see also Cimasoni, \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.3158}{arXiv:1004.3158}).
Use $f_e(d)=z^{c_e(d)}$ times any pinned edge-difference indicator. For a character $(-1)^{a\cdot x}$, if $a$ has odd sum on any core component the signed polynomial vanishes by complement; otherwise express $a$ as a sum of edge endpoint vectors on a spanning forest and negate $f_e(1)$ on the corresponding edges. Evaluate the weighted Pfaffian at $W+1$ integer points and interpolate, keeping all signed coefficients. Entries, minors, and interpolation have polynomial bit lengths for polynomial $W$; arbitrary binary-encoded exponential total weights are NOT covered. The count below a budget with $a\cdot x=b$ is half the unsigned count plus $(-1)^b$ times half the signed count. For $r$ guards use the $2^r$ character sum. Witnesses are acquired by successive pinning of actual spanning-tree differences through these same counts (no noncofacial vertex pins), then solving the remaining component-root affine system and verifying the word.
Starting at actual $x_0\in S$, maintain a span $V'$ of actual witnessed differences. For each basis row $a$ of $(V')^\perp$, test the opposite parity to $a\cdot x_0$ at budget $K-\ell$. If positive, reconstruct the word and increase rank; if all tests vanish, $S\subseteq x_0+V'$ and equality of affine hulls follows. At most $n$ rank increases, $O(n^2)$ parity queries and $O(n^2)$ edge-pin witness queries. Transfer only certified equations under their actual guards and repeat closure after each accepted deduction.
On $A$, choose $r$ independent original rows of $B$ restricted to $V$; every other row value is a linear combination plus known offset. Enumerate the $2^r$ selected syndromes, rejecting wrong guards and computing $E_X$ exactly for each. Test ACTUAL core support at budget $K-E_X$ under those row values by $2^r$ character queries; this budget is at most $K-\ell$. Positive count iff actual feasible word exists, with paid pinned reconstruction as above. Include embedding, factor compilation, bit arithmetic, guard and provenance verification, failed queries, and all reconstruction. Peak space at most $2^r\operatorname{poly}(N+W)$; same serial cumulative memory at most $(T+1)S_{\rm peak}$. Universal discovery, universal logarithmic $r$ and aggregate credit do not follow.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[All-two-hub signed Steiner obstruction]\label{lem:m30-sts}
In a signed Steiner triple system on $n\ge7$ actual bits with unit signed NAE pair cost, choose ANY two hubs. Take as core every incident pair edge, and as exceptional graph the remaining leaf pairs. With threshold $K=m$ and independent ownerwise exceptional lower bound $\ell=m-(n-2)$, the budget hull in Lemma~\ref{lem:m30-budget} is all of $\mathbb F_2^n$ for EVERY sign pattern. Hence the exceptional row rank after quotient is exactly $n-3$ (before extra guards), regardless of hub choice.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Every pair belongs to one owner. Exactly $n-2$ owners touch either hub (one contains both); the others are full exceptional triangles costing at least one each. Thus core budget is $n-2$. Fix either relative hub mode. Each ordinary leaf has two hub preferences with minimum cost zero or one; the special leaf in the owner containing both hubs, together with their hub edge, has minimum exactly one for either mode by odd preferred triangle parity. Both modes have minimum core cost at most $n-3+1$. For each leaf there is a hub mode in which its two incident preferences disagree, so either leaf value occurs in otherwise identical minimizing words. Their differences give every leaf unit vector. Global complement gives the all-ones vector. A difference between minimizing words of opposite hub modes has different relative hub parity and completes the full-dimensional span. Exceptional graph is complete on $n-2$ leaves and has binary incidence row rank $n-3$. Unbounded STS sizes exist via nonzero vectors of $\mathbb F_2^k$ and triples $\{a,b,a+b\}$. This falsifies universal favorable quotient rank for this two-hub core and ownerwise bound, not for stronger lower bounds, other cores, nonlocal deductions or unrestricted computation.
\end{proof}
