\section{Deterministic sign-class normalization and affine-cube cancellation (RT32)}\label{sec:rt32}
The signed compatibility polynomial of RT31 admits an exact deterministic improvement at strict deficiency one, without presuming universal identity testing. Let $m=r+1$, $\operatorname{rank}L=r$, and let every proper owner subset have observation rank at least its cardinality. DS15's smallest maximum-deficiency core satisfies these hypotheses when the maximum deficiency is one. Work on the actual authenticated chart after certified closure, and recertify the premises on any changed chart. Write the signs as $s\in\mathbb F_2^{2m}$ and $G=\operatorname{im}L$; translation of the source word makes all signs in one coset of $G$ equisatisfiable. For each direction $a\in U_i\setminus\{0\}$ let $c_{ia}$ denote the corresponding linear functional of the sign coordinates, extended by zero on other owners.
\begin{lemma}[At most one UNSAT sign coset]\label{lem:rt32-coset}
If $s+t\notin G$, a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm produces a satisfying assignment for at least one of these two signings.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Put $\delta=s+t$. The row spaces lifted by $a\mapsto(a,c_{ia}\delta)$ have total rank $r+1=m$, since otherwise $\delta$ is a common source evaluation. Every proper subset has lifted rank at least its cardinality by projection. Rado's theorem and deterministic linear/partition matroid intersection give one independent lifted direction per owner. The projected rows $a_i$ have rank $r$ and one nonzero dependency $\lambda$; independence of the lifts implies $\sum_i\lambda_i c_{ia_i}\delta=1$. The selected satisfying equations $a_i x=1+c_{ia_i}s$ are consistent precisely when $\sum_i\lambda_i(1+c_{ia_i}s)=0$. This consistency bit differs by one between $s$ and $t$. Thus exactly one selected system has a unique solution, satisfying the corresponding chart. All witness checks use the actual original signs and rows.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Polynomial acquisition of an exceptional coset]\label{lem:rt32-acquire}
At most $2m-r=m+1$ deterministic matroid intersections produce an affine coset $s_0+G$ containing all UNSAT signings. For every signing outside the coset, the retained certificates give a satisfying assignment by Gaussian elimination. If one independently certified UNSAT signing of the geometry is available, this is an exact deterministic decision procedure for every signing.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For a transversal as above, let $p=\sum_i\lambda_i c_{ia_i}$. Every UNSAT signing must satisfy $ps=1+\sum_i\lambda_i$; otherwise the selected equations are consistent. All $p$ annihilate $G$. Start with no equations and choose $\delta$ in their homogeneous kernel outside $G$ using Gaussian elimination whenever possible. The lifted transversal supplies a new equation with $p\delta=1$, independent of the previous rows. After $2m-r$ additions the common homogeneous kernel is exactly $G$. The independent affine equations have a solution $s_0$; their solution set is $s_0+G$. A violated equation supplies its stored transversal and the corresponding unique source solution. A certified UNSAT reference identifies the entire exceptional coset by gauge equivalence. Without that reference or a separate exact decision of $s_0$, the exceptional class is UNKNOWN; it may be SAT, as the three identical rank-two planes with three owners demonstrate. The chosen candidate need not be independent of the acquisition order when all signs are SAT.
\end{proof}
With a ground set of $3m$ labeled directions in dimension $m$, ordinary augmenting-path matroid intersection and naive binary rank tests give a conservative $O(m^7)$ bit-operation allowance for the $O(m)$ calls, plus polynomial discovery/rechecks, actual certified closure, source verification and lifts. Store polynomially many row IDs, masks and transversals; polynomial peak space and same-execution cumulative storage bounded by $(T+1)S$. Hypothetical signs are separate queries, not necessary deductions on the original sign chart. No extra guarded source constraints may be ignored.
\begin{lemma}[Top-order multisign cancellation]\label{lem:rt32-cube}
For an RT31 Hall core with $m=r+d$, let $\delta_1,\ldots,\delta_d$ be specified sign shifts and define $D_{ij}(z)=\sum_{a\ne0}z_{ia}c_{ia}\delta_j$. For common selector variables $z$ and the RT31 coefficient matrix $A(z)$,
\[
\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb F_2^d}P_{s+\sum_j\alpha_j\delta_j}(z)=\det[A(z)\mid D(z)]
\]
over characteristic two. The right-hand identity is decidable deterministically in polynomial time by row-separated matroid intersection. If the $2^d$ signings are distinct and all but one have independently certified UNSAT, this decides the remaining signing exactly.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Combine the sums over $x$ and $\alpha$ in the RT31 polynomial. The product has $m$ affine factors on $r+d=m$ Boolean variables. Binary summation kills all terms except those hitting every variable once, and the permanent equals the determinant in characteristic two. Each monomial of this determinant selects one direction per owner, with coefficient equal to the determinant of the corresponding lifted rows. A full independent transversal therefore supplies a nonzero coefficient and a unique solution of the selected equations in $(x,\alpha)$. If all other compatibility polynomials vanish identically, the identity equals the designated polynomial. No acquisition of the other refutations is assumed free.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Local exact substitution cannot lower maximum deficiency]\label{lem:rt32-local}
Replace each rank-two puncture by an exact existential avoidance-packet gadget using only its original observation plane $U_i$ and a disjoint private coordinate block. Then maximum rank-Hall deficiency of the resulting chart is at least that of the original.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Apply DS15 extraction to the private projections of each gadget's row spaces. Its maximum private deficiency is at least one, since otherwise independent private representatives would satisfy all owners for every exterior word. For a maximizing subregistry $C_i$ of private rank $p_i$, all outside owners can be satisfied preserving exterior and core observations by the quotient independent-transversal argument. Hence $C_i$ still projects to the original puncture. If $W_i$ is its full row span, the projected relation depends only on $W_i\cap U_i$: preservation of the pure exterior observations is exactly the solvability condition for the private linear system preserving all core row observations. A genuine two-bit puncture has no nonzero observation-space period, so $W_i\cap U_i=U_i$. For any old owner subset $J$, disjoint private blocks give rank $\sum_{i\in J}p_i+\dim\sum_{i\in J}U_i$ for the union of the $C_i$. Its deficiency is at least $|J|-\dim\sum_{i\in J}U_i$, because each $|C_i|-p_i\ge1$. Maximize over $J$. This does not exclude nonlocal exact transformations or gadgets using additional exterior information.
\end{proof}
Executed raw-chart audit: 21 geometry controls, 27,344 signing queries, 27,045 verified SAT lifts, 139 matroid-intersection calls, 1,320 augmentations, 1,200,660 exhaustive reference visits and 56,578 checks. Fano: all 16,384 signings, exactly 64 UNSAT in one coset; repeated-plane all-SAT control has a SAT candidate. Expanded 28-owner RT21 geometry strictness and root UNSAT justified symbolically; sampled signs and actual lifts tested, not exhaustive large enumeration. Separate 72 affine-cube controls at $d=1,2,3$: 52,002 coefficient comparisons, 339,228 signing coefficient checks, 15,738 verified lifts and 83,478 checks. No failures. Private substitution theorem symbolic only. No production core extraction, full cooperative closure, native replay, TeX/kernel or measured cumulative memory. See \url{https://github.com/j15marti/pnp/commit/bcc0b36d34d9c5413cb33f7a1eeb26d2b3095fb6}.
The reference-free exceptional-coset decision remains open; so does a uniform nonlocal reduction of arbitrary deficiency with fixed original-$N$ credit. U-PROGRESS, universal SEM/CLOSE and unconditional COST remain BLOCK. No public proof claim.


\section{Deterministic degree-band identity testing (RT33)}\label{sec:rt33}
For the authenticated RT31 maximum-deficiency Hall chart, with $m=r+d$ and $d\ge0$, fix an owner order. Put $A_i=\sum_{j\le i}U_j$, $C_i=\sum_{j>i}U_j$, $B_i=A_i\cap C_i$, $w_i=\dim B_i$, $e_i=\dim A_i-i$, and $h_i=w_i-e_i=i-r+\dim C_i$. Apply available certified closure before admission and preserve actual guards.
\begin{lemma}[Exact degree-band PIT]\label{lem:rt33-band}
Set
\[
K_i=\sum_{j=\max(0,h_i-d)}^{\min(w_i,h_i)}\binom{w_i}{j}
=\sum_{j=\max(0,e_i)}^{\min(w_i,e_i+d)}\binom{w_i}{j},\qquad K=\max_i K_i.
\]
A deterministic algorithm tests the identity $P_s=0$ and reconstructs a verified witness in the nonzero case in $\operatorname{poly}(N)(1+K^3)$ bit time and $\operatorname{poly}(N)(1+K^2)$ peak space, given the order and the authenticated chart. In particular fixed $d$ and fixed bounded prefix rank excess suffice even at growing interface rank.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For an actual selector prefix, let $F_i$ on $B_i^*$ be the parity of valuations on $A_i$ extending the boundary and satisfying all selected prefix equations. $F_0=1$. Put $D_i=B_{i-1}+U_i$; it contains $B_i$ and its intersection with $C_i$ is $B_i$, while $D_i+C_i=C_{i-1}$. The exact linear-gluing recurrence sums $F_{i-1}\ell_{ia}$ over valuations of $D_i$ extending the new boundary. In a basis extending $B_i$, this eliminates $k_i=\dim C_{i-1}-\dim C_i\le2$ bits. Substitution preserves the degree upper bound, multiplication adds at most one and summation over $k_i$ bits drops degree by at least $k_i$. Since $h_i=h_{i-1}+1-k_i$, degree never exceeds $h_i$, and a term below $h_{i-1}-d$ remains below $h_i-d$. At the final cut $B_m=0,h_m=d$, only the constant is relevant. Hence the band projection preserves the final scalar exactly.
For a transfer entry from old monomial $M$ to new monomial $Q$, set all new retained variables outside $Q$ to zero, and sum the substituted product over the $Q$ variables and the eliminated coordinates. Binary coefficient inversion gives the required entry. This sum is the parity of solutions to a binary affine system requiring each old linear factor and the new satisfaction factor to equal one. Gaussian elimination returns one iff that system is consistent and full rank in the summed variables. No expansion of high-degree products or $N^{O(d)}$ enumeration is needed for these entries.
Keep actual prefix coefficient vectors forming a linear basis, with actual prefix words, and a separate reduced copy for rank tests. Apply each of the three next-owner maps to each basis vector and keep independent actual outputs. Linearity gives the span of all actual truncated prefix vectors. At the final scalar coordinate this span is zero iff the compatibility polynomial is identically zero; otherwise a retained word has coefficient one and provides a unique solution by RT31. Verify the original source and lift. Matrix entry costs are polynomial in $N$, and dense binary rank tests and matrix-vector applications have cubic overhead in the coordinate width. Compute binomial sizes before enumeration and decline if exceeding a fixed original-$N$ cap. No free discovery of a good order, hidden guard, or semantic closure.
\end{proof}
The recursive RT21 raw expansion has a supplied order with bounded excess: process all deepest unshifted triples one at a time and then shifted owners in the inherited order. Each complete triple contributes three private ranks and three owners, and the partial triple excess is at most one. The shifted owners modulo that private span have exactly the previous chart's observation ranks. The base Fano rank bounds the excess by six. At the cut separating the bottom triples from shifted owners the boundary rank equals $m_0+1$, where $m_0$ is the preceding owner count. Thus the band test is polynomial on this infinite family even in an order with linear width; the earlier RT21 triple closure is an alternative.
The explicit band cap is not universally small at strict $d=1$: take $r$ odd, $m=r+1$, and independently sample two uniform binary vectors per owner. The probability a size-$s$ subset has rank below $s$ is at most $C2^{-(s+1)(r-s+1)}$ by counting subspaces of dimension $s-1$, for an absolute constant $C$. Union bound (including pair independence) gives the strict Hall condition with probability tending to one. Simultaneously every half-subset has rank at least $r-\lfloor r/8\rfloor$ by the same counting bound and union over subsets. Thus at every order's balanced cut $e_i,h_i=\Omega(r)$, and $K_i\ge\binom{w_i}{e_i}=2^{\Omega(r)}$. These existential raw geometries can be signed SAT with a known word; this is only a coordinate-band representation barrier, not a lower bound on actual coefficient rank or on an unrestricted algorithm.
\begin{lemma}[Deficiency-one determinant support inclusion]\label{lem:rt33-contain}
For $d=1$, let $D_s(z)=\det[A(z)\mid b_s(z)]$, where $b_s$ gives the opposite RHS for each selected direction. Let $Q_i(z)=\det[A(z)\mid c_i(z)]$, where only the last column's row $i$ is nonzero, equal to $\sum_a z_{ia}$. Then
\[
P_s=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{supp}Q_i\subseteq\operatorname{supp}D_s\quad\hbox{for every }i.
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Each selector monomial chooses one binary row per owner. The coefficient in $D_s$ is one iff the observation rank is $r$ and the selected equations are inconsistent. Its coefficient in $Q_i$ is one iff deleting row $i$ leaves an independent basis. Thus a full-rank consistent selector exists iff one inclusion fails. All coefficient matrices have rank one, but testing support inclusion is not ordinary determinant equality; the recent principal-minor equivalence theorem of Chatterjee et al.\ does not directly imply these inclusions.
\end{proof}
Executed 74 raw-chart cases, 71 SAT verified witnesses, three UNSAT, 195291 coefficient queries, 5052 coefficient-vector candidates, 4911 span XORs, 3280 brute reference source words on the 72 small cases. Full 28-owner RT21 expansion pair had peak band 126, live basis 9/12 for UNSAT/SAT; labels for that pair justified symbolically rather than full enumeration. Separate Fano selector enumeration confirmed the containment criterion. No complete portfolio, source compiler, formal kernel, large random geometry generation, or measured cumulative memory. See \url{https://github.com/j15marti/pnp/commit/d86417012f8922a97cf35ebe03d4d16c557df1c2}. U-PROGRESS, universal SEM/CLOSE and unconditional COST remain BLOCK; no universal PIT or public proof claim.


\section{Reference-free binary complementarity and implicit Gram PIT (RT34)}\label{sec:rt34}
For a strict deficiency-one chart, omit one owner and acquire an independent row transversal $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ of the others by Rado's theorem and deterministic matroid intersection. Solve their opposite-RHS equations to obtain a near-model $x_0$. If the omitted owner accepts, return SAT. Otherwise take the other satisfied nonzero observation $b_i$ at each retained owner. In coordinates $y_i=a_i(x+x_0)$, let row $i$ of $M$ express $b_i$ in the acquired basis. The retained system is exactly
\[
y_i(My)_i=0\quad (1\le i\le r).
\]
The omitted owner requires $(\ell_1(y),\ell_2(y))\ne(0,0)$ for its two actual independent linear observations. Thus the chart is UNSAT iff both annihilate the span $W$ of the retained legal words. This reduction is unconditional on the stated strict core; acquiring $W$ remains a charged task.
\begin{lemma}[Witnessed complementarity span on admitted SCCs]\label{lem:rt34-scc}
Suppose the directed graph of off-diagonal nonzeros of $M$ has each strongly connected component internally symmetric or a simple directed cycle. Then $W$ and an actual witnessed basis are deterministically computable in polynomial time, including witness verification and source lifts. This gives an exact reference-free identity test for admitted strict deficiency-one cores.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For a connected symmetric block with diagonal $d$, summing complementarity equations cancels the off-diagonal terms, so all legal words satisfy $d^\top y=0$. Zero-diagonal singletons and induced paths between two diagonal-one endpoints with zero-diagonal interiors are legal. Shortest paths split at marked vertices supply such paths; canceling interiors with singletons generates all even marked-coordinate differences. These span exactly $\ker d^\top$ (full if $d=0$). A connected symmetric matched chart thus always accepts some witness of the omitted rank-two owner.
For a simple directed cycle, selection of vertex $i$ requires its successor bit to equal $d_i$. With all diagonals one, only zero and all-ones are legal. With one zero at $z$, its successor is necessarily zero, since selecting that successor forces a full circuit ending at $z$ in contradiction. Legal paths ending at $z$ generate the hyperplane on the other coordinates. With at least two zeros, the path starting at any vertex and ending at its first zero is legal; differences generate all coordinate units. The single-zero exception was found and corrected during testing.
Now process SCCs sink first. With an actual downstream word $v$, the effective local diagonal is $d+M_{CD}v$. The new block zero is always legal. Hence the span of all extensions is the direct sum of the downstream span and the sum of local spans over attainable shifts. In each admitted block the zero-shift span is full, or any single nonzero shift gives a local span whose sum with the first is full. For symmetric blocks these are distinct hyperplanes or a full space; for a simple cycle, distinct nonfull labels have distinct coordinate hyperplanes or a hyperplane and the all-ones line. A downstream witness basis detects any nonzero linear shift. Use at most two diagonal modes per block, retaining actual combined witnesses and Gaussian independent selection. This recovers the exact span, not the full nonlinear support. At most $r$ independent actual vectors survive. If one violates either omitted observation, lift to $x=x_0+A^{-1}y$ and verify. Otherwise both vanish everywhere, certifying UNSAT. Charge actual matroid acquisition, SCC and path discovery, all shift tests, all candidates, elimination, closure, verification and lifts; all are polynomial on the admitted chart. One deterministic transversal per omitted owner can be tested within a fixed polynomial allowance, but universal eligibility is unproved.
\end{proof}
Opposite-label strict deficiency-one controls include a directed cycle with all diagonal ones and omitted observations $y_0+y_1,y_1+y_2$, forbidden $00$; changing the first owner's forbidden sign from $11$ to $10$ replaces its second satisfied observation by its sum with the coordinate row and toggles the diagonal. The resulting singleton is legal. A second family has two connected symmetric paths, one all marked and one with only its first diagonal marked, and a directed arc from the first block to that marked downstream bit. Omit the first-block parity and marked downstream bit, forbidden $00$. Root is UNSAT; flipping the second downstream diagonal admits a nonzero marked bit and upstream shift, producing SAT. Strict Hall follows from the coordinate rows and an outgoing edge for each proper subset with crossing, or an omitted observation on the missing block for a closed subset. No claim that arbitrary anchored matrices admit these SCC forms.
\begin{lemma}[Rank-one principal-minor containment]\label{lem:rt34-principal}
For arbitrary binary $M$ and row $\ell$, write $H_M(z)=\det(I+\operatorname{diag}(z)M)$. Then $\ell$ annihilates the actual legal span $W$ iff
\[
\operatorname{supp}H_{M+e_j\ell}\subseteq\operatorname{supp}H_M\quad\text{for every }j .
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The coefficient for subset $S$ equals $\det M[S,S]$. Every kernel vector on this principal submatrix extends by zeros to a legal word. If $\ell$ kills all such words, a rank-one row update cannot make any singular principal submatrix nonsingular. Conversely choose a legal word with $\ell x=1$ of minimum support $S$. Its kernel on $M[S,S]$ has nullity one, since a nonzero kernel vector of $\ell$-value zero could otherwise be added to reduce its support. Its nonzero right and left kernel vectors $x_S,u$ give $\operatorname{adj}(M[S,S])=x_Su^\top$ over $\mathbb F_2$. Choose $j\in S$ with $u_j=1$. The rank-one update has determinant one, whereas the original minor is zero. This is support containment, not equality of principal minors; ordinary deterministic principal-minor equivalence does not establish this test.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Implicit rational prefix-span PIT]\label{lem:rt34-gram}
On a supplied owner order of an authenticated rank-two chart, let $R$ be the largest rational span dimension of the actual prefix boundary count functions. A deterministic exact identity test with verified witness uses $\operatorname{poly}(N,R)$ bit work and peak storage without constructing the boundary truth tables or explicit RT33 degree bands.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Use the positive integer selector polynomial obtained from RT31's definition by summing over the integers, evaluating the individual affine factors as Boolean $0/1$. Nonzero iff SAT on every chart; on a Hall core its identity label equals RT31's, not its coefficients. Each fixed selector prefix describes a binary affine system; its boundary count is zero or a positive constant times an affine-subspace indicator. Compute the projected relation by Gaussian intersection of its selected row span and the actual RT33 boundary $B_i$, preserving RHS. Future transfer maps are rational-linear. Thus retaining actual independent indicator functions, ignoring nonzero scaling, preserves final zero/nonzero. Generate three extensions per retained selector prefix, project afresh, and test independence via the exact rational Gram matrix with entries $|S_u\cap S_v|$, either zero or a Gaussian-computable power of two. Its rank over the rationals equals the actual vector rank (not an assertion over characteristic two). Exact fraction-free rank or rational LDL tests retain independent actual witnesses. At final empty boundary a surviving prefix supplies an actual satisfying word by Gaussian solution and source verification. Gram entries have $O(N)$ bits, minors have $O(R(N+\log R))$ bits; all exact arithmetic, projections, admission, failed attempts and reconstruction are charged. A fixed original-$N$ cap on $R$ returns UNKNOWN if exceeded; under the cap time and space are polynomial, and cumulative storage is at most $(T+1)S$. No universal order or rank bound assumed.
\end{proof}
RT21's recursive deepest-triples-first order has bounded rational prefix rank: complete unshifted triples force the two private shifted observations to zero, so completed private blocks give a singleton on their exposed coordinates; a partial triple has at most eight valuations. After all unshifted triples, boundary valuations factor through the previous chart's boundary via projection onto old coordinates, because all observed private directions are fixed zero. Induct on expansion depth. The depth-two pair was executed with maximum actual rank $23$ and width $31$.
An all-order raw span obstruction: independently sample two binary rows per owner for $m=r+1$, as in RT33. For $s=\lfloor r/16\rfloor$, every $s$-owner subset simultaneously has $2s$ independent rows and its complement full rank with probability tending to one. Indeed the failure probabilities per subset are bounded by $2^{2s-r}$ and $2^{r-2(m-s)}$, and the entropy union bound tends to zero. The strict Hall condition also holds with probability tending to one by RT33. At cut $s$ in any order the boundary is the full independent prefix observation space. The three affine $0/1$ indicators on each two-bit plane have rational rank three, so their tensor products have rank $3^s$. Over $\mathbb F_2$, two independent leading linear terms per owner give $2^s$ independent degree-$s$ leading monomials, preserved by the RT33 band even under basis change. Thus actual span caps as well as explicit coordinate caps can fail on raw charts. These can be signed SAT with known anchor; not an unrestricted or whole-portfolio bound.
Executed local tests: 1268 exact complementarity span comparisons (300312 reference words), 30 both-label source controls through 128 variables, 12 actual matroid-acquired source tests; 584 principal-minor controls, 6784 linear queries and 30283 update tests; 90 Gram PIT controls (85 SAT/5 UNSAT), 83174 Gram queries and 13710 projections, both 112-owner depth-two RT21 controls correct. No final assertion failures; cycle single-zero correction recorded. Raw chart tests only; no full cooperative closure/native/kernel/measured CM. See \url{https://github.com/j15marti/pnp/commit/45819df1cd34821bac223b428cf365f9748c62af}. U-PROGRESS, universal SEM/CLOSE and unconditional COST remain BLOCK. No public proof.


\section{Symplectic dependency closure and polar-monotone private-pivot contraction (RT35--36)}\label{sec:rt36}
Work on the actual authenticated rank-two avoidance chart, after paid certified closure, with no omitted guard. Let $L$ be the full-column-rank $2m$ by $r$ binary observation matrix, $C=\ker L^\top$, $d=m-r$, and $J$ the block exchange matrix. Write $\Omega=L^\top JL$ and $q(p)=\sum_i(p_{i1}+p_{i2}+p_{i1}p_{i2})$, $Q_s(p)=q(p)+s^\top p$. Each full-rank transversal has a $d$-dimensional dependence space $\Lambda$ in $C$; selected equations are consistent iff $Q_s|_\Lambda=0$. RT31 proves existence of such a transversal iff SAT on the Hall core. At strict deficiency one, let $D$ be the nonzero dependence words of full-rank transversals. Then SAT iff some $p\in D$ has $Q_s(p)=0$.
\begin{lemma}[Zero-global-polar strict deficiency-one terminal]\label{lem:rt36-ranktwo}
For strict $d=1$ and $\Omega=0$, reference-free deterministic exact decision with a source witness is polynomial.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The polar form of $q$ is $B(p,u)=p^\top Ju$. Since $C^{\perp_B}=J\operatorname{im}L$, its radical has dimension $r-\operatorname{rank}\Omega$, so the restricted polar rank is $2d+\operatorname{rank}\Omega$. Fix $r$ independent selected rows from distinct owners of a full-rank transversal. Varying the local coefficient at each of the $d$ omitted owners freely and solving for coefficients of the fixed independent rows embeds a nondegenerate symplectic $2d$-space in $C$: the fixed owner blocks lie on lines and contribute zero polar pairing. It contains $\Lambda$. Thus $p\in D$ is nonradical. By RT32, $D$ spans $C$: any nonzero functional on $C$ supplies a homogeneous lifted full-rank transversal whose dependency hits that functional. With $\Omega=0$ and $d=1$, the radical quotient is two-dimensional. Its quadratic form $Q_*$ taking one on every nonzero point and zero at zero has polar $B$. Pull it back to $C$. Then $Q_s+Q_*$ is linear, and $Q_*(p)=1$ for all $p\in D$. The chart is UNSAT exactly when that linear functional vanishes on a Gaussian basis of $C$. Otherwise the RT32 lift produces an actual dependency hitting the functional, hence a consistent transversal and a verified witness. Admission and all costs are polynomial; no reference UNSAT chart required.
\end{proof}
For general $d$, if $\Omega=0$ and $Q_s$ vanishes on the radical with Arf invariant one on the quotient, the necessary totally singular $d$-plane does not exist; this follows by the symplectic quadratic Gauss sum. The converse fails on a disjoint sum of two anisotropic strict deficiency-one UNSAT charts. Arbitrary $d$ is not solved.

\begin{lemma}[Polar-monotone private-pivot resolution]\label{lem:rt36-pivot}
Let $a$ be a nonzero observation shared by owners $I=\{i:a\in U_i\}$, and suppose a primal vector $v$ satisfies $a(v)=1$, $U_j(v)=0$ for all $j\notin I$. Use the actual basis $(a,b_i)$ with $b_i(v)=0$ for each affected plane. Partition by its forbidden first value $\alpha_i$ into groups of sizes $p,q$. Replace those owners by all opposite-polarity pair exclusions $(b_i,b_j)\ne(\beta_i,\beta_j)$. The replacement is exact with a two-choice witness lift. Its global polar rank cannot increase, with difference zero or two. For both groups nonempty,
\[
d^*_{\rm new}\le d^*_{\rm old}+(p-1)(q-1).
\]
An empty side only deletes owners. A nondegenerate singleton-side contraction preserves strict deficiency one.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
All exterior observations annihilate $v$. At fixed exterior word, both values of $a$ are prohibited iff at least one pair of owners with opposite forbidden first values simultaneously has its second observation at the forbidden value. This is precisely the union of the new forbidden packets. Try $x,x+v$ to lift. Put $B_h=\sum_{i:\alpha_i=h}b_i$, and write $u\wedge w=uw^\top+wu^\top$. The old and new polar matrices are
\[
\Omega_{\rm old}=\Omega_R+a\wedge(B_0+B_1),\qquad
\Omega_{\rm new}=\Omega_R+B_0\wedge B_1.
\]
Thus the old is the new plus $(a+B_0)\wedge(B_0+B_1)$; in the basis beginning with $a+B_0$ and followed by a basis of $v^\perp$, this is exactly one alternating border. Rank cannot fall by more than two or increase on deletion of that border. For a nonempty subset $E$ of new cross pairs with endpoint sets $A,B$ and unaffected subset $R'$, the original corresponding row span equals the new row span plus independent $a$. Hence its new deficiency equals the old corresponding deficiency plus $|E|-|A|-|B|+1$, at most $(p-1)(q-1)$ extra. Subsets containing no resolvent inherit their rank. When both sides nonempty, full owner count changes by $pq-p-q$, full rank falls one; equality in the bound holds when the full old chart attained maximum deficiency, before degenerate closure. A singleton side maps every proper subset containing a new owner to a proper old subset of rank and cardinality each one larger, proving strict Hall preservation at deficiency one if new packets remain rank two. Rank-zero/one simplification and certified affine restriction cannot increase polar rank; a forced rank-one equality cannot increase maximum deficiency by quotient-rank comparison with the forcing owner included. Arbitrary extra nonlinear feedback is not covered by this monotonicity statement.
\end{proof}
At most $3m$ candidate directions and Gaussian solves discover admissible pivots. Singleton-side moves and $2$-by-$2$ moves with polar drop two do not increase $d^*+\operatorname{rank}(\Omega)/2$ or owner count and decrease active rank. Under this schedule, with paid rank-zero/one and affine closure, the number of accepted pivots is at most the original observation dimension. Discovery, failed scans, packet construction, storage and actual reverse lifts are polynomial, with same-run cumulative storage at most $(T+1)S$. Larger moves require a fixed original-input size cap. Neither universal admission nor coverage of fixed points is proved.

An infinite admitted family starts with the strict zero-polar common-hub geometry of two disjoint binary leaf circuits (each independent leaves plus their XOR) with planes $(a,b_j)$. Subdivide $t$ owners whose $a+b_j$ are independent into $(t_j,a),(t_j,b_j)$ with fresh private pivots and opposite forbidden first values. Every split preserves strict deficiency one, increases full rank and owner count by one, and the new total polar form is $\sum_j(t_j+a)\wedge(a+b_j)$, of rank $2t$. Resolving these pivots, each with rank drop two, recovers the rank-two terminal, solving both labels and lifting witnesses. Large initial polar rank alone is therefore not an obstruction to this collaborative normalization.

\begin{lemma}[Orthogonal dependency-triangle invariance]\label{lem:rt36-triangle}
In a strict deficiency-one geometry, replacing an owner $(a,b)$ by $(t,a),(t,b)$ with fresh private $t$ preserves the existence of an orthogonal triangle $p,u,p+u$ in $D$ with $B(p,u)=0$, in both directions.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Write the old local block as $(h,k)$ and the new blocks as $(\epsilon,h),(\epsilon,k)$. This identifies $C'$ with $C\times\mathbb F_2$. The new realizable set is the pure $\epsilon=1$ word with old projection zero, together with lifts of $p\in D$: block $00$ allows only $\epsilon=0$, singleton blocks both choices, and block $11$ only $\epsilon=1$. To verify, a full-rank split transversal must see $t$; eliminating it gives exactly one nonzero row in the old plane, hence an old full-rank transversal. Block $00$ with nonzero old projection and $\epsilon=1$ would produce two dependencies; block $11$ with $\epsilon=0$ cannot see $t$. Conversely, split the selected old direction with one row seeing $t$ and the other exterior, or with two $t$-containing rows whose sum is the selected direction; these realize the listed lifts. Pure $\epsilon$ uses two identical $t$ rows with independent representatives from remaining owners by strict Hall.
The local correction to $q$ is $hk+\epsilon(h+k)$. Every additive triangle of old $D$ lifts additively with zero sum of corrections: if one local block vanishes the others agree and use equal $\epsilon$; otherwise the three nonzero blocks are distinct, the $11$ block uses one and the singleton blocks opposite $\epsilon$. Thus polar pairing is preserved. A new triangle with three nonzero projections descends by the same computation. If a projection is zero, its lift is pure $\epsilon$, and the other two differ only in $\epsilon$ at a singleton old block. Their pairing with the pure word is one, not zero. This proves both directions.
\end{proof}
The all-SAT geometry property itself is invariant under this subdivision: opposite pivot signs give an arbitrary old signing; equal pivot signs allow all affected owners to be satisfied and leave a satisfiable proper old owner subset by Hall. Hence the triangle conjecture reduces to subdivision-irreducible strict cores. For the matrix $A_D$ with columns $p\in D$, the necessary equations for an UNSAT sign are $A_D^\top s=t$ where $t(p)=1+q(p)$. They are consistent iff $t$ annihilates $\ker A_D$. Triangle relations in that kernel have $t$-value $1+B(p,u)$. Thus generation of the full relation kernel by three-term relations would prove the triangle conjecture. This stronger generation conjecture and uniform polynomial acquisition remain OPEN; reference enumeration is not an acquisition algorithm.

Local executed tests: 1411 strict geometries, 235639 extendible dependencies, 1362 all-SAT all with orthogonal triangle, 49 with UNSAT class and none with triangle; separate 303 geometries with full triangle relation generation in every case. 200 subdivision pairs verified exact dependence-set map. 500 private-pivot systems, 12988 exact exterior fiber comparisons, 225 polar drops, 385 maximum-deficiency checks. Twelve scaling controls through 195 owners, 194 independent coordinates, polar rank 128 reduced to zero by 64 discovered pivots; six verified SAT source lifts and six UNSAT controls; 17837 assertions with no failures in contraction checker. No asymptotic proof by tests, no full native compiler/cooperative solver/kernel or measured CM. Fano has no shared nonzero observation direction between owners, hence no private-pivot admission; this rule alone cannot close universal progress. See \url{https://github.com/j15marti/pnp/commit/21ec09195213c8ba12515d9819e9882982ea155f}. U-PROGRESS, universal SEM/CLOSE and unconditional COST remain BLOCK.


\section{M\"obius seam normalization and transverse dependency transport (RT37)}\label{sec:rt37}
We work with authenticated strict deficiency-one charts ($m=r+1$, every proper owner subset has row rank at least its cardinality) after paid certified closure. Retain the two labeled observation coordinates of each owner even when conditioning lowers its projected rank. The following extends RT32 and RT36; it is not a universal progress theorem.

\begin{lemma}[Single-defect algebraic seam]\label{lem:rt37-seam}
Partition the owners into nonempty $J,K$ of sizes $k,h$. Put $A=\sum_{i\in J}U_i$, $D=\sum_{i\in K}U_i$, $B=A\cap D$, and $w=\dim B$. Suppose $\dim A=k$. The exact boundary support of $K$ on $B^*$ is either all of $B^*$ or $B^*\setminus\{b_*\}$. The possibly forbidden word is acquired by deterministic polynomial work, and only one actual quotient decision of size $h$ is needed to determine its status. Every nonexceptional boundary has a constructive witness.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The quotient $D/B$ has rank $h-1$. For proper $S\subsetneq K$, original strict Hall on $J\cup S$ gives projected rank at least $|S|$. RT32 applies even to projected owners of rank less than two: the three nonzero two-bit coefficient labels are retained, and the two satisfied coefficient directions span the projected row space. Lifting by a sign difference outside the source gauge space $G$ raises total rank from $h-1$ to $h$, preserving proper Hall; a full lifted transversal projects to a unique dependence and gives opposite consistency bits for the two signs. Acquire the $h+1$ independent necessary sign equations by RT32. Thus all signs outside the acquired candidate coset have actual witnesses; the candidate is not presumed UNSAT.
Fix a linear extension of a boundary word $b$ into $D$, zero on a complementary basis. Its observation sign shift $H(b)$ is injective modulo $G$: if $H(b)$ belongs to $G$, a private valuation cancels the entire shift on $D$, forcing $b=0$. The preimage of the candidate coset under $s_K+H(b)$ is consequently empty or one word, found by Gaussian elimination. For an unreachable candidate the boundary is full. Otherwise decide the single actual quotient instance at $b_*$. If SAT its witness is transported by the gauge; if UNSAT exactly that boundary word is excluded. The stored transversals lift all other words. Rank-zero singleton quotients are directly decidable; rank-one active owners give forced bits and strict quotienting, while inactive owners can be removed using proper Hall. There is no free reference decision or boundary enumeration.
\end{proof}
For $w=1$ both regions are tight since their ranks sum to $m$. The symmetric argument gives each side a full or singleton binary seam; opposite singleton values obstruct gluing. This is the precise parity-twist connection to the M\"obius-fiber heuristic, not a universal orientation representation.

\begin{lemma}[Strict reassembly and charged recursion]\label{lem:rt37-reassemble}
An excluded word on a rank-$w$ seam can be replaced by $w-1$ rank-two owners with $w-2$ private bits for $w\ge2$, preserving strict deficiency one. The new owner count is $k+w-1$. A rank-one seam instead gives a forced bit and a strict quotient of $J$. If the seam is full, $J$ has a Rado witness which extends to the original chart.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Write the puncture as an OR of $w$ affine mismatch literals. Existentially replace the first two literals by $\operatorname{NAE}(\ell_1,\ell_2,z)$ and the remaining OR with leading literal $\neg z$; when both first literals are zero, $z=1$ is necessary, otherwise $z=0$ suffices. Iterate to the final binary OR. The private projected row spans at the chain owners are the incident private path edges. Every proper subset of the chain has at least its cardinality in independent private coordinates; the whole chain has one fewer. For a proper $S\subsetneq J$, original strict Hall on $S\cup K$ gives $\operatorname{rank}(U_S+B)\ge |S|+1$. This verifies strict Hall when the whole gadget is included; with a proper gadget subset use its private rank and Hall on $J$. Full rank is $k+w-2$. For $w=1$, the same inequality proves strict Hall after quotient by the forced bit. All replacements preserve actual assignments existentially and retain explicit lifts.
\end{proof}
For $w\le h$ a puncture replacement strictly shrinks owner count. If every recursive seam satisfies $w\le \min(k,h)/2$, the two possible recursive jobs have counts $h$ and at most $k+w-1$ ($k$ for $w=1$), and their squared counts sum to less than $(k+h)^2$. This is an actual integer square-credit bound, conditional on uniformly paid discovery, eligible base cases, and polynomial original-input representation size. Fixed bounded $J$ permits a constant-size compressed-side test, and fixed bounded $K$ with shrinking replacement permits iterative contraction. No claim that all residuals satisfy these hypotheses. Charge all discovery, failed probes, closure, certificates, source verification and reverse lifts; polynomial peak space and cumulative storage at most $(T+1)S$ on the same execution follow under the polynomial schedule.

\begin{lemma}[Nonlocal polar drop at a two-bit seam]\label{lem:rt37-polar}
If $w=2$, the exceptional boundary really is forbidden, and the private polar block $P$ of $K$ is nonsingular, then the one-owner replacement satisfies
\[
\rho_{\rm new}\le \rho_{\rm old}-(h-3),\qquad \rho=\operatorname{rank}\Omega.
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Use an exterior row basis extending $B$, then private coordinates of $K$. The old alternating form has blocks $[\Omega_J+S,X;X^\top,P]$, with $S,X$ supported on the two-dimensional seam on the exterior side. Eliminating the invertible block gives rank $h-1+\operatorname{rank}(\Omega_J+S+XP^{-1}X^\top)$. This exterior form differs from the replacement's $\Omega_J$ plus the rank-two seam form on at most a two-dimensional space, so their ranks differ by at most two.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Constructive transverse two-plane]\label{lem:rt37-section}
In any strict deficiency-one geometry, even with projected degenerate owners, let $C$ be the dependence space and $F:C\to\mathbb F_2^2$ be any surjective linear map. There is a two-dimensional symplectic plane of actual full-rank dependence words on which $F$ is bijective. It can be acquired by deterministic polynomial work.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Represent $F$ by two tag coordinates on the original labeled directions. Use RT32 homogeneous lifting by the first tag to find a full independent lifted transversal; delete one supporting owner from its unique projected dependence. This yields an independent quotient basis $T$ from all but one owner $o$. The residual tag of any direction is its tag minus the tag of its expression in $T$. The omitted owner's residual map is nonzero. If its rank is two, finish. Otherwise its image is $L=\{0,l\}$. A selected owner's chosen direction has zero residual and its other two labels have equal residual. Some selected owner has a residual outside $L$, since the total augmented rank is $r+2$; mark all such owners.
Construct the directed exchange graph in the initial basis, with an arc from owner $i$ to selected slot $j$ if a direction of $i$ has nonzero coefficient at $j$. Every owner is reachable from $o$: a proper closed reachable set containing $o$ would have rank at most its size minus one, contradicting strict Hall. Choose a shortest path to the marked set. At every step exchange a direction of the current omitted owner into the next slot, removing its owner. The slot coefficient and the residual-line coefficient are nonzero linear functionals on the two-bit label space, so some nonzero direction hits both one. The swap changes all residual tags by multiples of $l$; the newly omitted owner's old selected direction now has residual $l$. Until the marked endpoint its residual rank stays one; at the endpoint a residual outside $L$ remains, so its rank is two. In the original shortest path there are no forward shortcuts to later slots. Replacing a slot by a vector with zero coefficients in all later path slots preserves those coordinates of every vector. Induction therefore preserves every needed next arc. There are at most $h-1$ swaps for $h$ owners. With the resulting basis fixed, each of the three nonzero omitted-owner directions gives a full-rank transversal. Their dependencies form a linear two-plane, nondegenerate because all fixed basis-owner blocks lie on lines and the omitted block is the standard two-bit pairing. The residual map is bijective by construction. All data are actual row coefficients, obtained by one lifted intersection and polynomial Gaussian and graph operations.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Triangle transport through a two-bit seam]\label{lem:rt37-triangle}
For the strict seam of Lemma~\ref{lem:rt37-seam} with $w=2$, every orthogonal dependency triangle of the contracted geometry (one seam packet) lifts to an orthogonal dependency triangle of the original geometry. Also any such triangle of the conditioned $K$ geometry lifts to the original.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
On the quotient dependence space of $K$, summing original rows with their dependence coefficients lands in $B$ and surjects onto $B$ (each row of $B$ lies in the original row span and has zero private image). Use Lemma~\ref{lem:rt37-section} to get a symplectic section $\sigma$. Replace every selected nonzero seam direction in a contracted transversal by a $K$ transversal with boundary sum that direction. Independent private rows together with the contracted rank prove full rank in the original. Its dependence lifts linearly, with seam block $c$ replaced by $\sigma(c)$, including zero if the seam owner did not participate in the dependence. All pairings are preserved. For a triangle in the conditioned $K$, fix independent representatives in the tight region $J$, lift dependencies by their unique compensating $J$ coefficients; the extra blocks all lie on lines so their polar contributions are zero. This gives the second claim.
\end{proof}
If the quotient geometry $K$ admits an UNSAT sign class, arbitrary seam punctures can be attained by shifting its signing, and any other signing gives either a puncture or full support. Consequently the original geometry admits an UNSAT signing iff the contracted seam geometry does. If $K$ has no UNSAT signing then the original geometry is all-SAT. Together with Lemma~\ref{lem:rt37-triangle} this is an inductive reduction of the triangle conjecture through admitted two-bit tight seams, not a proof of general triangle generation or a converse triangle-transport statement.

A related defect-repair observation uses a hypothetical actual satisfying assignment $x^*$. A basis with one omitted owner gives a near-model, and if not SAT, the omitted owner alone is violated. Select one direction of that owner satisfied by $x^*$; its discrepancy from the near-model is one. Some basis row in its support therefore has a discrepant selected equation. Exchange it out, recompute the basis model, and the number of selected equations disagreeing with $x^*$ falls by one. Hence a SAT chart has a defect-moving repair path of length at most $r$ from any basis near-model. This path uses the unknown witness for its selection; bounded path length is not a polynomial discovery bound.

\paragraph{Unbounded initial polar rank without shared directions.}
Use a strict zero-global-polar base of two common-hub leaf circuits, as in RT35--36. Replace every owner by a seven-owner positive Fano chart on six private bits, with two exterior tag masks $5,11$ (little-endian two-bit owner blocks) acting on the original seam rows. The fixed Fano planes are $(1,2),(4,8),(16,32),(5,17),(9,33),(6,34),(10,18)$. Their private rank is six, polar rank six, and proper subsets satisfy strict Hall; all nonzero directions are distinct. The two tags are independent modulo gauge even after deleting one owner, as verified by the seven rank-eight matrices. Shift the signs to designate the original forbidden seam word. The quotient has its unique UNSAT class at the positive Fano signing, so the seam is exactly the original puncture; a single actual owner-sign change in a module makes its candidate unreachable. Private blocks of different modules are disjoint, so the expanded geometry has no shared nonzero direction. Hall is preserved because a proper module subset contributes its count in private rank, and a whole module contributes six private ranks plus its old plane. Lemma~\ref{lem:rt37-polar} gives a strict drop at every module contraction, followed by the RT36 rank-two terminal. For this one-level family, blind enumeration of seven-owner sets with tight complement and rank-two projected owners is a polynomial discovery rule: a partly removed module losing at least two owners contributes positive private excess (Fano minimum ranks for sizes 1 through 6 are 2,4,5,5,6,6); a partly removed module losing one owner still contributes both exterior seam rows, and any mixed seven-owner cut of that type has positive exterior excess. Sets of seven already contracted common-hub singleton owners have projected rank at most one per owner, unless the base terminal has already been reached. Thus admitted sets are genuine modules. Large experiments use supplied module indices, not exhaustive large cut discovery.

\paragraph{Remaining irreducible obstruction.}
There are arbitrarily large strict deficiency-one geometries with no nontrivial tight subset. For $m=r+1$ independently sampled pairs of binary rows, a fixed $s$-owner subset with $1\le s\le r-1$ has rank at most $s$ with probability at most $C2^{-s(r-s)}$ by subspace counting. Union bound over all such subsets tends to zero: for $s\le r/2$ use $m^s2^{-sr/2}$; for $s>r/2$ put $t=r-s$ and use $m^{t+1}2^{-rt/2}$. Pairwise shared-direction collisions can also be avoided. These raw geometries can be signed SAT with a known model. Only trivial one-owner complement tight cuts remain. This is a scoped representation barrier, not unrestricted hardness. Even Fano itself has no nontrivial tight subset. Universal seam admission, triangle-relation generation and arbitrary-deficiency coverage remain unproved.

Executed local raw-chart tests: 160 strict small charts, 3880 exact fibers, 2962 local and 160 full source lifts, 176 degenerate projected owners; 2032 gadget Hall subsets, 4064 gadget fibers, 141 local polar checks. Ten scaling controls through 245 owners/rank244, polar rank210 to zero, 35 contractions in largest control, five reconstructed SAT source witnesses. Small blind discovery 120 cuts, one admitted. Separate 1681 transverse plane tests, 874 swaps (max3); 560 witness-guided repair paths (max5); 105 triangle insertions with 315 verified dependencies. Six one-bit seam both-label controls, one reachable SAT exceptional class, 21 single-sign openings, 260 additional exact fibers. Total 68262 assertions without failures. No complete cooperative/native/kernel/TeX replay, large blind discovery execution, asymptotic random generation, or measured cumulative memory. Reference exceptions decided by exact enumeration only at fixed small rank. See \url{https://github.com/j15marti/pnp/commit/22425eb0dda70851a4352cdd1f60e67868b4aabc}. U-PROGRESS, universal SEM/CLOSE and unconditional COST remain BLOCK. No public proof claim.


\section{Paired-dependency identity testing and conditional orientation gluing (RT38)}\label{sec:rt38}
Continue RT35--37 on actual strict deficiency-one charts with paid guard substitution and closure. For an omitted rank-two owner $o$ with rows $a,b$, let $C_0=\{p\in C:p_o=0\}$ and fix an independent retained transversal $T_0$. For any independent retained transversal $T$, its three fundamental dependencies $p_a(T),p_b(T),p_{a+b}(T)$ form a symplectic plane. Define
\[
W_o=\operatorname{span}_{T}\{(p_a(T)+p_a(T_0),p_b(T)+p_b(T_0))\}\subseteq C_0^2.
\]
\begin{lemma}[Constructive independent-transversal walk]\label{lem:rt38-walk}
Any two supplied independent retained transversals can be connected by at most $r(r+1)/2$ single-owner legal changes, with polynomial discovery.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Write the target rows in the current basis. The restriction $M$ to the $k$ unmatched slots is invertible. A diagonal one permits direct target installation. Otherwise take a shortest directed cycle of nonzero entries. At a cycle slot $i$, replace the current direction by current plus target; this is independent since $M_{ii}=0$. In the new basis the unmatched target matrix is $M+M_{:,i}M_{i,:}$. Either a diagonal one appears or the shortest cycle shortens: the original shortest cycle has no chord forming a shorter cycle, so the introduced predecessor-successor edge and the other surviving cycle edges are nonzero. A two-cycle produces a diagonal one. At most $k-1$ third-direction moves followed by one target installation decrease $k$. Sum over $k$. Coordinates and cycle search are polynomial. This does not acquire a satisfying target basis.
\end{proof}
An active single-owner switch gives $v\in D\cap C_0$ from the sum of old and new selected directions at its slot and the representation of that sum in the other basis rows. For each omitted $c$, $p_c(T')=p_c(T)+\lambda_cv$, where $\lambda_c$ is its old slot coefficient. If active, two of three $\lambda_c$ are one and $B(p_c,v)=1$ for each affected $c$. Conversely a supplied $p\in D\cap C_0$ admits an active-switch construction. For support $S$ let $V$ be its circuit span, dimension $|S|-1$. In the quotient by $V$, free owners outside $S,o$ have independent representatives completable by some $o$ direction. Some supporting owner $j$ has an alternate direction that also completes them: otherwise tight free-owner subsets whose spans contain the respective projected $U_j$ have tight union by submodularity, contradicting proper-subset Hall for $S$ plus that union. Acquire the two completions by independent-representative tests. Their two homogeneous block-linear determinants each exclude at most one nonzero choice per free group while remaining nonzero; greedy fixing preserves both. The selected free rows and circuit rows minus $j$ span a hyperplane, with both alternate $j$ and the chosen $o$ direction outside it. Switch the alternate by adding the circuit direction at $j$. The active vector is exactly $p$. Thus $W_o$ is generated by actual active-edge pairs $(v,0),(0,v),(v,v)$; supplied independent state witnesses give polynomially many edge witnesses by Lemma~\ref{lem:rt38-walk}.

\begin{lemma}[Deterministic paired-span acquisition]\label{lem:rt38-pme}
The exact span $W_o$ and a basis of actual transversal witnesses can be acquired in deterministic polynomial time using the published rank-one symbolic determinant equality theorem.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
In $T_0$ coordinates use retained first rows $e_j$, alternatives $M_j$, selected symbolic rows $A_j=\alpha_je_j+\beta_jM_j$, and $\Delta=\operatorname{diag}(\beta_j)$. Coordinates on $C_0$ are the alternate-row coefficients. Any paired linear functional is represented by columns $t,u$ on these coordinates, with ambient extension zero on the initial units. Put
\[
f=\det A,\qquad
g=\det(A+\Delta ta)+\det(A+\Delta ub).
\]
On invertible binary selections the determinant lemma makes $g=aA^{-1}\Delta t+bA^{-1}\Delta u$ the functional value on the paired difference. If $g$ is formally nonzero, then $f,g$ can be kept nonzero simultaneously while fixing each two-variable group to one of its three nonzero choices: both polynomials are separately homogeneous linear in that group, so each excludes at most one direction. Therefore $g\equiv0$ iff the functional annihilates $W_o$. Each variable occurs in one row, giving rank-at-most-one coefficient matrices. Chatterjee, Ghosh, Gurjar and Raj, \emph{Characterizing and Testing Principal Minor Equivalence of Matrices}, STOC 2025, Theorem 1.3, proves deterministic polynomial equality testing for these two symbolic determinants, including fixed-prefix restrictions. Use independent-representative feasibility for $f$. Test an annihilator basis of the acquired span, and when a functional fails, greedily extract a witnessed independent transversal outside it. At most $2r$ rank increases. Charge all failed identity/feasibility probes, Gaussian work, and actual witnesses. No general support-containment test is inferred.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Conditional contradiction through orientation gluing]\label{lem:rt38-glue}
Suppose the parent is seam-irreducible ($\operatorname{rank} U_S>|S|$ for nonempty $|S|\le r-1$). If all three one-direction quotient children have triangle-relation generation and $W_o=C_0^2$, the parent has triangle-relation generation.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Impose the selected opposite-RHS equation at $o$, remove $o$ and quotient observations by its direction $c\in\{a,b,a+b\}$. Proper child subsets satisfy Hall by irreducibility and rank drops by at most one. The child dependency space embeds bijectively into $C_c=\{p:p_o\in\{0,c\}\}$; the child dependency set $D_c$ lifts to the actual parent dependencies realized with $c$, preserving polar pairing. Their union is $D$. A function respecting all additive dependency triangles restricts to a linear functional $f_c$ on each $C_c$ by hypothesis. Subtract the initial fundamental triangle identity from each triangle at $T$. The functional $((f_a+f_{a+b})|C_0,(f_b+f_{a+b})|C_0)$ annihilates $W_o$. Full span forces agreement on $C_0$; the initial plane triangle forces consistent extension over the remaining two coordinates. Hence the function extends linearly to $C$. Finite-dimensional duality gives triangle-relation generation.
\end{proof}
For the weaker all-SAT triangle conjecture, a smallest seam-irreducible all-SAT counterexample without orthogonal triangles has smaller strict children without orthogonal triangles. If the smaller conjecture holds, each child admits an UNSAT sign, so its $1+q_{\rm child}$ extends linearly. The parent's $1+q$ differs on $C_c$ only by the linear indicator of nonzero $o$ block. The gluing proof gives an UNSAT parent signing if some $W_o$ is full, a contradiction. Thus every omitted rank-two owner must have deficient $W_o$ in such a counterexample. This is conditional induction, not universal full-span admission. Two children suffice for the generation argument when $\operatorname{span}(D_a\cap D_b)=C_0$: agree there, use fundamental triangles for the third label, and complete any zero-label dependency with at least one of $a,b$ outside its retained hyperplane. Even three smaller children of size $m-1$ give no polynomial aggregate bound by themselves.

\begin{lemma}[Structural alternative for deficient orientation span]\label{lem:rt38-cut}
For each eligible omitted rank-two owner, deterministic polynomial work obtains full paired span, or proves $\rho=\operatorname{rank}\Omega\le4$, or produces an almost-tight proper owner subset, or an actual algebraic seam of width at most six.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
With a nonzero annihilator $(t,u)$, the identity from Lemma~\ref{lem:rt38-pme} is precisely principal-minor equivalence of $M_1=M+ta$ and $M_2=M+ub$. Equality is impossible since $a,b$ are independent. Transpose equality gives $\operatorname{rank}(M+M^\top)\le2$, and $\Omega=M+M^\top+a^\top b+b^\top a$ has rank at most four. If $M_1$ is reducible, an SCC sink proper set $S$ has $M_1[S,T]=0$. Thus $\operatorname{rank}M[S,T]\le1$ and $\operatorname{rank} U_S\le |S|+1$. Otherwise use the cited principal-minor equivalence cut-free theorem, Lemma 2.8, and cut discovery Lemma 4.3: over $\mathbb F_2$ diagonal similarity is trivial, so irreducible matrices not related by equality or transpose have a nontrivial cut with both off-diagonal ranks at most one in $M_1$. Removing its rank-one update gives both off-diagonal ranks at most two in $M$. The original owner partition $S$ versus $T\cup\{o\}$ then has intersection dimension at most $2+2+2=6$. These are cuts of the actual chart. Almost-tight $S$ may be trivial, and a six-bit seam need not be tight; conditioning can raise deficiency. Neither case establishes universal progress.
\end{proof}
Executed local audits: 253 basis walks through rank64, 2338 switches; 290 constructive active-switch realizations; 74 strict geometries exact active-switch/dependency equality; 82 two-child gluing controls. 125 principal-minor/paired charts, 618 annihilator checks, 500 greedy witnesses with finite reference oracle; 18 transpose, 98 reducible (19 high-polar), two cut cases. 56 full paired-span acquisitions, 406 independent witnessed states. All seven Fano views full rank12. Among 228 tested seam-irreducible geometries, all have at least one full-span owner (190 all owners), not a theorem. Rank-two repeated-plane base is an exception with rank3 rather than4 at every owner. Additional 453 irreducible geometries and 2319 owner views disprove naive universal pair-overlap and agreement conditions. Total 119739 assertions without failure. Imported general PME backend not executed; tests use exponential small reference enumeration. No complete native/cooperative/kernel/TeX replay or measured CM. Report: \url{https://github.com/j15marti/pnp/commit/2113f15b686a8c6b90855090a0defab154ee1ad3}. U-PROGRESS, general triangle generation/acquisition, arbitrary deficiency, universal SEM/CLOSE and unconditional COST remain BLOCK. No public proof claim.


\section{Exact two-child orientation classification and global overlap gluing (RT39)}\label{sec:rt39}
Work with the actual authenticated strict deficiency-one chart, $m=r+1$, full observation rank $r$, and rank at least cardinality on every proper owner subset. Retain two labeled coefficient coordinates even for degenerate projected rows. All actual guards remain in the chart; available certified closure is charged before and after deductions and at stagnation. This section distinguishes complete reference-free decision from a polynomial aggregate bound.

\begin{lemma}[Two-child exact geometry classification]\label{lem:rt39-two}
A strict deficiency-one geometry can be classified deterministically as all-SAT or assigned an actual reference UNSAT sign and its entire gauge class, by recursion with at most two strictly smaller geometry jobs and polynomial local work. Rank-one owners require at most one child. This does not assert polynomial total recursion.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
At a rank-two owner $o$, choose two independent labeled directions $a,b$. The avoidance relation is exactly the disjunction of their two satisfied equations $a(x)=1+c_a(s_o)$ and $b(x)=1+c_b(s_o)$. Hence the parent is SAT iff either of the corresponding quotients (impose the equation and remove the owner) is SAT. The remaining owners span the old rank $r$ by proper-subset Hall, so after either quotient the $r$ owners span $r-1$. Every subset of these owners loses at most one rank and had rank at least cardinality, so maximum deficiency is exactly one. Acquire a smallest deficient subregistry by deleting an owner whenever the remaining groups still fail to admit independent representatives, using deterministic linear/partition matroid intersection. The resulting core is strict; all outside owners can be satisfied for every core assignment using DS15 quotient representatives. Preserve their actual source maps and signs for reconstruction. Each child core has fewer owners. In particular, this argument permits tight subsets and projected rank degeneracy, not just seam-irreducible parents.
For fixed branch direction $c$, the actual child sign word is an affine function $R_c(s)$ of the parent signs, found by substituting the imposed equation and projecting. By induction, either the child geometry admits only SAT signs, or it has a certified UNSAT sign $t_c$. RT32 applies with the two labeled coordinates even when projected rows coincide or vanish, as established in RT37. Its UNSAT set is exactly $t_c+\operatorname{im}L_c$. An all-SAT child makes the parent all-SAT. Otherwise the parent UNSAT set is exactly
\[
 \{s:R_a(s)\in t_a+\operatorname{im}L_a\}\ \cap\
 \{s:R_b(s)\in t_b+\operatorname{im}L_b\}.
\]
Each membership test is represented by linear equations for a basis of $\ker L_c^\top$. Pull back and solve their affine intersection. If empty, the geometry is all-SAT; otherwise any solution is a genuine UNSAT reference for the parent, and by RT32 the entire intersection is its gauge class. This is exact orientation gluing and does not require triangle generation or full paired span.
For a rank-one owner let $z$ be its unique nonzero zero-row label. If $c_z(s_o)=1$, its forbidden word cannot be attained; the remaining proper subset is SAT by Hall. Otherwise the owner is equivalent to one satisfied nonzero-row equation, so there is a single child; add $c_z(s_o)=0$ to the pulled-back UNSAT equations. A rank-zero owner can occur in a strict chart only at the base $m=1,r=0$, where precisely sign $00$ is UNSAT. This proves the induction. To recover a witness at a SAT signing, select a tested child with SAT sign, reconstruct its model, fill outside core observations by DS15 independent representatives modulo its span, and solve the original affine equations including the imposed row. For an inactive rank-one owner use a Rado witness on the other owners. Verify the actual source.
\end{proof}
The naive recurrence is bounded by $2^{O(m)}\operatorname{poly}(N)$ time, including failed work, guards, discovery, extraction, sign maps, closure, verification, and lifts. Depth-first classification uses polynomial peak space, with cumulative storage at most $(T+1)S$; retaining a full memo table or proof tree need not. Recomputing child classifications during reconstruction adds at most a polynomial factor to this exponential allowance. Exact labeled coordinate-normalized keys are a sound cache, not a free semantic canonicalization. A conditional polynomial schedule exists when each binary stage either has a uniformly bounded child and a strictly rank-decreasing other child, or a paid verified isomorphism between the two children (including actual label and affine sign transport) permits just one recursive classification. The two pulled-back orientations still must be reconciled. This is an exact form of the proposed M\"obius reorientation, but its universal availability and acquisition are unproved. Arbitrary deficiency remains outside the theorem.

\begin{lemma}[Polynomial fixed-selector overlap acquisition]\label{lem:rt39-overlap}
For a strict deficiency-one chart and any prescribed set $I$ of owner-direction labels, the span of the actual full-rank transversal dependence words $D_I$ respecting $I$ is deterministically computable in polynomial time, with actual transversal witnesses.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For a linear functional $h$ on the coefficient dependency space append the bit $h(c)$ to each labeled direction $c$. A full independent lifted transversal respecting the fixed labels exists iff an actual $p\in D_I$ has $h(p)=1$: its projected rank is exactly $m-1=r$, with unique dependence whose appended bit is nonzero. The converse follows by the same rank argument. Contract fixed lifted rows and use deterministic linear/partition matroid intersection; reject dependent fixed rows. Test an annihilator basis of the current span; if a probe hits, add the actual dependency and its selector word. At most $r+2$ independent additions suffice, and failure of every annihilator-basis probe certifies exact span. All queries, failed tests and source row representations are polynomial in the explicit chart size. This is linear-span acquisition, not a quadratic identity oracle.
\end{proof}
For a seam-irreducible rank-two parent put $H_{ic}=\{p\in C:p_i\in\{0,c\}\}$, one hyperplane per owner $i$ and nonzero label $c$. The one-owner quotient is strict and RT32 gives $\operatorname{span}D_{ic}=H_{ic}$. Assign a local linear functional to each $H_{ic}$ and impose agreement on the exact acquired $\operatorname{span}D_{ic,jd}$ for distinct owners, optionally also actual fundamental-plane triangle equations. The resulting system has $O(mr)$ unknowns and $O(m^2r)$ witnessed overlap equations plus polynomial triangle equations. Global linear functionals on $C$ inject into its solution space. If the solution dimension is $r+2$, every compatible family glues to a global functional. If all smaller one-owner quotients have triangle-relation generation, any triangle-additive function on the parent's $D$ is locally linear, satisfies these overlap equations, and hence extends linearly. This is a conditional induction, not a complete identity test.

\begin{lemma}[Strong double-Hall gluing]\label{lem:rt39-doublehall}
Suppose the strict rank-two parent is seam-irreducible, $r\ge4$, and for all owner subsets $S$ with $2\le |S|\le r-2$ one has $\operatorname{rank}U_S\ge |S|+2$. Then agreement on the acquired cross-owner overlap spans suffices to glue every compatible family of local linear functionals globally.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Any two owner planes have disjoint nonzero directions. Fix a nonzero direction $c$ at owner $i$ and $d$ at another owner $j$. They are independent. Remove both owners and quotient by their span. The remaining $r-1$ owners had full rank $r$ by seam irreducibility, so the new rank is $r-2$. Each proper subset of at least two owners loses at most two rank from excess at least two. A singleton loses at most one, since its plane cannot contain $c$ or $d$ by disjointness, and thus cannot equal their span. The double quotient is strict deficiency one. Its dependency space embeds bijectively as $H_{ic}\cap H_{jd}$ by unique compensating coefficients along the fixed rows. Full-rank child selections lift by the fixed rows, and conversely, so RT32 gives
\[
\operatorname{span}D_{ic,jd}=H_{ic}\cap H_{jd},\qquad
\dim(H_{ic}\cap H_{jd})=r .
\]
Choose four independent hyperplane normals in $C^*$ at distinct owners. Each owner's two-dimensional normal space has rank two since the other owners span $r$; the total normal span has dimension $r+2$. By Rado, if no four independent owner representatives exist, some nonempty owner subset $S$ has normal rank plus $m-|S|$ at most three (the empty set cannot qualify since $m\ge5$). Its rank is at least two, so it omits at most one owner; including that owner's two normals cannot yield total rank $r+2\ge6$. Contradiction. Find four anchors by fixed-size search. Two anchor hyperplanes glue their functionals by full intersection agreement; the third and fourth agree with this global functional on two intersections spanning each hyperplane, by independence of normals. Any other chart has at least three independent anchors with distinct owners from it. Choose two of those whose normal span does not contain its normal. Their intersections with the chart span it, proving agreement with the global functional everywhere. Thus cross-owner agreement is sufficient, regardless of same-owner overlap ranks.
\end{proof}
For independent fixed $c,d$ in any seam-irreducible parent, the double quotient fails strictness iff a proper nonempty set $S$ of remaining owners has rank $|S|+1$ and contains $\operatorname{span}(c,d)$. Before quotient it has rank at least $|S|+1$, so losing two ranks is the only way to create deficiency. The converse follows by subtracting two. Its smallest maximal-deficiency core then contains every dependence of every full-rank transversal (there is already exactly one dependence in that core), and all core full-rank selections extend by DS15. Thus the overlap span equals the embedded core dependency space. If two fixed rows coincide, any full-rank selection with them fixed has the unique two-owner dependence, and ordinary independent completion tests feasibility. Overlap failure is therefore an actual near-tight structural obstruction, not merely an orientation heuristic.
The strong double-Hall condition is polynomial to certify or falsify: enumerate required included pairs $I$ and excluded triples $E$. Over the remaining free owners, quotient by $U_I$ and compute their maximum Hall deficiency $d^*_{\rm free}$ by Rado's min--max formula and matroid intersection. Then the minimum of $\operatorname{rank}U_S-|S|$ for $I\subseteq S\subseteq [m]\setminus E$ is $\operatorname{rank}U_I-|I|-d^*_{\rm free}$. Acquire a maximizing subset by the DS15 extraction if needed. All sizes $2$ through $r-2$ are covered by some such included pair and excluded triple. Thus a smallest triangle-generation counterexample within the strict rank-two class, if seam-irreducible and rank at least four, must have a nontrivial almost-tight subset of those sizes: otherwise all one-owner quotients remain nondegenerate strict and smaller, and the gluing theorem gives the induction contradiction. This narrows the structural problem without resolving near-tight cases, triangle generation for degenerate charts, or aggregate recursion.

\paragraph{Polynomial signed-orientation certificates.}
Collect witnessed dependency bases from all single and double selector charts by Lemma~\ref{lem:rt39-overlap}. Append $t(p)=1+q(p)$ as one extra bit. If the augmented rank exceeds the ordinary dependency rank, Gaussian elimination gives at most $r+3$ actual dependencies summing to zero with $t$-sum one. This is an all-SAT certificate: no signing can make all those dependencies inconsistent. For any sign one certificate dependency has $Q_s=0$, yielding a verified SAT witness by its retained full-rank transversal. If sampled equations are consistent, they specify a candidate gauge coset, not a certified UNSAT reference. No universal sample-completeness theorem follows.
