Three strong geometries $r=12,14,16$, 211397 reference subset checks and 36 sampled actual overlap acquisitions, all rank $r$. Classifier: 107 strict geometries including degeneracies, 57 all-SAT and 50 with UNSAT classes, 25650 reference signing tests including all 16384 Fano signs, 474 verified top-level SAT witnesses, 814 recursive and 411 inactive-owner lifts, 680 expanded jobs, 145 binary and 428 unary, 57 orientation conflicts, 105 all-SAT child shortcuts, 2203 exact cache hits, 4533 core tests. Total 58324 assertions, no failures. Finite reference enumeration is not a production bound; strong-condition admission theorem not implemented in these finite tests. No whole cooperative/native/kernel/TeX execution or measured CM. See \url{https://github.com/j15marti/pnp/commit/52cd08ddb63d947656e805254a659ac8158f761a}. Universal polynomial classification, arbitrary deficiency, U-PROGRESS, SEM/CLOSE and unconditional COST remain BLOCK. No public proof.


\section{Subpower light-child credit (T4-AS1)}\label{sec:t4-as1}
\begin{lemma}[Conditional asymmetric branch recurrence]\label{lem:t4-as1}
Fix constants $a,q,K\ge1$, $\beta\ge0$, and $0\le\alpha<1$. Every authenticated live obligation has a computable integer deficiency $0\le d\le (N+2)^a$ in original encoded length $N$, with $d=0$ terminal. Suppose a uniform deterministic procedure, including all failed lane work, acquisition, checks, representation changes and reconstruction, costs at most $(N+2)^q$ bit operations per expanded occurrence and either decides it correctly or produces an exact exhaustive family of strictly smaller-deficiency children. For each expansion of deficiency $d>0$, at most one heavy child has $d_h\le d-1$ and at most $K(d+1)^\beta$ other children have $d_\ell+1\le K(d+1)^\alpha$. At small deficiencies it suffices to have a fixed bound on branching and strict decreases or a uniformly paid terminal. All child occurrences, including already contradicted ones, are charged. For any fixed integer $c>(1+\beta)/(1-\alpha)$, the total occurrence count is $O((d+1)^c)$. If initialization and terminal cost are polynomial in the original $N$ and the charged procedure preserves exact semantics, total deterministic bit time is polynomial. No universal existence or acquisition hypothesis is supplied by the lemma.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For fixed small $d$ the occurrence count is uniformly bounded by a constant, by strict decreases and bounded branching. For larger $d$, inductively bound each child by $C(d_i+1)^c$, for constant $C$. The total count satisfies
\[
W(d)\le 1+C d^c+C K^{c+1}(d+1)^{\beta+\alpha c}.
\]
Since $c\ge1$,
\[
(d+1)^c-d^c\ge(d+1)^{c-1},
\qquad \beta+\alpha c<c-1 .
\]
For all sufficiently large $d$, the light-child contribution uses at most half this difference and the remaining credit pays one occurrence. Choose $C$ to cover the finitely many smaller deficiencies. Thus $W(d)\le C(d+1)^c$. Multiplying by the charged per-occurrence original-$N$ cost gives $O((N+2)^{ac+q})$, in addition to separately polynomial initialization and terminals. With all cell writes and retained objects charged in the same bit model, polynomial total time bounds peak written storage and cumulative live storage; any sharing or parallel scheduling must also charge its aggregate work and all live child obligations. Correctness follows by exact composition, not by selecting the favorable child. This result permits a long heavy spine with a small unresolved child at each step. Mere strict local decrease is inadequate: two children of deficiency $d-1$ at every node give $2^d$ leaves.
\end{proof}
Finite audit, 27 November 2026: strict signed E4/B4 common native EB-JOINT-24 and EB-RANDOM-3CNF-40 were authenticated by full SHA-256 and exact original lengths $5{,}363{,}624$ and $5{,}027{,}816$ bits. Five separately executed guarded methods (occupancy, affine hull, bijunctive relaxation, bounded exact bucket, guarded proof tree) produced $4/2$ immediate occupancy-refuted guards and $5/5$ proof-tree-refuted guards respectively. The other three relaxation methods obtained no additional guard contradictions. Exact native parity and private-variable projection, restricted original-B-support refutations and 31-term guard coverage were independently checked. Original support unions were 312 and 300 B vertices. Both original CNFs also independently refuted. Under the selected policy, RANDOM had seven genuine two-survivor forks, all failing the unit-constant square-root and three-quarter-power thresholds, including $(39)\to(38,38)$. Independently replaying two partial peer guard exclusions reduced downstream row events from 370048 to 314658 and nodes from 61 to 50, but this is not an aggregate speedup claim. All of these are finite scoped results; they do not show that the lemma's macro-acquisition hypothesis holds on arbitrary inputs. See the pinned report \url{https://github.com/j15marti/pnp/commit/3b1617c44ae2defdebd1903fd68d912f8a545a02}. The first unresolved implication remains Obligation~\ref{obl:progress}, including universally acquirable progress, correctness of all invoked transformations, and the unconditional original-$N$ cost bound. No public resolution.


\section{T1: Irredundant affine guard covers have bounded relative codimension}
\label{sec:t1-five-guard-rank}
\begin{lemma}[Affine obstruction-cover rank firewall]\label{lem:t1-cover-rank}
Let $A$ be a nonempty affine space of dimension $d$ over $\mathbb F_2$, and let $G_1,\ldots,G_k$ be affine subspaces of $A$. If they cover $A$ irredundantly, then $\operatorname{codim}_A(G_i)\le k-1$ for every $i$. If they do not cover $A$, the complement of their union contains a nonempty affine flat of codimension at most $k$ in $A$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
In an irredundant cover choose $x_i\in G_i\setminus\bigcup_{j\ne i}G_j$. For each $j\ne i$, choose one affine defining equation of $G_j$ violated at $x_i$ and reverse its right-hand side. The intersection of these $k-1$ reversed equations in $A$ is nonempty, contains $x_i$, and avoids every $G_j$, $j\ne i$. By coverage it is contained in $G_i$ and has codimension at most $k-1$. For noncoverage take a point outside the union and apply the same construction to each nonempty guard; empty guards impose no restriction. The resulting flat avoids the union.
\end{proof}
For fixed $k$, exact inclusion--exclusion of at most $2^k-1$ affine intersection counts, Gaussian elimination, and coordinate self-reduction acquire an uncovered or exclusive point with polynomial bit work in the explicitly given affine chart size. Greedy deletion of redundant guards obtains an irredundant subcover. The codimension bound is tight for the usual prefix partition by $k-1$ bits. In particular a five-guard cover has an irredundant subcover with individual relative codimensions at most four. This is a post-acquisition result only; even rank-one normals have exponentially many candidates, and an uncovered relaxation point need not satisfy the source. No universal guard acquisition or progress follows.

The pinned STRICT-EB4-v1 common instances were regenerated and authenticated in the five-lane experiment. On EB-JOINT-24, five source-only guarded RUP refutations covered the $2^{27}$-point projected carrier; four guards suffice, with a replay-derived original B-support union of 404 vertices out of 788. On EB-RANDOM-3CNF-40 four independently replayed guard refutations covered seven eighths of the $2^{40}$-point carrier. The remaining affine flat had dimension 37. The T4 guard asserting relative port 16 to port 10 equals zero was independently re-proved on the T1 chart using its 41-node tree; the imported opposite unary eliminates the remaining flat. Five checked guards cover the full carrier; three suffice. The original B-support union is 536 of 736 (all E and edge constraints retained). These are scoped replay-dependent support claims, not minimum cores. Occupancy, affine, matching, bounded separator and guarded-DAG lanes were independently evaluated serially; matching contributed no additional cuts, and fixed-seed random guard search did not close the remaining flat. All failed work and replay are recorded, not treated as free. See \url{https://github.com/j15marti/pnp/blob/ab7288cdb8b8f1c3942ba8e2cb5abb83fb267984/research/hcl201/matching/2026-11-27_T1_five_guard_cover_rank/report.md}.
